hot.title: Environmental Concerns in the Fashion Industry: A Twin Transition With the Digital Product Passport
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT The fashion industry exerts a significant impact on ecosystems, prompting consumers to seek sustainable solutions and companies to adapt their production processes to minimize environmental harm. The digital product passport (DPP) may play an important role in facilitating the twin green and digital transitions. Proposed by the European Commission, the DPP aims to enhance the sustainability and traceability of products throughout their life cycle, and the recent literature reflects a growing scholarly interest in this initiative. The present paper presents the findings of an online survey conducted in Italy with a sample of 549 participants, exploring consumer perceptions regarding digital device knowledge, purchasing habits, and environmental and economic considerations. The results show a general lack of familiarity with the DPP but a strong confidence in digital labels as tools for enhancing corporate transparency. While consumer awareness of environmental issues remains somewhat ambiguous, there is growing attention to the use of raw materials. Notably, respondents expressed a willingness to pay a 17% premium for products featuring the DPP, with this tendency emerging as most pronounced among women, individuals aged 31–50 years, and those with high incomes. Additionally, 58% of respondents indicated a willingness to donate money in support of sustainability initiatives, though younger respondents (aged 18–30 years) appeared less inclined towards such altruistic contributions. The findings may inform business strategy and provide valuable insights into how the DPP may support the green and digital transition. However, its effectiveness depends on the integration of environmental protection measures with socioeconomic considerations, aligning with the objecti

hot.title: Measuring Companies’ Environmental and Social Impacts: An analysis of ESG Ratings and SDG Scores
hot.abstract: Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) ratings are central to sustainable investing and research but face criticism for inaccurately reflecting corporate sustainability performance. In response, new metrics have emerged that assess companies’ impacts on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This article compares four ESG ratings with two SDG scores, revealing no correlation between them. It then evaluates the alignment between these sustainability ratings and how investors and regulators assess corporate (un)sustainability. The findings show that SDG scores capture how these stakeholders judge companies’ negative and positive impacts on sustainable development, while ESG ratings do not. This implies that SDG scores have high, and ESG ratings low, construct validity for assessing corporate sustainability performance. These results underscore that concepts like ESG, corporate sustainability, and company impact can be used complementarily but not interchangeably. The practical implication is that sustainable investors should prioritize sustainable development impacts next to avoiding ESG risks.

latest.title: Decision pathways in mobile-app shopping: a Throughput Model study of online consumers
latest.abstract: Purpose Mobile shopping environments increasingly rely on artificial intelligence (AI) to personalise recommendations, curate product information and support purchase decisions. Yet, existing consumer decision-making models maintain a linear, stage-based logic that fails to capture how AI-enabled interfaces compress, extend or reconfigure the pathways consumers actually follow. This study aims to use the Throughput Model (TPM) to conceptualise and empirically validate distinct algorithmic decision pathways through which perception, information search and evaluative judgement interact to shape purchase intentions in mobile-app shopping contexts. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from Gen Z consumers with recent mobile-app shopping experience. The study applies partial least squares structural equation modelling and mediation analysis to test the TPM and estimate one-step, two-step and three-step decision pathways in AI-enabled mobile commerce. Findings Perception, information search and judgement each exert significant effects within the model, with judgement emerging as the central integrative mechanism linking upstream inputs to purchase intention. These results demonstrate that AI-enabled mobile interfaces simultaneously support impulsive, efficiency-driven and deliberative decision architectures. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study provides the first empirical operationalisation of the TPM in mobile-app commerce, reconceptualising purchase decisions as coexisting algorithmic pathways rather than a single sequential route. It offers marketers a diagnostic framework for segmenting consumers by decision architecture and designing adaptive AI-enabled shopping experiences accordingly.

latest.title: Evaluating human-like chatbot interaction in customer service: integrating anthropomorphism and conversational capability
latest.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI)-based technology has driven the development of rule-based chatbots into AI-based chatbots. This development is used by various companies to use AI chatbots as the frontline of customer service. Meeting user expectations for AI chatbots requires an evaluation model to measure chatbot quality. Based on the literature, chatbot evaluation models still focus solely on technical quality, even as AI chatbots are evolving towards human-like services. This research will explore the integration of the technical dimensions of information system success with a new dimension, namely Human-Like Chatbot Interaction (HLCI) as a higher-order construct of anthropomorphism and conversational capability. This quantitative study uses an explanatory research approach. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of users of the Veronika chatbot, owned by Telkomsel, an Indonesian telecommunications company. A total of 213 respondents had data ready for analysis using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) method in SmartPLS 4, namely the measurement model and structural model tests. The analysis results show that service quality is not significantly related to user satisfaction but has a direct effect on trust. Meanwhile, information quality, system quality, and human-like chatbot interaction are positively related to trust and user satisfaction. Trust and user satisfaction are positively related to intention to continue using. The results of this study can contribute both theoretically and practically to modern AI chatbot quality evaluation models.

latest.title: A transformer-based explainable machine learning framework for heterogeneous ESG risk and return prediction using text intelligence
latest.abstract: Corporate ESG disclosure has shifted toward narrative form, yet vendor ESG ratings that most empirical work depends on show substantial disagreement across providers, and encoders dominant in financial text analysis inherit a 512-token ceiling that discards most of a typical 10-K. HET-ESGFormer combines hierarchical long-document encoding, heterogeneity-aware sparse expert routing conditioned on industry sector and firm size, and a dual-channel explanation layer subject to faithfulness verification. The framework is evaluated on 3,182 U.S.-listed firms over 2015 to 2024 using 10-K filings, sustainability reports, earnings call transcripts, and ESG-tagged news. Against nine baselines spanning econometric, dictionary-based, contextual encoder, sparse-attention, and time-series approaches, HET-ESGFormer reduces return RMSE from 0.0417 to 0.0389 and QLIKE from 0.148 to 0.128, with Diebold-Mariano tests rejecting equal predictive accuracy against every baseline after correction for multiple comparisons. The text channel's marginal contribution to downside risk prediction is materially larger than its contribution to return prediction, widening at longer forecast horizons, indicating that ESG narratives carry more information about risk than about expected return. Ablations reveal a decoupling between predictive skill and explanation faithfulness: removing the consistency regularizer barely affects accuracy but sharply degrades explanation quality. The dual-channel explanation improves ERASER comprehensiveness by 50% over SHAP applied to XGBoost, and human raters significantly prefer the framework's rationales over SHAP-based rationales on trustworthiness. Decile-sorted long-short portfolios deliver a post-cost Sharpe ratio of 1.31 against 0.74 and 0.62 for portfolios built o

latest.title: L'identité numérique au service de la personnalisation de l'expérience client : un levier de compétitivité pour les entreprises
latest.abstract: Résumé À l’ère du digital, l’identité des consommateurs se construit à travers les données qu’ils génèrent en ligne : profils, historiques d’achats, interactions et comportements numériques. Ces informations constituent une ressource stratégique pour les entreprises, qui les exploitent grâce au Big Data, à l’intelligence artificielle et aux outils CRM afin de proposer des expériences personnalisées. La personnalisation des offres, de la communication et des parcours clients renforce la satisfaction, la fidélisation et la proximité avec la marque. Elle devient ainsi un véritable levier de compétitivité, permettant aux entreprises de se différencier, d’améliorer leur performance marketing et d’optimiser leur productivité. Toutefois, cette dynamique soulève des défis liés à la vie privée, à la confiance numérique et à la régulation des données. Cet article s’attache à comprendre comment l’identité numérique des consommateurs, constituée par l’ensemble des données qu’ils laissent en ligne, peut être utilisée par les entreprises pour concevoir des expériences personnalisées. Il met en évidence les mécanismes par lesquels ces données favorisent l’adaptation des offres, la fidélisation des clients et l’optimisation des stratégies marketing. Il interroge également les retombées de cette personnalisation sur la compétitivité des entreprises, en soulignant à la fois les opportunités d’innovation et les défis liés à la confiance, à la régulation et à l’éthique à l’ère du digital.Mots clés : Identité numérique, Expérience personnalisée, Données clients, Compétitivité des entreprises. Abstract In the digital age, consumer identity is built through the data they generate online: profiles, purchase histories, interactions, and digital behaviors. This information is a strategic resourc

latest.title: The Effects of Digital Entrepreneurship, Digital Literacy, and Digital Platforms on Gen Z Purchase Decisions
latest.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies has fundamentally transformed the competitive landscape of micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). To remain competitive, MSMEs are increasingly required to strengthen their digital entrepreneurial capabilities, improve consumers' digital literacy, and optimize the use of digital platforms. This study examines the effects of digital entrepreneurship, digital literacy, and digital platforms on Generation Z purchase decisions as a strategy for strengthening MSME competitiveness in the era of artificial intelligence. The study employed a quantitative approach involving 175 Generation Z consumers of a local culinary MSME in Bogor, Indonesia. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The findings demonstrate that digital entrepreneurship has a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions (β = 0.336, t = 4.040, p < 0.001). Digital literacy also positively and significantly influences purchase decisions (β = 0.205, t = 2.009, p = 0.045), while digital platforms show a positive and significant effect (β = 0.296, t = 3.180, p = 0.001). The model explains 55.8% of the variance in Generation Z purchase decisions. These findings highlight the importance of integrating entrepreneurial digital capabilities, consumer digital literacy, and effective digital platform utilization to enhance MSME competitiveness. In the era of artificial intelligence, these capabilities provide an important foundation for MSMEs to improve market engagement, strengthen consumer decision-making, and sustain their competitiveness in an increasingly technology-driven business environment.

latest.title: AI-powered capabilities are associated with green new product development through exploratory and exploitative pathways
latest.abstract: Abstract Purpose – This study aims to investigate the mechanisms through which AI‑powered capabilities influence green NPD in manufacturing firms. Specifically, it examines the dual mediating roles of green exploratory and green exploitative, and tests whether the mediating effect of exploration is stronger than that of exploitation in the AI‑green NPD link. Design/methodology/approach – Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory, this study develops a dual mediation framework distinguishing green exploratory (sensing‑driven opportunity identification) from green exploitative (seizing/transforming‑driven process refinement). Hypotheses are tested using survey data from 333 Chinese manufacturing firms across five high‑priority sectors. Hierarchical regression and bootstrapped mediation analysis (PROCESS Model 4; 5,000 resamples) are employed. Findings – The results show that both green exploratory and green exploitative significantly mediate the positive relationship between AI‑powered capabilities and green NPD. Critically, the indirect effect via green exploratory is significantly stronger than that via green exploitative, supporting asymmetric mediation. The full model explains 54% of the variance in green NPD. Originality/value – This study makes three key contributions. First, it unpacks the mediation black box between AI and green NPD by specifying two distinct process architectures. Second, it challenges the “balance assumption” of ambidexterity theory by demonstrating the primacy of exploratory mediation in AI‑enabled green innovation contexts, thereby extending dynamic capabilities theory. Third, it provides a rigorous methodological template for testing dual and asymmetric mediation, offering actionable guidance for managers, AI vendors, and policymakers.

latest.title: Too little, too much, or just right? How AI recommendation information volume shapes trust and consumer behavior
latest.venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) shopping assistants explain why a product is selected, yet the appropriate defaults remain unclear. We define recommendation information volume as the amount of nonredundant, product-relevant information and compare five ordered explanation packages. Study 1 identifies an inverted-U response in a randomized Chinese mobile-retail experiment. Study S1 compares identical messages attributed to an AI assistant or a human salesperson, with separate source-neutral measurement validation. Study 2 reports conditional positive indirect associations through perceived usefulness, trust in AI, and decision comfort, and conditional negative indirect associations through information overload and algorithmic over-justification. Same-session estimates do not establish causal mediation. Its product-version comparison combines complexity, functionality, and safety considerations. Study 3 provides behavioral evidence across 51,248 recommendation impressions and service outcomes for 5000 distinct users. Moderate packages perform best within the tested sets. Bounded information processing explains the benefit–burden trade-off; persuasion knowledge suggests that disproportionate justification depends on expectations of selective versus comprehensive advice, across AI and human sources. Because amount, diagnostic priority, and content composition vary jointly, the experiments identify assigned-package effects, not pure quantity effects. The findings support category-specific testing of default explanations without establishing an exclusively algorithmic mechanism.

latest.title: Creating satisfaction and loyalty among tourists: the power of experiential tourism
latest.abstract: Abstract The current research examines whether experiential tourism activities in the tourism industry can influence tourists’ behaviour. Using the stimulus-organism-response framework, the study examines how experience affects travellers’ intentions for satisfaction and loyalty among online travel agents (OTAs). Data were collected from 208 visitors across five travel destinations in India, specifically wildlife sanctuaries and national parks, to examine their lived experiences. The results were analysed using a partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) approach, indicating that experiential tourism indicators have a direct effect on customer engagement. The study suggests that experiential motivation is vital in shaping tourists’ satisfaction and loyalty. The results suggest that tourists are more likely to return to the OTA and recommend it to others if they have positive experiential motivation during their travel encounter. Moreover, the study highlights the importance of co-creation in the tourism industry. In the challenging competitive space, leveraging experiential strategies can help managers gain a competitive advantage. Travel retailers must focus on increasing tourists’ conscious participation and include certain activities that may motivate them and create enthusiasm. This study is one of the few in India to explore the relationship between experiential activities and tourist satisfaction and loyalty among wildlife sanctuaries and national parks travellers.

latest.title: Dynamic Capabilities, Organizational Resilience, Digital Transformation and Organizational Performance of Deposit-Taking Saccos in Nairobi County, Kenya
latest.venue: Journal of Economics Finance and Management Studies
latest.abstract: This study examined the influence of dynamic capabilities on the organizational performance of deposit-taking SACCOs in Nairobi County, Kenya, and tested the mediating role of organizational resilience and the moderating role of digital transformation. Given the importance of SACCOs and the various challenges they face from digital disruption and regulation, this study aims to investigate the impact of dynamic capabilities on the performance of SACCOs in Kenya’s Nairobi County. The survey design was used to collect data directly from the SACCO managers in the study areas. Out of the 240 questionnaires distributed, 210 yielded usable responses for the study, giving the study an 87.50% response rate. The data were collected using five-point Likert scales and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, hierarchical regression, Hayes PROCESS Models 4 (mediation), 1 (moderation), 14 (moderated mediation), and 59 (second-stage moderated mediation). The findings of the study revealed that dynamic capabilities had a positive and significant effect on organizational performance. Furthermore, dynamic capabilities significantly enhanced the organizational resilience of these SACCOs, and the organizational resilience significantly improved their organizational performance. Additionally, digital transformation significantly predicted their organizational performance. The study also established that organizational resilience partially mediated the relationship between dynamic capabilities and the performance of these SACCOs. The index for moderated mediation was significant, as digital transformation significantly moderated the relationship between dynamic capabilities and the organizational performance of these SACCOs. The findings of this study showed that deposit-t

latest.title: INFLUENCER CREDIBILITY AND TRAVEL DECISION-MAKING AMONG YOUNG GEN Z SOCIAL MEDIA USERS IN PENANG
latest.venue: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
latest.abstract: Social media has become a significant influence on consumer decisions worldwide, including decisions about where and how to travel. Drawing on the source credibility model, this study examined the relationship between three influencer credibility dimensions, attractiveness, trustworthiness and expertise; and travel decision-making among young Generation Z (Gen Z) social media users in Pulau Pinang, Malaysia. A total of 266 respondents aged 18 to 28 were recruited using non-probability purposive sampling, supported by online snowball distribution through university and young-adult networks. Data were collected through a self-administered online questionnaire adapted from established credibility scales and analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression. All three dimensions correlated positively and significantly with travel decision-making at the bivariate level. In the regression model, the three dimensions jointly explained 54.3 per cent of the variance, F(3, 262) = 103.68, p < .001. Expertise emerged as the strongest predictor (β = .49, p < .001), followed by attractiveness (β = .23, p < .001), while trustworthiness made no significant unique contribution (β = .10, p = .165), a result attributable to its strong correlation with expertise (r = .80). The achieved sample was predominantly female (82.0 percent), aged 18 to 24 (91.7 percent), and not in paid employment (83.8 percent); the findings therefore characterise this specific segment of young, highly engaged Gen Z social media users rather than the Gen Z population of Pulau Pinang as a whole. The study extends understanding of influencer credibility in a Malaysian travel context and indicates that destination marketers targeting young Gen Z audiences should prioritise dem

latest.title: The Impact of Audit on Good Governance in Dimen Shoring Incorporated: Basis for Compliance and Transparency
latest.venue: World Journal of Sustainable Advances in Multidisciplinarity
latest.abstract: This study assessed employee perceptions of the impact of audit practices on good governance in Dimen Shoring Incorporated – Calamba, Laguna Branch. Using a quantitative-descriptive research design, data were collected from 105 employees through a close-ended survey questionnaire and analyzed using weighted means. The findings indicated that employees strongly agreed that internal audit practices (overall weighted mean = 3.68), external audit practices (3.66), compliance audit procedures (3.67), and audit frequency and follow-up implementation (3.69) were effectively practiced and contributed to organizational improvement. Results further showed that good governance was strongly perceived in the workplace, particularly in accountability (3.75), compliance with policies and regulations (3.76), ethical management and resource utilization (3.70), and transparency (3.67). The study concluded that employees perceived auditing as a valuable mechanism that supports governance outcomes through strengthened compliance, accountability, transparency, and ethical management. Recommendations focused on improving communication of audit results, enhancing follow-up visibility, strengthening audit procedure orientation, improving decision-related transparency, and reinforcing ethical culture initiatives.

latest.title: Analyzing Consumer Loyalty to Ultra‐Fast Fashion: An Integrative Analysis Based on the Stimulus‐Organism‐Response Model
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT The ultra‐fast fashion industry generates massive online sales, partly because of its ability to attract the custom of Generation Z (Gen Z). Given that this generational cohort typically has low brand loyalty, this paper examines how the dimensions of the stimulus‐organism‐response (S‐O‐R) model explain Gen Z's loyalty to the ultra‐fast fashion industry. For this purpose, the analysis presented in this paper relies on both a linear and an evolutionary view of the S‐O‐R model. Based on data from 208 questionnaires completed by consumers of ultra‐fast fashion, two analytical phases were conducted: (1) partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) and (2) qualitative comparative analysis (QCA). The results of the first phase suggest that consumer sustainability consciousness is associated with brand loyalty directly and under mediation, whereas social media peer communication is associated with brand loyalty only under mediation by brand equity. The second phase shows the relevance of brand equity in explaining both high and low brand loyalty. The configurations explaining high brand loyalty or low brand loyalty show that the relationship of each outcome with consumer sustainability consciousness and social media peer communications reflects psychological mechanisms that allow consumers to overcome the cognitive dissonance between their attitudes and behavior.

latest.title: Komunikasi Bisnis Berbasis AI: Analisis Ketegangan antara Efisiensi Teks Generatif dan Degradasi Otentisitas Brand Voice pada UMKM
latest.venue: Equivalent Journal Of Economic Accounting and Management
latest.abstract: Perkembangan AI generatif menawarkan efisiensi produksi konten pemasaran bagi UMKM, namun memunculkan masalah berupa keseragaman linguistik, hilangnya identitas merek, dan berkurangnya kedekatan emosional. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis karakteristik bahasa AI dalam komunikasi pemasaran UMKM, bentuk intervensi manusia melalui pendekatan Human-in-the-Loop (HITL), serta implikasinya terhadap kepercayaan konsumen. Penelitian kualitatif ini menggunakan metode analisis isi terhadap teks pemasaran AI dan draf modifikasi pelaku usaha. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa teks bawaan AI cenderung homogen, klise, dan kurang mencerminkan konteks budaya lokal. Sebaliknya, intervensi manusia melalui penyesuaian gaya bahasa, humor, adaptasi budaya, dan storytelling terbukti efektif memperkuat identitas merek dan kedekatan dengan audiens. Temuan juga mengindikasikan bahwa konsumen semakin mampu mengenali konten generik, sehingga autentisitas menjadi faktor krusial. Disimpulkan bahwa komunikasi bisnis yang efektif di era AI memerlukan kolaborasi yang memadukan efisiensi draf mesin dengan kapasitas empati dan makna dari manusia. Oleh karena itu, pendekatan HITL menjadi strategi esensial bagi UMKM untuk mempertahankan autentisitas dan meningkatkan kepercayaan konsumen.

latest.title: Integrating the Technology Acceptance Model and Hifz al-Mal: Digital Financial Literacy and Digital Payment Adoption in Shaping Financial Behaviour
latest.venue: International Journal of Academic Research in Business and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of digital financial technologies has reshaped the global payment landscape, contributing to the shift toward a cashless society. While digital payment platform offers greater convenience and efficiency, they can also affect how individuals manage their finances and make spending decisions. This study examines the influence of digital financial literacy and digital payment adoption on responsible financial behaviour by integrating Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) with the Islamic principle of Hifz al-Mal (protection of wealth). Using a quantitative research design, data were collected among 210 university students who actively use digital payment platforms. The study employs Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) to examine the proposed research model. The findings reveal that digital payment usage has a positive and significant effect on financial behaviour and digital financial literacy emerged as the strongest predictor. This study contributes theoretically by integrating TAM and Hifz al-Mal into the domain of financial behaviour and highlighting the critical role of digital financial behaviour as both a driver and a protective mechanism against financial risk.

latest.title: The Taxation of Non-Resident Digital Service Providers Without Physical Presence In Tanzania: Jurisdictional and Enforcement Challenges
latest.venue: East African Journal of Law and Ethics
latest.abstract: The study examines the jurisdictional and enforcement challenges associated with taxing non-resident digital service providers without physical presence in Tanzania. The rapid growth of the digital economy has enabled non-resident providers to supply digital services to Tanzanian consumers without establishing conventional physical premises in the country, creating challenges for traditional tax rules based on physical presence. The study adopts doctrinal and non-doctrinal legal research methodologies. The doctrinal approach analyses relevant tax legislation, subsidiary legislation, policy documents, international tax materials and scholarly literature, while the non-doctrinal approach draws on empirical information obtained from selected respondents and interviews with Tanzania Revenue Authority tax officials. The study is guided by the Ability to Pay Theory, Benefit Theory and Neutrality Theory. The findings indicate that jurisdictional challenges include difficulties in establishing a taxable nexus, determining the location of digital transactions and consumers, accessing information held outside Tanzania, and exercising taxing authority over providers operating across borders. The study further finds that enforcement is constrained by difficulties in identifying and monitoring non-resident providers, obtaining reliable transaction information, reliance on voluntary compliance, limitations in monitoring payment systems, technological and data-integration challenges, and difficulties in enforcing tax liabilities against providers located outside Tanzania. The study concludes that although Tanzania has established a legal and administrative framework for taxing non-resident digital service providers, its effectiveness is constrained by practical jurisdictional and enfo

latest.title: A Study on the Research Description Development at Grand View Research
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: Research Description (RD) development requires the conversion of extensive market information into a concise, accurate and client-facing overview. This case study examines the role of secondary market research in RD creation and updating at Grand View Research (GVR), based on the author’s on-the-job training in the Product Development Team. The study follows a descriptive case-study design using internship observations and publicly available secondary information; no primary survey was conducted. During the training, more than 450 RDs were updated, and more than 50 were created from scratch across multiple industry verticals. The observed workflow included assignment understanding, market and report review, information synthesis, RD drafting, self-quality control, mentor review, revision, and progression to editing and publication. A focused case of artificial intelligence (AI) in marketing within the Consumer Goods segment illustrates how global, segment-level and country-level market information can be synthesized while preserving differences in scope. The study finds that RD quality depends on source relevance and authority, consistency of definitions and numbers, selective synthesis, and human quality control. It recommends a standardized RD checklist, a structured knowledge repository and carefully governed AI-assisted checks with human validation.

latest.title: Significance of OTT platforms and challenges faced by the Pakistani film industry
latest.abstract: This paper examines the position of local Over-The-Top (OTT) platforms in Pakistan such as Tamasha, SeePrime, Tapmad, and UrduFlix and the issues they encounter in the changing media environment in Pakistan. These sites have revolutionized the way viewers (especially the younger ones) watch movies and plays by offering them the convenience of on-demand viewing. They have also provided a platform to filmmakers to present a variety of stories and spread Pakistani culture beyond conventional cinemas. Along with these opportunities, the Pakistani OTT platforms have a number of challenges that restrain its growth. They cannot fulfil the demands of the audience because of low budget, censorship, piracy, weak internet connection, and inadequate technology. Most of the viewers want quality productions yet they want them to be free or pirated, which makes the local platforms even weaker in terms of revenue. The research was quantitative in nature, since it entailed survey of OTT users and media professionals in Pakistan. The survey findings indicate that most of the younger audiences are moving towards the digital platforms, which they find convenient and diverse. Nevertheless, the respondents also pointed to the poor quality and affordability of local services in comparison to international ones. The results indicate that Pakistani OTT platforms need to enhance the quality of productions, invest in low-cost subscriptions, and invest in digital infrastructure so that they can survive and succeed. All these can be addressed by local platforms which can aid in revival of the Pakistani film industry and make it relevant in the digital world.

latest.title: Strategic Cooperation Between the State and Business in the Tourism Industry
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study aims to develop directions for improving the organisational and economic mechanisms of public–private partnership in Ukraine’s tourism sector, based on a comparison with international practice and an analysis of regional tourism tax revenues from 2021 to 2024. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study examines public-private partnership mechanisms in tourism infrastructure development and destination management. It combines a narrative review of 32 purposively selected publications (2021–2025) with official statistics for 24 regions of Ukraine; the research instrument was an analytical matrix of five partnership dimensions, and data were analysed using comparative and trend analyses. Research Limitation: The proposed mechanisms, derived from secondary data, have not been empirically validated. Findings: Effective government–business interaction in tourism depends on a clear distribution of responsibilities, the integration of environmental and social criteria into partnership projects, and the institutionalisation of local community participation. These factors strengthen investment effectiveness, improve destination management, and enhance the long-term sustainability of tourism development. Practical Implication: The findings provide guidance for improving tourism policy, designing effective public-private partnership models, and strengthening the governance of tourism destinations. Social Implication: Strengthened cooperation between the public and private sectors contributes to sustainable tourism, greater community engagement, and balanced regional development. Originality/Value: The study proposes an integrated framework for enhancing organisational and economic mechanisms of state–business cooperation by incorporating sustainable development prin

latest.title: Digital Transformation of MSMEs in Southwest Nigeria: The Interactive Effects of Infrastructure, Digital Skills, and Policy Environment on Adoption and Firm Performance
latest.venue: International Journal of Modern Science and Research Technology
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study explored the digital transformation of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Southwest Nigeria by investigating the effects of digital infrastructure, digital skills, policy environment, and their interaction on digital adoption and firm performance. The study addressed a gap in the literature by evaluating the possibility of the determinants working independently or in complement to each other in influencing the MSME digital transformation. Methodology: The mixed method research design was used by collecting quantitative data from 240 MSMEs in Lagos, Ogun, Oyo and Ekiti States, while qualitative data was gathered through key informant interviews and focus group discussions. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations and Generalized Linear Models (GLM) were used for analyzing quantitative data, and thematic analysis of NVivo software was used for analyzing qualitative data. Findings: The results show that digital infrastructure is the strongest determinant of digital adoption, followed by digital skills and policy environment. The interaction effects of digital infrastructure and digital skills, digital skills and policy environment, and digital infrastructure and policy environment were statistically significant, showing that these factors are complementary and mutually reinforcing. Furthermore, digital adoption, digital infrastructure, digital skills, and policy environment significantly improve MSME performance. These findings suggest that coordinated investments across all three areas yield greater returns than isolated interventions. The study reveals that digital transformation in MSMES in Southwest Nigeria is attributed to the synergistic effect of digital infrastructure, digital capabilities and policy interventions. Originality: T

latest.title: The Legal Framework for Digital Lending by Tier 2 Microfinance Service Providers in Tanzania: Assessing Applicability and Enforcement Challenges
latest.venue: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
latest.abstract: Digital lending through mobile applications has become a major source of credit for individuals and small traders in Tanzania, but it has been accompanied by high and poorly disclosed costs, the harvesting of borrowers’ telephone data and abusive methods of debt collection. This article examines the legal framework that regulates digital lending by non-deposit-taking (Tier 2) microfinance service providers in Mainland Tanzania and asks whether that framework is applicable to the lenders it is meant to govern and capable of being enforced against them. Using doctrinal legal research supplemented by a limited comparison with Kenya, it analyses the Microfinance Act, the Microfinance (Non-Deposit Taking Microfinance Service Providers) Regulations, 2019, the Bank of Tanzania (Financial Consumer Protection) Regulations, 2019, the Guidelines on Fees and Charges, 2024, the Guidance Note on Digital Lenders, 2024, the Personal Data Protection Act, the Electronic Transactions Act and the National Payment Systems Act, and evaluates them against the public interest theory of regulation, the distinction between entity-based and activity-based regulation, and responsive regulation. The article finds that the rules specific to digital lending are contained in a guidance note rather than in regulations, although the Microfinance Act empowers the Bank of Tanzania to make regulations on digital microfinance business; that the price of credit is controlled by disclosure alone; that the binding rules on personal data and debt collection are general and fragmented, with inconsistent sanctions; and that the conduct rules bind only licensed providers, leaving unlicensed and foreign-hosted lenders largely outside the framework. The claim is one about statutory design, established by doctrinal a

latest.title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Tourism Business
latest.abstract: Purpose: To examine the use of artificial intelligence in the tourism industry and evaluate its impact on operational efficiency and service quality in the context of smart tourism. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study combines an analysis of 32 tourism enterprises operating in the European market with a survey of 124 consumers conducted in 2024–2025. Artificial intelligence adoption was assessed through the level of operational process automation, and content analysis of enterprise reports and platform analytics was used to measure performance before and after implementation. Research Limitation: The study is limited to European tourism enterprises and a relatively small consumer sample. Future research should include broader geographical coverage and longitudinal analysis. Findings: Artificial intelligence significantly improved operational performance. Average service time decreased from 18.6 to 11.2 minutes, automation increased from 27.4% to 61.8%, and customer interaction intensity rose from 1.8 to 2.6 contacts per user. Consumers reported high satisfaction with service quality and personalisation, although trust in intelligent systems remained moderate, indicating that behavioural barriers still constrain the full benefits of AI adoption. Practical Implication: The findings support the adoption of hybrid service models that combine artificial intelligence with human interaction. Social Implication: Effective AI implementation can improve service accessibility, customer satisfaction, and the sustainable development of smart tourism. Originality/Value: The novelty lies in an integrated model linking the share of AI-automated processes with operational variables (service time, customer contacts) and consumer variables (service quality, personalisation, trust).

latest.title: AI capacities and digital entrepreneurship: The moderating role of Fintech entrepreneurial ecosystems and university infrastructure
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping digital entrepreneurship by supporting business decision making, digital planning, customer analysis, and process automation. However, the mechanisms through which students’ perceived AI capacities relate to digital entrepreneurial self-efficacy and digital entrepreneurial intention remain insufficiently theorized. Drawing on Social Cognitive Career Theory (SCCT), this study examines whether digital entrepreneurial self-efficacy mediates the association between AI capacities and digital entrepreneurial intention, and whether FinTech entrepreneurial ecosystems and university infrastructure condition these relationships. Based on cross-sectional survey data from 1061 higher education students in Vietnam, the results show that AI capacities are positively associated with digital entrepreneurial self-efficacy, which in turn is positively associated with digital entrepreneurial intention. Crowdfunding is associated with a stronger AI capacities–self-efficacy association, whereas mobile payment shows a negative moderating association and blockchain shows no significant moderation. University entrepreneurial environment and entrepreneurial program learning positively—though modestly—moderate the examined associations. Because the study applies an efficacy-centered, partial specification of SCCT to cross-sectional data, all findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal effects. These findings contribute to technology-enabled entrepreneurship research by linking user-centric AI capacities with financial and institutional boundary conditions in an emerging-market context. Practically, the findings suggest that universities, FinTech providers, and policymakers should not treat all digital-finance and institutional supports as

latest.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Sales Productivity: Field Experiments in Online Retail
latest.abstract: We quantify the short-term impact of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) on sales performance through a series of large-scale randomized field experiments involving millions of users and products at a leading crossborder online retail platform. Over 2023–2024, the platform integrated GenAI into seven business workflows spanning customer service, consumer-product matching, advertising, and seller services. We find that GenAI adoption increases sales in most workflows, with effects ranging from no detectable impact to 16.3% depending on GenAI’s marginal contribution relative to baseline firm practices. Across the four GenAI applications with positive sales effects, the implied annual incremental value is roughly $5 per consumer—an economically meaningful impact given the retailer’s scale and the early stage of GenAI adoption. The gains operate primarily through higher conversion rates rather than larger cart values, consistent with GenAI improving the shopping experience by reducing search, information, communication, and personalization frictions. Importantly, these effects are not associated with worse postpurchase outcomes as product return rates and customer ratings do not deteriorate. Finally, we document substantial demand-side heterogeneity, with larger gains for less experienced consumers. Our findings provide novel, large-scale causal evidence on how GenAI shapes sales productivity in online retail, highlighting both its immediate value and broader potential. This paper was accepted by Jean-Pierre Dube, marketing. Funding: L. Fang acknowledges financial support from the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grants 72501258 and 72192803], the Major Special Project in Philosophy and Social Sciences of the Ministry of Education of China [Grant 2026JZD

latest.title: Do financial analysts improve the quality of earnings forecasting? Evidence from Central Europe, 2014–2024
latest.abstract: Purpose This study examines whether consensus analyst forecasts for annual earnings per share (EPS) are more accurate than a standard random walk (RW) model for companies listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange, the Prague Stock Exchange, the Budapest Stock Exchange and the Bucharest Stock Exchange during 2014–2024. Design/methodology/approach Consensus analyst forecasts for annual EPS from EquityRT are compared against RW model predictions using mean arctangent absolute percentage error, mean absolute error and mean square error. Wilcoxon and permutation tests assess statistical significance. For the Warsaw Stock Exchange, which provides the largest sample, the analysis is further stratified by analyst coverage intensity, firm capitalization, industry classification, corporate governance structure, institutional ownership composition and dividend orientation. Robustness checks employ alternative error metrics across multiple dimensions. Findings Consensus analyst forecasts for annual EPS demonstrate no statistically significant differentiation from RW predictions for Poland (excluding 2020), the Czech Republic (excluding 2020 and 2022), Hungary (excluding 2020) and Romania (excluding 2019 and 2022). This finding holds with respect to ownership structures and dividend policies. In the Polish market, for which detailed multi-dimensional analysis is provided, the absence of analyst advantages persists across annual periods, analyst coverage levels, firm sizes and industry groupings. These results challenge prior evidence of analyst superiority over statistical models in developed markets by drawing on a distinct market setting. Originality/value This investigation provides the first rigorous statistical examination of analyst forecasting performance across the major Central E

latest.title: Revolutionising White‐Collar Help‐Seeking in Organisations: The Impact and Dynamics of Artificial Intelligence‐Driven Chatbots
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT This study explores how white‐collar workers perceive AI‐driven chatbots, and how affordances and constraints shape their help‐seeking behaviours. Help‐seeking is essential for learning and collaboration but is often limited by social barriers. Drawing on Affordance Theory, this research examines how technological and social affordances influence chatbot use. Based on 24 in‐depth interviews, conducted between May and December 2023, at the inception of ChatGPT's public diffusion, the study reveals that chatbots offer judgement‐free support for repetitive and informational tasks, fostering autonomy and bypassing interpersonal discomfort. However, concerns about trust, limited capabilities, surveillance and job security constrain adoption. Individual mindset and age, together with organisational culture (e.g., innovation climate), further influence use. Chatbots redefine help‐seeking as a human‐machine dynamic, complementing rather than replacing human support. The study highlights the importance of designing chatbot systems that align with user needs and workplace cultures. In doing so, it contributes to debates on algorithmic management and worker autonomy and offers practical implications for integrating AI tools to support knowledge sharing and collaboration in work environments.

latest.title: The effects of visual cues on sustainable consumer behavior and their underlying mechanisms
latest.abstract: 摘要： 视觉元素是消费者感知环境刺激、加工产品信息的重要输入, 对可持续消费决策具有重要影响。针对现有关于视觉元素影响可持续消费的研究较为碎片化、结论零散甚至矛盾等问题, 本文基于视觉元素所传递的象征意义与物理功能差异, 将色彩、图像、字体、标识、立体形态与材质等元素归类为图形线索与结构线索, 并系统梳理其对绿色购买、可持续使用与循环处置等行为的影响。为推进视觉线索作用机制的结构化研究, 本文借鉴可持续消费决策中的合意性与可行性考量, 从意义价值评估与执行可能性判断两个维度, 构建视觉线索影响可持续消费的解释框架。具体而言, 图形线索主要通过合意性路径发挥作用, 概念隐喻与认知图式等机制具有较强解释力; 结构线索主要通过可行性路径发挥作用, 可供性与自动分类等机制具有较强解释力。此外, 为丰富视觉线索作用效果的边界研究, 本文从个体层、产品层与环境层挖掘影响视觉线索效应的调节因素。未来可进一步比较两类线索的相对效应, 拓展视觉线索的分类维度, 深入探讨可持续消费行为的多样化表现, 并在数字化场景与互动媒介中推进多感官整合研究。

latest.title: Epistemic Risks and a Framework for Critical Generative AI‐Mediated Reading
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used to explain, summarize, and generate information, yet these activities are rarely framed as reading practices. This conceptual paper examines GenAI‐mediated reading, in which readers engage with responses generated by large language models (LLM) during inquiry and knowledge construction. GenAI frequently presents fluent and synthesized responses whose evidentiary basis, source relations, assumptions, and limitations may remain opaque. This paper identifies three epistemic risks: (a) fluent language may be misrecognized as truth, (b) algorithmic authority may encourage the outsourcing of epistemic judgment, and (c) responsive generation may weaken readers' critical monitoring through confirmation, sycophancy, or automation bias. To address these risks, the paper brings together critical reading and critical literacy and proposes the Critical Generative AI‐mediated Reading (CritGAIR) framework. The framework includes three recursive dimensions: (a) reading the response, (b) reading the system, and (c) reading the self. These dimensions direct attention to evaluating claims, evidence, and source credibility; interrogating authority, sociotechnical conditions, representations, and power; and reflecting on readers' prompts, trust, and uptake, respectively. Guiding questions and a hypothetical reading example illustrate how scrutiny can be calibrated to task purpose and consequences of error. The paper outlines educational applications and directions for investigating readers' evaluative processes, judgment quality, and the effort required for critical engagement.

latest.title: THE IMPACT OF AI-POWERED DIGITAL MARKETING ON CONSUMER PURCHASE INTENTION IN QUICK COMMERCE (WITH SPECIAL REFERENCE TO CHENNAI CITY)
latest.venue: International Journal of Progressive Research in Engineering Management and Science
latest.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered digital marketing has transformed the quick commerce industry by enabling personalised advertisements, product recommendations, predictive analytics, and targeted promotional campaigns.The present study aims to examine the impact of AI-powered digital marketing on consumer purchase intention in quick commerce, with special reference to Chennai City.The study focuses on how personalised marketing messages, AIbased recommendations, chatbots, and customised offers influence consumer preferences, buying decisions, and purchase intention.It also examines the role of consumer trust, perceived usefulness, convenience, and privacy concerns in shaping responses to AI-driven marketing strategies.The study adopts a descriptive research design, with primary data collected from quick commerce consumers through a structured questionnaire.Suitable statistical tools may be employed to analyse the relationship between AI-powered marketing practices and consumer purchase intention.The findings are expected to provide insights for quick commerce companies to develop effective digital marketing strategies, improve customer engagement, and strengthen consumer relationships in the competitive online marketplace.

latest.title: The Nexus Between Sustainable Human Resource Management and Sustainable Development Goals—Literature Review and Future Research Directions
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable Human Resource Management (SHRM) has emerged as a strategic approach for enabling organisations to simultaneously achieve economic, social and environmental sustainability. Despite the growing body of SHRM research, limited attention has been devoted to systematically examining how SHRM contributes to the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This study addresses this gap by combining a bibliometric analysis with a systematic literature review to examine the evolution, intellectual structure and research themes of SHRM, while developing a transparent framework for mapping SHRM research to the SDGs. Following the PRISMA guidelines, 1129 articles published between 2015 and 2026 were retrieved from the Scopus and Web of Science databases and analysed using VOSviewer. The findings reveal a substantial increase in SHRM research since 2020 and identify six dominant clusters. Building on these themes, this study develops a coding framework that systematically links the identified clusters to multiple SDGs. The findings highlight the multidimensional role of SHRM in advancing the social, economic, environmental and institutional dimensions of the 2030 Agenda while identifying emerging future research areas. This study extends the existing SHRM literature by providing a comprehensive synthesis of the field, introducing a transparent SDG mapping framework and offering practical guidance for organisations seeking to align their human resource strategies with sustainable development objectives.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: STRATEGIC SUCCESSION PLANNING AND ORGANIZATIONAL RESILIENCE IN SUSTAINABLE FAMILY ENTERPRISES: A CAPABILITY-BASED PERSPECTIVE
latest.venue: Issues in Contemporary Accounting and Business
latest.abstract: Strategic succession planning is increasingly recognized as a critical determinant of the long-term sustainability of family enterprises. However, extant literature has largely examined succession as a leadership replacement or governance process, with limited attention to the organizational mechanisms through which it contributes to sustainable enterprise development. This conceptual paper develops a capability-based framework that explicates how strategic succession planning enhances organizational resilience and ultimately, sustainable family enterprise development. This study adopts a narrative literature review and theory synthesis approach, drawing on the Resource-Based View (RBV), Dynamic Capability Theory (DCT) and contemporary literature on family business succession, organizational resilience, governance and sustainability. Through conceptual integration of extant literature, this paper develops a framework in which formal succession planning and systematic successor identification strengthen organizational resilience by preserving strategic knowledge, institutionalizing governance and improving organizational adaptability. This framework advances succession planning beyond its classical role as a leadership replacement mechanism by positioning it as a strategic capability that enables family enterprises to preserve valuable organizational resources while continuously renewing capabilities required to navigate environmental uncertainty and intergenerational transitions. This study contributes to family businesses and strategic management literatures by integrating RBV and DCT into a unified capability-based explanation of succession planning and by identifying organizational resilience as the critical mechanism linking succession planning to long-term sustaina
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: How do virtual streamers turn viewership traffic into sales? Consumer behavior mechanisms from an interaction characteristics perspective
latest.abstract: 摘要： 人工智能驱动的虚拟主播能够作为真人主播的补充, 在直播带货中与消费者互动, 然而直播效果参差不齐, 这影响了其在电商直播领域的广泛应用。本研究从虚拟主播交互特征的视角研究消费者购买决策行为的影响因素及其作用机制。具体包括: (1)虚拟主播形象对消费者购前行为的影响, 以及产品信息呈现的调节作用; (2)虚拟主播沟通风格对消费者购前行为的影响, 以及消费者特征和产品类型的调节作用; (3)消费者对虚拟主播服务质量的购后口碑评价。本研究构建了信息与情感双路径整合分析框架, 弥补了现有研究对虚拟主播交互机制与购后行为影响机制缺乏探讨的不足, 拓展了电商直播与消费者在线行为领域的理论边界。在实践层面, 该框架为提升消费者直播参与度、优化购买决策, 以及推动数字经济与电子商务高质量发展提供了理论支撑。

latest.title: The AI trust paradox: how disclosure, brand authenticity and consumer mindset shape communication effectiveness
latest.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the trust paradox in artificial intelligence (AI)-generated content, where efficiency conflicts with perceived inauthenticity. Integrating source credibility theory and congruity theory, it examines how the interplay between ad genesis (AI vs. genuine), strategic context (disclosure, brand authenticity) and consumer mindset (construal level) determines communication effectiveness. Design/methodology/approach A three-study experimental design was employed to isolate specific contingencies. Study 1 manipulated ad genesis and AI disclosure to test engagement. Study 2 examined the moderating role of brand authenticity on purchase intentions. Study 3 tested the congruity between AI message focus (hedonic vs. utilitarian) and consumer construal levels. Findings Genuine imagery generally outperforms AI-generated imagery; however, effectiveness is contingent on strategic fit. Disclosure boosts engagement for genuine ads but reduces it for AI content. AI ads enhance purchase intentions for low-authenticity brands but damage high-authenticity ones. Furthermore, hedonic AI appeals align with high-construal mindsets, whereas utilitarian appeals suit low-construal consumers. Research limitations/implications The experiments used static images in controlled online settings. Future research should test dynamic and multimodal AI content and validate the effects with real-world behavioral metrics, such as click-through and conversion rates. Practical implications AI use should fit the context. Heritage brands should avoid AI imagery, whereas challenger brands can benefit from it. Disclosure helps genuine-image ads but hurts AI-generated ads. Hedonic AI appeals suit abstract mindsets, whereas utilitarian appeals suit concrete mindsets. Originality/value Th

latest.title: Exploring the Potential of Rural Marketing in Bangladesh: Opportunities for Sustainable and Inclusive Development
latest.venue: Research journal in business and economics.
latest.abstract: Rural marketing has immense potential to become a sustainable and inclusive development in Bangladesh since more than half the population is rural. The aim of the paper is to explore the implicit aspects that impact the growth and sustainability of rural marketing opportunities. The quantitative research design was the methodology applied, which included a questionnaire that was structured and 460 rural respondents represented various occupational groups, education levels, and income brackets. Data were tested using descriptive statistics, correlation, and multiple regression analysis to determine the most significant predictors of marketing opportunities in rural locations. The results indicate that the most significant effect on market growth is made by infrastructure development and government support, technology adoption, distribution systems, and consumer awareness have moderately significant impact. Nonetheless, growth is still hampered by structural factors like poor transport, poor financial inclusion, and unreliable implementation of policies. The analysis highlights that to unlock the potential of untapped rural markets, coordinated efforts that incorporate infrastructure, technology, supply chains, consumer education, and good policies are critical to achieving the desired outcomes. The insights are useful to businesses interested in market penetration, and policymakers who want to develop frameworks to enable inclusive rural development.

latest.title: Enhancing Social and Environmental Sustainability in Tourism Through Smart Tourism Systems Integration
latest.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT This research is an explanatory sequential mixed‐methods study focused on the effect of Smart Tourism Systems (STS) on sustainable tourism. 543 participants were included, and 22 were interviewed in a semi‐structured manner. Structural equation modeling found significant positive associations across the model. Environmental sustainability tourism was associated with social sustainability tourism ( β = 0.508), and social sustainability tourism with sustainable development outcomes ( β = 0.426). Smart tourism systems with environmental sustainability in tourism ( β = 0.405), real‐time environmental monitoring ( β = 0.252), and information transparency ( β = 0.181) were associated with environmental sustainability, while perceived usefulness ( β = 0.174), perceived ease of use ( β = 0.221), and carrying‐capacity control ( β = 0.189) were associated with social sustainability. Qualitative findings highlighted stakeholder inclusion, conservation, digitalization, resilience, and responsible governance. The research expanded the Technology Acceptance Model in that the capabilities of technology for environmental and social sustainability were shown.

latest.title: Pathways, Strategies, and Conditions: A Resource Reservoir Framework for Tourism Startup Ecosystems
latest.abstract: Tourism startups are increasingly positioned as agents of renewal, yet existing theory offers limited insight into how these ventures navigate external resource environments they depend on. Resource-based perspectives privilege internal capabilities, while ecosystem approaches treat entrepreneurial contexts as relatively undifferentiated. Drawing on 57 in-depth interviews, conducted in 2025, with founders and ecosystem coordinators across 26 countries, this study develops the Startup Ecosystem Resource Reservoir (SERR) framework. This framework theorizes tourism entrepreneurial environments along three analytical layers: a pathway layer distinguishing Endowed-Access Resources (allocated through gatekeeper selection) from Ambient-Access Resources (worked out through participation and relational labor); a strategy layer identifying three founder postures (substantive engagement, performative conformity, and pathway avoidance) through which ventures engage these pathways; and a conditioning layer in which a structurally bifurcated legitimacy regime (investor-track and industry-incumbent-track) and infrastructural conditions shape availability and posture viability across the reservoir.

latest.title: Mukhang Totoo, Mukhang AI: Isang Kritikal na Pagsusuri sa Kulturang Biswal ng AI Face Filters at ang Konstruksyon ng Pamantayan ng Kagandahan ng Kabataang Pilipino
latest.venue: International Journal of Research on Multidisciplinary Studies
latest.abstract: Bagama’t maraming pag-aaral ang tumalakay sa impluwensiya ng midyang panlipunan at mga beauty filter sa pananaw ng mga gumagamit sa pisikal na anyo, limitado pa ang pananaliksik na sumusuri kung paano binibigyang-kahulugan ng mga mag-aaral sa kolehiyo sa kontekstong Pilipino ang mga katangiang biswal ng AI face filters at ang papel ng mga ito sa konstruksyon ng pamantayan ng kagandahan sa kulturang biswal. Layunin ng pag-aaral na kritikal na suriin ang mga katangiang ginagamit ng mga mag-aaral sa pagtukoy ng mga larawang binago gamit ang AI face filters, ang kahulugang iniuugnay nila sa mga katangiang ito, at ang papel ng mga filter sa paghubog ng pamantayan ng kagandahan. Gumamit ang pag-aaral ng kwalitatibong disenyo sa pamamagitan ng Visual Elicitation Technique (VET) at semi-structured interview. Limang (5) mag-aaral na may edad na labingwalong taong gulang pataas mula sa Don Carlos Polytechnic College ang lumahok sa pag-aaral. Ipinakita sa kanila ang dalawampung (20) larawan na binubuo ng sampung orihinal na selfie at sampung bersiyong binago gamit ang AI face filters. Sinuri ang mga nakalap na datos sa pamamagitan ng thematic analysis. Ipinakita ng mga resulta na ginagamit ng mga kalahok ang pagkawala ng likas na detalye ng balat, proporsyon ng mukha, at kabuuang pagiging makatotohanan ng larawan bilang mga palatandaan ng paggamit ng AI face filters. Iniuugnay nila ang mga katangiang ito sa idealisadong kagandahan, digital na presentasyon ng sarili, at pagkakaiba ng artipisyal at likas na anyo. Lumitaw din na nakikilahok ang mga filter at midyang panlipunan sa pagpapalaganap at normalisasyon ng pamantayang nakasentro sa makinis, simetrikal, at tila walang kapintasang mukha. Gayunman, kinikilala ng mga kalahok na hindi ganap na itinatakda ng teknolohiya ang kahulug

latest.title: From E-Commerce to AI Commerce: Rethinking the Consumer Journey in the Era of AI Agents
latest.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
latest.abstract: The emergence of increasingly autonomous Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents is reshaping how consumers search for information, evaluate alternatives, and make purchasing decisions. While existing consumer journey models have incorporated AI primarily as a decision-support technology, they provide limited conceptual guidance for understanding situations in which AI agents perform purchasing activities on consumers’ behalf. Drawing on consumer journey theory, AI-enabled commerce, and human–AI collaboration research, this conceptual paper adopts a theory-adaptation approach to examine how established frameworks may be extended to account for emerging forms of delegated decision-making. We propose the Human–AI Collaborative Consumer Journey, a framework that conceptualizes purchasing as a collaborative process involving consumers and consumer-authorized AI agents across different stages of the journey. Its central contribution is the concept of Delegated Consumer Agency (DCA), defined as the configuration of authority consumers grant AI agents to perform cognitive or operational purchasing activities within predefined goals and constraints. The framework highlights how human and AI participation may vary across purchasing contexts and identifies implications for consumer autonomy, decision-making, and e-commerce management. Finally, six research propositions and a future research agenda are presented to guide empirical investigation.

latest.title: DIGITAL MARKETING AND CUSTOMER ENGAGEMENT IN THE AGE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE A STUDY OF PERSONALIZATION, TRUST, PRIVACY, AND CONSUMER RESPONSE
latest.venue: International Journal of Progressive Research in Engineering Management and Science
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping digital marketing through recommendation engines, conversational agents, predictive analytics, automated content, and individualized customer journeys.These tools can make interactions more relevant and efficient, yet they also raise questions about privacy, transparency, algorithmic bias, and the authenticity of brand communication.This paper develops an integrated framework for examining how AI-enabled personalization, interaction quality, trust, and privacy concern relate to customer engagement and downstream outcomes such as satisfaction, loyalty, and purchase intention.Drawing on research in AI marketing and AI-enabled service, it proposes a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design using a structured questionnaire and five-point Likert items.The proposed analysis includes descriptive statistics, reliability assessment, correlation analysis, multiple regression, and hypothesis testing.Statistical figures included in this document are explicitly illustrative examples generated from synthetic values to demonstrate how results can be presented; they are not observations from real respondents and must not be reported as empirical findings.The paper provides a practical foundation for a student research project and identifies managerial implications for designing customer-centred, transparent, and responsible AI marketing.

latest.title: From awareness to action: mapping online gambling prevention and treatment research through a social marketing lens
latest.abstract: Social marketing interventions have emerged as important approaches for addressing online gambling-related harm, particularly amid the proliferation of digital gambling platforms and sophisticated marketing practices. However, existing bibliometric studies on gambling prevention have paid limited attention to the social marketing dimensions. This study addresses this gap by conducting a bibliometric analysis of 333 peer-reviewed articles selected from 481 Scopus-indexed records using predefined document type, language, publication year, and relevance criteria. Social marketing is operationally defined as the application of marketing principles to influence voluntary behaviours for individual and societal benefit, particularly prevention, harm reduction, consumer protection, and responsible gambling. Using VOSviewer, the study identifies research streams and thematic clusters, highlighting growth since 2005. Bibliographic coupling identified four areas: safer gambling message effectiveness and consumer protection, behavioural addiction mechanisms, industry practices and regulatory responses, and problem gambling epidemiology and behavioural patterns. Co-word analysis revealed three clusters related to responsible gambling campaigns, psychological and population-level vulnerability, and technology-related addiction patterns. The findings reveal an uneven geographic distribution, with research concentrated in English-speaking countries. Persistent gaps remain in cross-cultural prevention, harm-reduction messaging, and the integration of emerging technologies into intervention design. The study provides a knowledge map and identifies future research directions.

latest.title: Service Quality and Price Effects on Customer-Perceived Firm Performance: The Mediating Role of Trust at PT Anugrah Karunia Mahakam
latest.abstract: In shipping agency and general supplier services, customers evaluate providers through operational dependability, pricing practices, and confidence in business commitments. This study examined the associations of service quality and price with customer-perceived firm performance and considered customer trust as a potential intermediary at PT Anugrah Karunia Mahakam. A quantitative explanatory, cross-sectional survey was conducted with 61 customers selected through purposive sampling. Responses to a 19-indicator, five-point Likert-type questionnaire were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4.0. All indicators exceeded the specified outer-loading threshold, and the reported AVE and HTMT values met the measurement criteria. Price showed the largest association with trust (β = 0.778), whereas the service quality–trust coefficient was small (β = 0.061). For customer-perceived firm performance, the estimated coefficients were 0.397 for trust, 0.277 for service quality, and 0.102 for price. The model explained 55.1% of the variance in trust and 42.9% in customer-perceived firm performance. These results indicate differences in how pricing and service evaluations relate to relational confidence and perceived organizational performance within the surveyed company. The coefficient pattern is compatible with a possible indirect pathway through trust, but the statistical significance of mediation cannot be established from the reported coefficients without bootstrap inference. The findings support cautious managerial attention to pricing fairness, service dependability, and trust while acknowledging the single-company, nonprobability, cross-sectional design.

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Abstract Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer

hot.title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
hot.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
hot.abstract: People increasingly use videos on the Web for learning, be it for daily tasks in formal or informal educational settings. To enhance this type of learning, scientists are continuously conducting experiments, proposing guidelines, analyzing data, and researching artificial intelligence methods for tool development. In this comprehensive review, we analyze 257 articles (using PRISMA guidelines) on video-based learning from a technological perspective for the period from 2016 to 2021. One of the aims is to identify video characteristics that support learning as explored by previous research. Based on our analysis, we suggest a taxonomy that organizes the video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: (1) audio features, (2) visual features, (3) textual features, (4) instructor behavior, (5) learners’ activities (play, pause, etc.), (6) interactive features (quizzes, etc.), (7) production style, and (8) instructional design. Also, we identify four representative methodological approaches: (1) tool support of video-based learning, (2) controlled experiments, (3) data analysis studies, and (4) design guidelines for learning videos. We find that the most explored characteristics are textual features followed by visual features, learners’ activities, and interactive features. Tools that aid learning through videos frequently utilize text from transcripts, video frames, and images. The learner’s activity is heavily explored through log files in data analysis studies, and interactive features are frequently scrutinized in controlled experiments. As further contributions, we contrast research findings on how video characteristics affect learning effectiveness, report on tasks and technologies used to develop tools, and summarize design guideline trends to prod

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control.
