latest.title: PENDAMPINGAN TRANSFORMASI DIGITAL MELALUI PENGEMBANGAN DAN IMPLEMENTASI WEBSITE EDOTEL DI SMK NEGERI 2 GORONTALO
latest.abstract: SMK Negeri 2 Gorontalo memiliki edOTEL sebagai unit hotel latih yang berfungsi sebagai sarana pembelajaran praktik bagi siswa Kompetensi Keahlian Perhotelan. Namun, pengelolaan edOTEL masih menghadapi kendala berupa promosi konvensional, pencatatan reservasi kamar secara manual, dan latihan praktik front office berbasis dokumen kertas. Kondisi tersebut menyebabkan proses administrasi kurang efisien dan belum optimal dalam mendukung kesiapan siswa menghadapi sistem perhotelan digital. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan mengembangkan, menyosialisasikan, dan mengimplementasikan website edOTEL yang mengintegrasikan fungsi promosi, manajemen reservasi berbasis web, dan e-learning simulasi praktik front office. Kegiatan dilaksanakan selama Mei–Juli 2026 dengan melibatkan 58 peserta, terdiri atas 8 guru/pengelola dan 50 siswa Kompetensi Keahlian Perhotelan. Metode pelaksanaan menggunakan pendekatan Participatory Action Learning yang dipadukan dengan Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) model Waterfall, meliputi analisis kebutuhan, perancangan, pengembangan dan pengujian, pelatihan, serta evaluasi. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan bahwa landing page, sistem manajemen reservasi, modul e-learning front office, serta sosialisasi dan distribusi panduan digital mencapai ketercapaian 100%, sedangkan integrasi payment gateway mencapai 60%. Evaluasi terhadap 58 responden menunjukkan tingkat penerimaan dan kelayakan sistem sebesar 87,91% dengan kategori sangat layak. Dengan demikian, website edOTEL mampu meningkatkan efisiensi administrasi dan promosi serta mendukung pembelajaran digital terapan dalam ekosistem Teaching Factory

latest.title: Depression, anxiety, stress, and intolerance of uncertainty during the COVID-19 pandemic by considering the impact of pre-existing mental health issues
latest.abstract: Purpose This research was conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic. This study aims to investigate self-reported mental health issues in a public sample, including depression, anxiety and intolerance of uncertainty about the future. Design/methodology/approach A public sample (N = 313) was obtained through social media, and collected using an online survey. Participants completed a series of demographic questions including disclosure about previous mental health issues, the depression anxiety stress scale (DASS) and the intolerance uncertainty scale (IUS). Findings There was a strong positive relationship between elements of the DASS and IUS. Having previous mental health issues were strongly associated with higher scores across all measures. Originality/value Evidence is provided to support the notion that additional stress, anxiety and fear is experienced by people with pre-existing mental health issues during unprecedented times. This research offers a unique insight into the mental health of the general public during a global pandemic.

latest.title: Challenges Faced by Parents in Raising Children with Special Needs: A Narrative Literature Review
latest.venue: Journal Of Education And Teaching Learning (JETL)
latest.abstract: Parents raising children with special needs face interconnected psychological, physical, social, financial, and service-related challenges. This narrative literature review aimed to synthesize evidence on parental difficulties, influencing factors, coping strategies, and support needs. Fifteen empirical studies published between 2019 and 2026 were selected through eligibility screening and qualitative appraisal. Data were extracted using a structured matrix and analyzed through thematic narrative synthesis. The findings showed that parents commonly experienced emotional distress, fatigue, stigma, social isolation, financial pressure, employment disruption, family strain, and limited access to healthcare, rehabilitation, and inclusive education. The severity of these challenges was shaped by the child’s condition, parental knowledge, coping capacity, family support, socioeconomic status, cultural beliefs, geographical location, and service accessibility. Parents used acceptance, information seeking, spiritual practices, advocacy, structured routines, and social support. The review highlights the need for continuous family-centered services integrating psychological, educational, financial, professional, workplace, and policy support. Ultimately, establishing robust policy frameworks and fostering cross-sectoral collaboration among healthcare providers, educators, and community leaders are essential to mitigate systemic barriers, alleviate caregiver burnout, and promote holistic family resilience. Furthermore, future empirical research must prioritize longitudinal methodologies to evaluate the sustainable real-world efficacy, accessibility, and scalability of culturally tailored intervention programs across diverse socioeconomic landscapes.

latest.title: Supply chain networks in horticulture: an assessment of farmers' perceptions and market linkages
latest.venue: Modern Supply Chain Research and Applications
latest.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the determinants of horticulture supply chain efficiency (SCE) and the mediating effects of market linkage strength (MLS). Design/methodology/approach The study conceptualises and tests a partial least squares structural equation modelling model based on the resource-based view and relational exchange theory, with the data collected from 500 horticultural farmers from Shimla, Kullu and Kinnaur districts of Himachal Pradesh. Findings The findings show that logistics capability (LC) has the strongest effects on MLS (β = 0.395) and SCE (β = 0.388), followed by information and coordination (IC). Transaction fairness (TF) and digital adoption (DA) significantly strengthen MLS, while MLS positively influences SCE (β = 0.233). MLS provides complementary mediation for LC and IC and indirect-only mediation for TF and DA. Originality/value The study integrates operational capabilities and relational mechanisms to explain how market linkages contribute to horticultural supply-chain efficiency, offering context-specific evidence from an underexplored horticultural setting.

latest.title: The social self in sustainable luxury services: psychological ownership, identification and willingness to use
latest.abstract: Purpose Drawing on symbolic interactionism, this study aims to examine how social expressiveness influences consumers’ willingness to use sustainable luxury services (SLS). It further investigates the mediating roles of identification with SLS and utilitarian well-being, and the moderating role of psychological ownership. Design/methodology/approach The research uses a two-study design. Study 1 uses survey data from Prolific to test the hypothesized direct, mediation and moderation relationships and to assess the measurement model. Study 2 provides field-based evidence using two Facebook advertisements for a sustainable luxury hotel and click-through rate (CTR) as the behavioral outcome. Study 1 was analyzed using structural equation modeling and moderation analysis. Findings Social expressiveness is positively associated with willingness to use SLS, and this relationship is sequentially mediated by identification with SLS and utilitarian well-being. Psychological ownership significantly moderates the relationships among social expressiveness, identification, utilitarian well-being and willingness to use SLS; however, the negative interaction terms indicate attenuation rather than the hypothesized strengthening. In Study 2, the social-expressiveness advertisement generated a CTR more than 40% higher than the non-social-expressiveness advertisement. Originality/value This research extends luxury service research by showing how a socially expressive motive is translated into willingness to use SLS through identification and well-being. It also positions psychological ownership as a boundary condition in a non-ownership service context, while showing that high psychological ownership can reduce the marginal importance of other drivers of willingness. The study thereby offe

latest.title: Do you really voice for constructiveness? Investigating when and how constructively delivered employee voice fails to be enacted
latest.abstract: Purpose Constructive voice delivery remains a valuable strategy for enhancing managerial voice endorsement. However, its effectiveness may be weakened by how employees present themselves. Drawing on the principle of distinctiveness within attribution theory, this study examines how inconsistencies between employees’ expression of ideas and presentation of strengths influence managerial perceptions and voice endorsement. Design/methodology/approach A multi-source and multi-wave field study was conducted to investigate how employee-exaggerated self-enhancement affects managerial instrumental attribution and subsequent endorsement of constructively delivered voice. Findings The results reveal that employees exhibiting exaggerated self-enhancement are less likely to receive managerial endorsement for their constructively delivered voice, as managers may interpret their voice as instrumental. Originality/value This study highlights that employees’ voice expression and self-presentation are distinct yet interconnected forms of self-expression that shape managerial reactions to employee voice. It offers a more nuanced perspective on how self-expression influences managerial voice endorsement.

latest.title: Realism or retreat: Unilever weighs the future of purpose
latest.abstract: Research methodology The case was prepared entirely from public secondary sources. These include company regulatory filings submitted to the United States Securities and Exchange Commission, Unilever corporate communications and reporting by established business and trade publications. No primary research was conducted, no interviews were held, and no confidential information was used. No information was disguised. Because the case relies only on public sources and does not draw on privileged access to the protagonists, it does not require a signed protagonist release. All factual claims are attributed in the narrative, and quotations are limited to statements already in the public record. Case overview/synopsis For more than a decade, Unilever was regarded as a leader in purpose led business, built on the Sustainable Living Plan launched under chief executive Paul Polman. In April 2024, under new chief executive Hein Schumacher and amid investor pressure, the company scaled back several environmental and social commitments, including its headline plastics and living wage targets, and narrowed its agenda to four priorities. Schumacher framed the change as realism. Less than a year later he stepped down by mutual agreement, and the former chief financial officer, Fernando Fernandez, took charge and sharpened the reset toward a simpler, more focused portfolio. By 2026, the reset met a condition it had not anticipated, as India, Unilever’s second largest market, converted recycled content from ambition into binding law just as the parent company loosened its voluntary targets, leaving Fernandez to set commitments for the next reporting cycle. The case places students at that decision and asks whether a firm’s social and environmental commitments are a defensive strategic a

latest.title: Drivers of sustainable fashion purchase in India: a moderated value framework
latest.abstract: Purpose Although sustainable fashion research has extensively examined either consumer attitudes or purchase intentions, limited studies have explicitly distinguished between the cognitive foundation of attitude and the situationally driven nature of intention within the eco-fashion context. Furthermore, the interactive role of psychological traits such as altruism and mindfulness, along with economic considerations like willingness to pay a premium, in moderating the attitude–intention relationship remains underexplored, particularly in emerging markets such as India. This study aims to address these gaps by developing and empirically validating an integrated framework that captures both individual and contextual drivers of eco-fashion purchase intention. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a comprehensive mixed-methods design informed by grounded theory principles, this study explores the underlying factors that shape the phenomenon. Qualitative data from interviews and FGD enabled themes to emerge inductively, while quantitative survey data validated and extended these insights. Statistical analyses examined relationships among variables, and hypotheses were tested using SEM to ensure robustness of the conceptual model. Findings Environmental consciousness, social influence and marketing stimuli considerably shape eco-fashion attitude and purchase intention, while attitude mediates these relationships. Altruism, mindfulness and willingness to pay strengthen the relationship between attitude and purchase intention. Originality/value The study proposes a moderated value framework that explains sustainable fashion purchase more dynamically by treating altruism, mindfulness and willingness to pay as moderators in the Indian context.

latest.title: Assessing the impact of gender affirming endocrine interventions on the mental health and well-being among transgender youth
latest.abstract: Purpose In the absence of previous systematic longitudinal evidence, this pilot study aims to evaluate the quality of life (QOL) of transgender youth in relation to several other psychological variables impacting the mental health of youth. Design/methodology/approach The cross-sectional descriptive study, conducted as a small-scale trial run, examined several mental health variables such as stress, anxiety, depression, social support, resilience and self-efficacy influencing the QOL of the transgender youth. The participants were assessed for relevant, detailed demographic and clinical information, along with a semi-structured questionnaire. Findings The pilot study included 50 transgenders between 18 and 25 years age category, categorized as youth. Descriptive data indicated the diversity in the demography and perception of transgender individuals about the gender-affirming care received during transitions. The favorable scores of Cronbach’s alpha indicated that the tool is highly reliable for measuring the intended objectives. Low scores of depression, anxiety and stress indicate a good QOL among the youth. Further results also indicate that the gender affirmation care received has a greater impact on the mental health variables that determine the self-identity of the trans individuals. Originality/value Mental health plays a critical role in determining the QOL of transgenders. Therefore, studying the longitudinal impact on suitable gender-affirming endocrine interventions can provide a foundation for drawing evidence-based health care practices and policies to protect the transgender youth, thereby promoting their effective functioning in the society.

latest.title: Fostering Innovative Work Behaviour Through Positive Work Environment: The Moderating Role of Ambidextrous Leadership Evidence From Structural Equation Modeling Approach
latest.abstract: Innovation is increasingly recognised as a critical driver of organizational competitiveness, yet the mechanisms that foster employees’ innovative work behaviour (IWB) remain underexplored. This study investigates the effect of a positive work environment on IWB, with a focus on the moderating role of ambidextrous leadership. Drawing on organizational climate and leadership theories, the research proposes that supportive workplace conditions directly encourage creativity and idea generation, while ambidextrous leadership balancing opening behaviours that promote exploration with closing behaviours that ensure discipline enhances the translation of these ideas into actionable innovations. A quantitative, cross-sectional survey design was employed, with data collected from industry professionals using validated scales for workplace climate, ambidextrous leadership, and innovative work behaviour. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) was applied to test the hypothesized relationships. The findings are expected to confirm that positive work environments significantly influence IWB, and that ambidextrous leadership moderates this relationship, thereby strengthening the impact of workplace positivity on innovation outcomes. This study contributes theoretically by bridging organizational climate and leadership research, extending ambidextrous leadership theory to individual-level innovation, and clarifying pathways to innovation. Practically, it offers actionable insights for organizations to cultivate supportive environments and develop ambidextrous leadership capabilities, ensuring sustained innovation in dynamic markets.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Pet insurance services adoption: how values, reasoning, and insurance literacy shape consumer intentions in an emerging market
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine pet-insurance adoption in India through behavioral reasoning theory (BRT), focusing on how openness to change and social value shape reasons for and against adoption, how these reasons influence attitude and purchase intention and whether insurance literacy strengthens the attitude–intention relationship. Design/methodology/approach A sequential mixed-methods design was used. Interviews with 17 pet owners identified the facilitators and inhibitors. Survey data from 352 respondents were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling to test the mediation and moderation effects. Demographic moderation was treated as an exploratory analysis. Findings Openness to change strengthened both reasons for and reasons against adoption, whereas social value strengthened supportive reasoning and reduced opposing reasoning. Reasons for adoption positively influenced attitude and intention, whereas reasons against adoption had negative effects. Attitude was the strongest predictor of purchase intention, and insurance literacy strengthened the attitude–intention relationship. The unexpected positive association between openness to change and reasons against adoption suggests that receptiveness to novelty may intensify scrutiny of benefits and barriers instead of uniformly increasing adoption readiness. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional sample limits the causal inference and generalizability of the findings. Future research should test the deliberative role of openness to change using longitudinal, behavioral and cross-market designs. Practical implications Insurers should address benefits and barriers, including affordability, exclusions, coverage limits and claims procedures, while using pet-insurance education

latest.title: The Influence of Training and Development, Education and Learning, Performance Management, and Career Development on Nurses' Performance
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of Training and Development, Education and Learning, Performance Management, and Career Development on nurse performance in the Hemodialysis Unit of Ratu Aji Putri Botung Regional Hospital, North Penajam Paser Regency. The study used a quantitative design with a survey approach, supplemented by qualitative data to obtain a comprehensive understanding. Quantitative data were collected through a Likert-scale questionnaire from the entire population of 31 nurses, while qualitative data were obtained through semi-structured interviews and documentation studies. Data analysis was conducted using descriptive analysis and multiple linear regression to test the partial and simultaneous effects of independent variables on nurse performance. The results showed that partially, Training and Development, Education and Learning, and Career Development did not significantly influence nurse performance. Conversely, Performance Management significantly influenced nurse performance. However, simultaneously, all four human resource development variables significantly influenced nurse performance. These findings indicate that in standardized, high-risk clinical work units such as hemodialysis, an objective performance management system, regular evaluations, and consistent feedback are dominant factors in improving performance. Meanwhile, individual development factors serve more as supporting factors that contribute collectively. This study recommends strengthening the performance management system integrated with human resource development programs and adjusting development policies based on the characteristics of the work unit.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: AI-Focused Promotional Positioning and Client Attribution of Responsibility for Accounting Firm Service Failures
latest.abstract: Accounting firms are investing heavily in generative AI and increasingly promoting these investments as central to their service models. While such messaging signals innovation and efficiency, it may also influence how clients assign blame when service errors occur. Drawing on attribution theory, this study employs a between-subjects experimental design to test whether clients assign responsibility for errors differently based on a firm’s marketing emphasis on generative AI versus traditional services. Participants read a scenario in which a firm-prepared tax return contained errors. In one condition, the accounting firm’s marketing highlighted its use of generative AI tools; in the other, it emphasized a focus on traditional services. The source of the error was left ambiguous. Participants exposed to AI-promoting messaging attributed more blame for the errors to the firm, perceived it as having greater control over error prevention, and judged the errors as more likely to recur. These findings suggest that promoting generative AI in firm marketing may raise client expectations about control and reliability, increasing reputational risk even when the technology’s role in an error is unclear. The study contributes to research on attribution in professional services and highlights a potential tradeoff: firms that emphasize technological sophistication may also be seen as more culpable when things go wrong.

latest.title: Multi-objective reinforcement-learning simulation for co-optimizing resource circularity and environmental performance in circular manufacturing
latest.abstract: More regulations require manufacturers to enhance material circularity and reduce their environmental footprint simultaneously; however, it remains unclear whether these two objectives align, and if so, in which domain. A discrete event simulation model for a remanufacturing plant operating multiple production lines with environmental performance measures at the process level is defined as a multiobjective Markov decision process, which is then solved using a preference-conditioned actor–critic technique, employing feasibility masking for the precedence and capacity constraints and adaptive sampling between the surrogate model and the full-scale simulator. Two life cycle accounting methods have been used: Boundary A (cut-off) and Boundary B (avoided burden). The environmental burden reveals three regimes, synergistic, trade-off, and inverted, characterized by transition points in secondary-material input levels at 0.38 and 0.61 for Boundary A and at 0.47 and 0.78 for Boundary B; sweeps with fixed ratios validate these transition points. One conditionally generated network accounts for 87.4% of the non-dominated solutions of eleven scalarized agents using 9.1% of the simulation budget allocated to them, and the switching strategy reduces the number of simulation calls needed to reach the reference hypervolume by 27.7%. A screening based on the unit-cost criterion limits the joint synergistic and economically viable domain to input levels ranging from 0.21 to 0.38. All parameters are synthetic values from published ranges for a single facility, so the boundaries describe a mechanism rather than plant-specific forecasts.

latest.title: Pengaruh Herding Behavior dan Risk Aversion terhadap Partisipasi Investor Muda di Reksa Dana dengan Peran Fintech sebagai Mediator
latest.abstract: This study examines the effect of herding behavior and risk aversion on young investors' participation in mutual funds, with fintech as a mediating variable. A quantitative survey was conducted using a questionnaire distributed to 130 young investors aged 30 years or younger who had invested in mutual funds through fintech applications, selected by purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The results show that herding behavior has no significant direct effect on young investors' participation, whereas risk aversion has a positive and significant direct effect. Fintech positively and significantly affects participation and is positively influenced by herding behavior and risk aversion. Fintech fully mediates the effect of herding behavior on participation and partially mediates the effect of risk aversion. These findings indicate that fintech is a mechanism that channels the behavioral tendencies of young investors into actual participation in mutual fund investment.

latest.title: Global value chains, domestic value creation, and firm performance: machine learning evidence from Vietnam
latest.abstract: This study examines the impact of domestic value added and participation in global value chains (GVCs) on firm performance, based on a sample of 287 observations from listed companies across five key industries in Vietnam's Southeast region during 2020-2024. Three machine learning methods, Ridge Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting, are applied to estimate the influence of each independent variable on firm performance. Ridge regression produced the best estimates of firm performance among these three model types, based on the lowest RMSE (4.97), MAE (2.78), and R-squared (0.57). This suggests that the relationship between GVC-related attributes and firm performance is largely linear and additive. Among the individual predictors, lagged profitability was the most important single predictor of current performance, followed by GVC activity. Notably, domestic added-value predicted firm performance more strongly than foreign added-value. Greater GVC activity therefore does not necessarily translate into stronger firm performance. Instead, firms appear to perform better when global engagement is combined with strong internal capabilities and substantial domestic value creation. Firm size, financial leverage, technological capability, and logistics efficiency also statistically explained variation in firm performance.

latest.title: Business Development Analysis of Ayam Geprek Mas Andre Lubuklinggau Based on Business Life Cycle Theory
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the development of the Ayam Geprek Mas Andre micro, small, and medium enterprise (MSME) in Lubuklinggau based on the Business Life Cycle Theory, including the marketing strategy and product innovation applied by the business. The research method used is a qualitative approach with a case study method. The subjects of this study were selected purposively, consisting of the business owner, employees, and customers of Ayam Geprek Mas Andre. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observation, and documentation. The data analysis technique used is the interactive analysis model developed by Miles, Huberman, and Saldana, which includes data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing/verification. The findings show that Ayam Geprek Mas Andre passed through the introduction/birth stage since its establishment in 2017 with pecel lele as its initial product, before developing into the growth stage (Growth Stage) after switching to ayam geprek as its main product, marked by increased consumer interest, business expansion to 13 branches, product innovation, and the use of digital marketing. The conclusion of this study is that Ayam Geprek Mas Andre is currently in the growth stage of its business life cycle, supported by product quality, affordable pricing, innovation, and adaptability to market changes, although it still faces challenges such as rising business competition, changing consumer preferences, and digital technology developments.

latest.title: Is It Healthy for the Human Race for Breasts to Be Sexual Icons?
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: The human female breast occupies an unusual position in biology and society, functioning as an organ of infant nutrition, a secondary sexual characteristic, a source of erotic pleasure, and a prominent symbol of femininity and sexual attractiveness. This interdisciplinary review examines whether the sexual symbolism assigned to breasts benefits or harms human well-being, integrating evolutionary biology, anthropology, psychology, neuroscience, and reproductive health. The investigation distinguishes sexual attraction from objectification, biological characteristics from culturally learned preferences, and voluntary erotic expression from imposed expectations. Research demonstrates that breast attractiveness reflects physical characteristics and sociocultural influences, while sexual objectification is associated with body dissatisfaction, psychological distress, and diminished perceptions of women's competence and personhood. Public breastfeeding further reveals conflicts between the breast's nutritional function and sexual interpretation. Nevertheless, sexual attraction is not inherently pathological, and evidence does not establish that eliminating breast-related erotic symbolism would improve human well-being. The principal concern is whether societies transform sexual significance into compulsory appearance standards, restrictions on bodily autonomy, or judgments about human worth. A healthy social framework must accommodate biological attraction, consensual sexuality, breastfeeding, anatomical diversity, and individual dignity without making any interpretation of the female breast compulsory.

latest.title: Faktor-Faktor Penentu Kinerja Manajerial Kepala Desa: Peran Komunikasi Interpersonal, Kepribadian, dan Motivasi Kerja
latest.abstract: The managerial performance of village heads is crucial for effective local governance; however, it remains suboptimal due to limited managerial capacity. This study examines the influence of interpersonal communication, personality, and work motivation on managerial performance using an integrated causal model. A quantitative explanatory survey was conducted among 115 village heads in Bogor Regency, selected through probability sampling. Data were collected via structured questionnaires and analyzed using path analysis to assess both direct and indirect relationships. The findings indicate that interpersonal communication, personality, and work motivation significantly influence managerial performance, with work motivation emerging as the strongest predictor. Interpersonal communication and personality also exert a positive influence on work motivation, although their mediating role is less pronounced than their direct effects. These results highlight the central role of internal motivation—supported by effective communication and adaptive personality traits—in enhancing managerial performance. This study offers an integrative empirical model of behavioral factors within village governance and contributes to the literature on organizational behavior in the public sector..
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Evaluating human-like chatbot interaction in customer service: integrating anthropomorphism and conversational capability
latest.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI)-based technology has driven the development of rule-based chatbots into AI-based chatbots. This development is used by various companies to use AI chatbots as the frontline of customer service. Meeting user expectations for AI chatbots requires an evaluation model to measure chatbot quality. Based on the literature, chatbot evaluation models still focus solely on technical quality, even as AI chatbots are evolving towards human-like services. This research will explore the integration of the technical dimensions of information system success with a new dimension, namely Human-Like Chatbot Interaction (HLCI) as a higher-order construct of anthropomorphism and conversational capability. This quantitative study uses an explanatory research approach. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of users of the Veronika chatbot, owned by Telkomsel, an Indonesian telecommunications company. A total of 213 respondents had data ready for analysis using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) method in SmartPLS 4, namely the measurement model and structural model tests. The analysis results show that service quality is not significantly related to user satisfaction but has a direct effect on trust. Meanwhile, information quality, system quality, and human-like chatbot interaction are positively related to trust and user satisfaction. Trust and user satisfaction are positively related to intention to continue using. The results of this study can contribute both theoretically and practically to modern AI chatbot quality evaluation models.

latest.title: The Role of Social Media and Digital Content in Increasing Sales of Culinary MSMEs in Lubuklinggau
latest.abstract: This study aims to determine and analyze the role of social media and digital content in increasing sales of culinary Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Lubuklinggau City, both partially and simultaneously. This study used a quantitative approach with an associative research design. Primary data were collected through questionnaires from 77 culinary MSME respondents selected using purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with SPSS version 25. The results showed that Social Media (X1) had a positive and significant effect on Sales Increase (Y), with a t-value of 11.029. Digital Content (X2) also had a positive and significant effect on Sales Increase (Y), with a t-value of 12.078. Simultaneously, Social Media and Digital Content significantly affected Sales Increase, with an F-value of 143.128. The R Square value of 0.795 indicates that the two independent variables jointly explain 79.5% of the variation in sales increase, while 20.5% is explained by other factors outside the study. These findings indicate that more optimal social media utilization and better digital content quality can strengthen the opportunity for culinary MSMEs to increase sales.

latest.title: A transformer-based explainable machine learning framework for heterogeneous ESG risk and return prediction using text intelligence
latest.abstract: Corporate ESG disclosure has shifted toward narrative form, yet vendor ESG ratings that most empirical work depends on show substantial disagreement across providers, and encoders dominant in financial text analysis inherit a 512-token ceiling that discards most of a typical 10-K. HET-ESGFormer combines hierarchical long-document encoding, heterogeneity-aware sparse expert routing conditioned on industry sector and firm size, and a dual-channel explanation layer subject to faithfulness verification. The framework is evaluated on 3,182 U.S.-listed firms over 2015 to 2024 using 10-K filings, sustainability reports, earnings call transcripts, and ESG-tagged news. Against nine baselines spanning econometric, dictionary-based, contextual encoder, sparse-attention, and time-series approaches, HET-ESGFormer reduces return RMSE from 0.0417 to 0.0389 and QLIKE from 0.148 to 0.128, with Diebold-Mariano tests rejecting equal predictive accuracy against every baseline after correction for multiple comparisons. The text channel's marginal contribution to downside risk prediction is materially larger than its contribution to return prediction, widening at longer forecast horizons, indicating that ESG narratives carry more information about risk than about expected return. Ablations reveal a decoupling between predictive skill and explanation faithfulness: removing the consistency regularizer barely affects accuracy but sharply degrades explanation quality. The dual-channel explanation improves ERASER comprehensiveness by 50% over SHAP applied to XGBoost, and human raters significantly prefer the framework's rationales over SHAP-based rationales on trustworthiness. Decile-sorted long-short portfolios deliver a post-cost Sharpe ratio of 1.31 against 0.74 and 0.62 for portfolios built o

latest.title: Socio-Cultural Dynamics and Organizational Performance of Indigenous Printing Enterprises in Rivers State, Nigeria
latest.venue: International Journal of Advanced Academic Research
latest.abstract: This empirical study investigated the influence of socio-cultural dynamics on the organizational performance of indigenous printing enterprises in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, Nigeria. Grounded in Hofstede's Cultural Dimensions Theory and Weber's Socio-Cultural Economic Theory, the study evaluated four specific socio-cultural variables: early skill inculcation, risk-taking orientation, religious beliefs, and professional network relationships, assessing their impact on enterprise performance measured by market share growth and customer retention. A survey design was employed with a structured questionnaire administered to owner-managers across 140 registered printing firms in Port Harcourt. Statistical analyses, including descriptive mean indices, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression, were performed on 96 validated responses. Results demonstrated that early skill inculcation (r = 0.745, p < 0.05) and professional networking (r = 0.832, p < 0.05) had strong positive relationships with enterprise market growth. Religious inclination significantly shaped work ethics, though it posed operational rigidity regarding working days. The study concluded that socio-cultural capital is a critical determinant of business success in indigenous African settings and recommended structured apprenticeship formalization and gender diversity in printing entrepreneurship.

latest.title: The Influence of Motivation, Welfare, and Work Morale on Employee Performance at PT. Soci Mas
latest.abstract: Employee performance is essential to organizational effectiveness, yet initial observations at PT. Soci Mas revealed delays in task completion, limited initiative, and concerns about employee welfare and work morale. This study examines the relationships of motivation, employee welfare, and work morale with employee performance. A quantitative associative design was applied to all 83 permanent employees using total sampling. Questionnaire data, supported by interviews, observations, and documentation, were analyzed using multiple linear regression in SPSS. Motivation (β = 0.319; t = 3.633; p < .001), employee welfare (β = 0.428; t = 4.336; p < .001), and work morale (β = 0.227; t = 2.539; p = .013) each showed a positive, statistically significant association with employee performance. Together, the predictors were significant (F = 164.224; p < .001) and explained 86.2% of the variance in performance (R² = 0.862). Employee welfare had the largest standardized coefficient. These results underscore the relevance of all three factors to human resource management at PT. Soci Mas.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Beyond Income: Social Drivers of Domestic Tourism Participation Among Public Sector Workers in the Sekondi-Takoradi Metropolis, Ghana
latest.abstract: This study investigated the social drivers influencing domestic tourism participation among public sector workers in the Sekondi-Takoradi Metropolis, Ghana, addressing a gap in the literature that has largely explained participation through economic and motivational lenses while overlooking family, peer, and community influences on travel decisions. Adopting a quantitative, descriptive cross-sectional survey design, the study targeted public sector workers drawn from institutions such as the Metropolitan Assembly and other government ministries, departments, and agencies. Because no consolidated register of this population existed, Cochran's formula for an unknown population determined a sample size of 303, with respondents selected through convenience sampling. Of 366 questionnaires distributed in person, 303 were retrieved and analysed, a response rate of approximately 82.8 percent. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and exploratory factor analysis with varimax rotation. A Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin value of 0.554 and a significant Bartlett's test confirmed the data's suitability for factor analysis, which extracted six reliable dimensions: Interpersonal and Family Motivators, Social Bonds, Socio-Cultural Influence, Family Influence on Travel Decisions, Peer Motivation and Family Leisure Priorities, and Social Engagement. Family encouragement, peer recommendations, social obligations such as funerals and weddings, and the belief that travel strengthens social relationships emerged as the strongest motivators, while household responsibilities and aged family members were notable constraints. These findings confirm that domestic tourism participation among public sector workers is a socially negotiated experience rather than a purely economic one. The study recomme

latest.title: The Influence of Business Risk, Financial Performance, and Debt Policy on Firm Value
latest.abstract: Firm value reflects management performance and investor confidence, which can be influenced by business risk, financial performance, and debt policy. This study aims to analyze the effect of business risk, financial performance, and debt policy on firm value in Consumer Non-Cyclicals sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2019–2024 period. A quantitative approach was employed using purposive sampling, yielding 396 observations from 66 companies. Data analysis was performed using panel data regression with the Fixed Effect Model via EViews 13. The results indicate that business risk, financial performance, and debt policy simultaneously have a significant effect on firm value. Partially, business risk proxied by Degree of Operating Leverage (DOL) has no significant effect on firm value. Conversely, financial performance proxied by Return on Assets (ROA) has a positive and significant effect on firm value, while debt policy proxied by Debt to Asset Ratio (DAR) shows no significant effect. This study concludes that profitability is a primary factor considered by investors in enhancing firm value.

latest.title: The Law of Wanting
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: The Law of Wanting introduces an original five-element conceptual framework examining the relationship between desire, learned expectations, acceptance, observable outcomes, and consciously perceived ideal reality. The framework proposes that intense wanting can influence what individuals recognize as fulfillment, while distinguishing observable circumstances from an individual’s subjective experience of an ideal life. The paper presents definitions, illustrative thought experiments, conceptual paradoxes, and opportunities for further investigation. This work is an exploratory philosophical proposal, not an experimentally established scientific law or peer-reviewed empirical study.

latest.title: Digital Technology Adoption and Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Risk Management: Evidence from West Java, Indonesia
latest.venue: INTENSIF Jurnal Ilmiah Penelitian dan Penerapan Teknologi Sistem Informasi
latest.abstract: Background: The increasing complexity of pharmaceutical supply chains, along with regulatory pressure and operational disruptions, has created an urgent need for effective supply chain risk management. Digital technology adoption is considered essential for improving operational resilience and continuity. Objective: The purpose of this research is to analyses the effect of digital technology adoption on supply chain risk management performance in pharmaceutical companies in West Java Province, Indonesia. Methods: This study used a quantitative approach with Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). Data were collected through structured questionnaires distributed to managers in pharmaceutical manufacturing, distribution, and logistics companies. A total of 100 valid responses were analyzed to evaluate the relationships among technological infrastructure, digital system utilization, and supply chain risk management dimensions. Results: The findings show that technological infrastructure significantly influences digital system utilization (β = 0.712; p < 0.001), while digital system utilization positively affects supply chain risk management performance (β = 0.684; p < 0.001). The model produced an R² value of 0.63, indicating substantial explanatory power. In addition, digital technology adoption improved operational efficiency, delivery reliability, and supply chain resilience. Conclusion: This research confirms that digital technology adoption plays a significant role in strengthening supply chain risk management and supporting sustainable operational performance in the pharmaceutical industry.

latest.title: Consciousness and anomalous aerial phenomena: Causal and empirical requirements for interpreting UAP
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Unidentified anomalous phenomena encompass reports of hovering, unusual motion, unclear propulsion and apparent disappearance or reappearance. These features need not share one cause. This perspective examines possible connections among local movement, apparent transfer and consciousness-associated contact, building on two earlier Observer preprints. Standard local-operation and ground-state identities constrain controllable spacelike influence and cyclic work extraction under stated assumptions. A conditional energy balance clarifies resource accounting. The paper distinguishes first detection from physical arrival, unresolved support or propulsion from gravity modification, and subjective contact experiences from independently recorded external events. CE5 practices and a newly funded prospective field study identify a related research question without establishing conscious control. The contribution is a set of causal, resource and observational requirements. Personal experiences motivate the inquiry but are not used as empirical evidence for its physical claims. No consciousness coupling, gravity modification, nonhuman-agent attribution or universal human capability is demonstrated. No new empirical dataset is presented. This is an author preprint with disclosed AI assistance and a scoped preparatory technical review; it is not journal peer review.

latest.title: Maqasid al-Sharia-based distribution of Islamic social funds: Evidence from Baitul al-Qur'an Gontor
latest.venue: Review of Islamic Social Finance and Entrepreneurship
latest.abstract: Purpose – This study explores how the Baitul al-Qur'an Gontor Social Fund Institution (Lembaga Dana Sosial Baitul Quran, LDSBQ) operationalizes maqasid al-Sharia principles in the governance and distribution of Islamic social funds to enhance community welfare.Methodology – Employing a qualitative single-case study, data were collected in July and August 2025 through semi-structured interviews with the LDSBQ director, 3 operational staff, and 10 program beneficiaries. Triangulated with non-participant observations and document analysis, the data were analyzed using thematic coding.Findings – LDSBQ integrates the five dimensions of maqasid al-Sharia not merely as a descriptive program matrix (e.g., da'wah for al-dīn, healthy smile for al-nafs), but as a holistic welfare creation mechanism. The analysis demonstrates how this maqasid-driven allocation moves beneficiaries from basic survival towards bounded economic empowerment. It also uncovers implementation challenges, particularly monitoring constraints in remote areas and limited long-term capital for micro-enterprises.Implications – The findings offer Islamic philanthropic institutions an illustrative, empirically grounded pathway to shift from ad-hoc charity to structured community empowerment by anchoring resource allocation directly in maqasid objectives. Originality – Moving beyond theoretical discussions, this study contributes to the Islamic social finance literature by empirically detailing the operational mechanisms, beneficiary impacts, and grassroots implementation challenges of a localized maqasid-based institutional framework.

latest.title: The Impact of Board Composition on Sustainability Report Readability
latest.venue: Journal of Strategic Innovation and Sustainability
latest.abstract: This study examines whether and how board composition influences the readability of corporate sustainability reports. Using a sample of 1,334 firm-year observations from S&P 500 companies between 2016 and 2023, we investigate the relationship between board characteristics and report readability while controlling for firm-specific factors. Contrary to conventional wisdom, we find no statistically significant evidence that board-level characteristics, including gender diversity and board size, directly influence sustainability report readability. Our findings suggest that report readability is more likely influenced by operational-level factors than board-level governance structures. These results contribute to the literature on corporate governance and sustainability reporting by challenging existing assumptions about the direct role of board composition in determining reporting quality. Our study has important implications for understanding the mechanisms through which organizational governance affects sustainability disclosure practices.

latest.title: AZƏRBAYCAN PAMBIĞININ BEYNƏLXALQ BAZARLARDA RƏQABƏT QABİLİYYƏTİNİN YÜKSƏLDİLMƏSİ İSTİQAMƏTLƏRİ
latest.abstract: XÜLASƏMəqalədə Azərbaycan pambığının beynəlxalq bazarlarda rəqabət qabiliyyətinin artırılması problemləri və onların həlli istiqamətləri araşdırılmışdır.Müasir şəraitdə qlobal kənd təsərrüfatı bazarlarında rəqabətin güclənməsi pambıq istehsalçısı olan ölkələr qarşısında yeni çağırışlar formalaşdırır.Tədqiqat çərçivəsində Azərbaycan pambıqçılığının mövcud vəziyyəti təhlil edilmiş, beynəlxalq bazarlarda rəqabət üstünlüklərinin formalaşmasına təsir edən amillər müəyyən edilmişdir.Eyni zamanda pambıq məhsullarının keyfiyyət göstəricilərinin yaxşılaşdırılması, emal sənayesinin inkişafı, logistika infrastrukturunun təkmilləşdirilməsi və beynəlxalq standartların tətbiqi istiqamətində təkliflər hazırlanmışdır.Araşdırmanın nəticələri göstərir ki, pambıq məhsullarının rəqabət qabiliyyətinin yüksəldilməsi qeyri-neft ixracının genişlənməsinə, regionların sosial-iqtisadi inkişafına və ölkənin valyuta gəlirlərinin artmasına əhəmiyyətli töhfə verə bilər. Açar sözlər:

latest.title: Membentuk Keputusan Pembelian Konsumen: Sinergi Digital Entrepreneurship, Persepsi Harga dan Kualitas Produk Studi Pada Konsumen Jatinangor House Kota Bogor
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze and determine 1) The Influence of Digital Entrepreneurship on Purchase Decisions, 2) The Influence of Price Perception on Purchase Decisions, 3) The Influence of Product Quality on Purchase Decisions of Jatinangor House consumens in Bogor City. The development of a competitive culinary industry in the digital economy era requires business actors to integrate technology and maintain product value alignment in order to influence consumer behavior. The type of research used is a quantitative approach with a survey method. Primary data collection was conducted through the distribution of structured questionnaires with a Likert scale to 180 respondents selected using non-probability sampling technique with a purposive sampling approach, which is a sampling technique based on certain criteria established by the researcher. The criteria for respondents are Jatinangor House consumens in Bogor City who have made a product purchase. The data analysis method used in this research is Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) through the Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) analysis tool with the assistance of SmartPLS 4.0 software. The results of hypothesis testing show that: 1) Digital Entrepreneurship has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Decisions with a t-statistic value of 3.021 and a p-value of 0.003, 2) Price Perception has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Decisions with a t-statistic value of 1.988 and a p-value of 0.047, and finally 3) Product Quality has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Decisions with a t-statistic value of 6.493 and a p-value of 0.000 The results of this study show that the variables of Digital Entrepreneurship, Price Perception, and Product Quality have a positive and significant influence on the Purc

latest.title: Minimum-Bill Thresholds in Promotional Milk Coupon Subscriptions: A Review of Consumer Redemption, Basket Value, and Association Rule Mining
latest.abstract: A minimum-bill coupon requires a shopper to reach a specified transaction value before receiving the offer. This paper examines a milk coupon subscription in which the qualifying minimum bill is raised from Rs 99 to Rs 149, an increase of about 50.5%. Through a focused narrative review of studies on coupon redemption, sales promotions, conditional (minimum-spend) promotions and association rule mining in retail, it argues that the higher threshold may encourage some customers to add products to qualify while discouraging redemption among those whose usual baskets fall below the new threshold, so that the net effect on sales and profitability cannot be inferred from the threshold alone. The paper proposes a conceptual framework, five research questions and four hypotheses, and a methodology for future empirical work combining pre-post or comparison-group analysis of redemption and transaction value with Apriori-based market basket analysis, together with a set of evaluation metrics.

latest.title: The Impact of the Digital Economy on the High-Quality Development of Foreign Trade: Evidence from City-Level Panel Data in Anhui Province
latest.abstract: The digital economy is reshaping global trade and creating new opportunities for the high-quality development of foreign trade.Taking the prefecture-level cities of Anhui Province during 2010–2023 as the empirical sample,this paper constructs a composite index of digital economy development along four dimensions—digital infrastructure,digital industrialisation,the digitalisation of industry,and digital talent—and an index of the high-quality development of foreign trade covering foreign trade volume,foreign trade structure and foreign trade competitiveness, both measured using the entropy weight method.A two-way fixed effects model is estimated to examine the effect of the digital economy on the high-quality development of foreign trade in Anhui.The results show that the digital economy exerts a significantly positive promoting effect on the high-quality development of foreign trade in the province,and that this effect displays pronounced regional and temporal heterogeneity. The findings carry practical implications for how Chinese provinces can seize the opportunities of the digital era to advance the high-quality development of foreign trade.

latest.title: The Effect of Company Size, Asset Management, and Capital Structure on Financial Performance of Palm Oil Plantation Companies Listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2021-2025 Period
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the partial and simultaneous effects of Firm Size (FS), Total Asset Turnover (TATO), and Debt to Equity Ratio (DER) on financial performance, measured by Return on Equity (ROE), in palm oil plantation companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2021–2025 period. This research employs a quantitative causal-associative design using secondary data obtained from companies' annual financial reports. The sample was selected using purposive sampling, consisting of 20 companies with a total of 100 panel data observations. Data analysis was conducted using panel data regression with the Fixed Effect Model (FEM) and White cross-section robust standard errors to address potential heteroscedasticity. The analysis also included classical assumption testing, the coefficient of determination, and hypothesis testing through partial (t-test) and simultaneous (F-test) tests. The results indicate that Firm Size has no significant effect on ROE (p = 0.6166), whereas TATO (p = 0.0005) and DER (p < 0.001) have positive and significant effects on ROE. Simultaneously, Firm Size, TATO, and DER significantly influence ROE (F-statistic = 30.564; p < 0.001). Furthermore, the Adjusted R-squared value of 0.8679 indicates that 86.78% of the variation in ROE can be explained by the three independent variables, while the remaining 13.22% is explained by other factors outside the research model.

hot.title: Trust in scientists and their role in society across 68 countries
hot.abstract: Science is crucial for evidence-based decision-making. Public trust in scientists can help decision makers act on the basis of the best available evidence, especially during crises. However, in recent years the epistemic authority of science has been challenged, causing concerns about low public trust in scientists. We interrogated these concerns with a preregistered 68-country survey of 71,922 respondents and found that in most countries, most people trust scientists and agree that scientists should engage more in society and policymaking. We found variations between and within countries, which we explain with individual- and country-level variables, including political orientation. While there is no widespread lack of trust in scientists, we cannot discount the concern that lack of trust in scientists by even a small minority may affect considerations of scientific evidence in policymaking. These findings have implications for scientists and policymakers seeking to maintain and increase trust in scientists.

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Abstract Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence and Its Role in Shaping Organizational Work Practices and Culture
hot.abstract: The advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is profoundly transforming organizational landscapes, significantly influencing work practices and triggering cultural shifts. This study explores the role of AI in reshaping organizational work practices and examines the resulting cultural transformation. Through a systematic literature review, this study synthesizes existing research to provide a comprehensive understanding of AI’s impact on organizational landscapes. A systematic literature review was conducted, analyzing peer-reviewed articles, books, and conference papers to identify key themes related to AI-driven changes in work practices, including automation, decision making, and employee roles. It also explores how these changes influence organizational culture, particularly shifts toward innovation, agility, and continuous learning, alongside challenges like resistance to change and ethical concerns. While AI adoption promises benefits such as enhanced efficiency, productivity, and innovation, it also presents significant challenges related to cultural alignment, employee resistance, ethical concerns, and leadership communication. Effective leadership, transparent communication, and investments in skills development emerge as pivotal strategies for overcoming these obstacles and ensuring successful AI implementation. The findings offer insights into the complex interplay between AI adoption and cultural transformation, highlighting gaps in the current research and suggesting directions for future studies. This study serves as a valuable resource for academics and practitioners seeking to understand the broader implications of AI on organizational structures and culture.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The evolving field of digital mental health: current evidence and implementation issues for smartphone apps, generative artificial intelligence, and virtual reality
hot.abstract: The expanding domain of digital mental health is transitioning beyond traditional telehealth to incorporate smartphone apps, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence, including large language models. While industry setbacks and methodological critiques have highlighted gaps in evidence and challenges in scaling these technologies, emerging solutions rooted in co-design, rigorous evaluation, and implementation science offer promising pathways forward. This paper underscores the dual necessity of advancing the scientific foundations of digital mental health and increasing its real-world applicability through five themes. First, we discuss recent technological advances in digital phenotyping, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence. Progress in this latter area, specifically designed to create new outputs such as conversations and images, holds unique potential for the mental health field. Given the spread of smartphone apps, we then evaluate the evidence supporting their utility across various mental health contexts, including well-being, depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, eating disorders, and substance use disorders. This broad view of the field highlights the need for a new generation of more rigorous, placebo-controlled, and real-world studies. We subsequently explore engagement challenges that hamper all digital mental health tools, and propose solutions, including human support, digital navigators, just-in-time adaptive interventions, and personalized approaches. We then analyze implementation issues, emphasizing clinician engagement, service integration, and scalable delivery models. hot.title: Job demands-resources and conservation of resources theories: How do they help to explain employee well-being and future job design?
hot.abstract: This paper examines the Conservation of Resources (COR) theory and the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) theory to understand and predict employee well-being and performance. COR theory suggests that individuals aim to acquire, protect, and maximize resources to reduce psychological distress and prevent burnout. JD-R theory posits that balancing job demands and resources affects employee well-being, behaviors, and performance. By exploring these theories together, the paper offers insights into supporting the workforce amid challenges like remote work and technological advancements. It highlights shared features and differences between the theories, unresolved issues, and research opportunities, such as operationalizing and testing COR theory and differentiating job demands and resources in JD-R theory. The paper concludes with predictions about future job design, emphasizing the need to balance job demands and resources to support employee well-being and performance, contributing to the literature by challenging and refining these theories.

hot.title: The impact of artificial intelligence on organizational performance: The mediating role of employee productivity
hot.venue: Journal of Open Innovation Technology Market and Complexity
hot.abstract: The adoption of Artificial intelligence (AI) technology in the workplace is becoming more common, with several research highlighting both its positive and adverse influence on employee productivity (EP) and organizational performance (OP). Furthermore, there is a scarcity of research focused on the mediator role of EP in the nexus between AI and OP. This ambiguity underscores the need for a comprehensive understanding of how AI interacts with EP and OP within specific organizational contexts, such as Ethio Telecom. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the impact of AI on OP with a mediating role of EP. Quantitative data was collected through an online survey using Kobo Toolbox from 172 purposively selected employees. AI was modeled as third-order formative construct, while EP and OP were first-order reflective constructs. The variables were measured using validated multi-item questionnaires with a 7-point Likert scale. The association between these variables was investigated with PLS-SEM in SMART PLS 4.1.03. The results showed that there were positive and significant relationships between AI and EP, AI and OP, EP and OP, and AI on OP through EP. Furthermore, EP served as a partial mediator between OP and AI. These findings are consistent with previous studies and theories, such as the resource-based view and human capital theories. The results suggest that organizations can dramatically improve performance in the digital age by implementing AI and creating a work environment that encourages productivity.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer

hot.title: Building trust in sustainable brands: Revisiting perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image
hot.abstract: This study revisits the key variables that build brand trust in consumers, addressing a critical issue for building lasting relationships between brands and consumers. Through a conceptual model, we examine how perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image influence consumer trust. The research is based on a sample of 1280 Spanish consumers over the age of 18, who responded to a questionnaire designed with previously validated scales. The PLS-SEM technique was used to validate the hypotheses and the proposed model. The findings reveal that perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image have a positive and significant effect on consumer trust. In particular, it was found that customer service directly influences customer satisfaction, which in turn reinforces brand trust. Additionally, the brand's communication strategy shows a significant positive relationship with brand image. Finally, customer satisfaction is identified as a mediating variable in the relationship between customer service and trust, indicating that a positive experience with customer service is fundamental for consolidating brand trust. This study contributes to enhancing the understanding of the factors that promote brand trust and offers practical implications for the development of effective marketing and brand management strategies. These insights can be especially relevant for sustainable brands, as the identified factors—perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image—are also critical in fostering trust in brands that prioritize sustainability. Incorporating sustainable practices into these areas may further strengthen consumer trust and loyalty toward sustainable brands.

hot.title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
hot.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
hot.abstract: People increasingly use videos on the Web for learning, be it for daily tasks in formal or informal educational settings. To enhance this type of learning, scientists are continuously conducting experiments, proposing guidelines, analyzing data, and researching artificial intelligence methods for tool development. In this comprehensive review, we analyze 257 articles (using PRISMA guidelines) on video-based learning from a technological perspective for the period from 2016 to 2021. One of the aims is to identify video characteristics that support learning as explored by previous research. Based on our analysis, we suggest a taxonomy that organizes the video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: (1) audio features, (2) visual features, (3) textual features, (4) instructor behavior, (5) learners’ activities (play, pause, etc.), (6) interactive features (quizzes, etc.), (7) production style, and (8) instructional design. Also, we identify four representative methodological approaches: (1) tool support of video-based learning, (2) controlled experiments, (3) data analysis studies, and (4) design guidelines for learning videos. We find that the most explored characteristics are textual features followed by visual features, learners’ activities, and interactive features. Tools that aid learning through videos frequently utilize text from transcripts, video frames, and images. The learner’s activity is heavily explored through log files in data analysis studies, and interactive features are frequently scrutinized in controlled experiments. As further contributions, we contrast research findings on how video characteristics affect learning effectiveness, report on tasks and technologies used to develop tools, and summarize design guideline trends to prod

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
