hot.title: The impacts of companion AI on human relationships: risks, benefits, and design considerations
hot.abstract: AI applications intended for companionship have increased in both availability and capabilities in recent years, alongside a spike in loneliness (Johnson 2023 ; Murthy 2023 ). According to a 2024 analysis by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, companion AI makes up 16 of the top 100 AI apps based on web traffic and monthly active users (Moore 2024 ). Moreover, today’s AI applications have a greater command of human language, an increasing capacity for storing memories, and more varied modalities to support an increasing diversity of experiences, a known driver in the development and deepening of emotional relationships (Skjuve et al. 2022 ).

hot.title: Organizational culture, digital transformation, and product innovation
hot.abstract: This research fills a knowledge gap by introducing a new conceptualization of digital transformation through a multidimensional digital transforming capability. It further examines the influence of four cultural types on this capability and its subsequent impact on product innovation . Empirical findings reveal that adhocracy, followed in descending order of influence by clan, market, and hierarchy cultures, is positively related to digital transforming capability, which in turn is positively related to product innovation in terms of new product newness, meaningfulness, and performance. Additionally, new product newness and meaningfulness each positively mediate the effect of digital transforming capability on new product performance.

hot.title: Supply Chain Resilience: A Critical Review of Risk Mitigation, Robust Optimisation, and Technological Solutions and Future Research Directions
hot.venue: Global Journal of Flexible Systems Management
hot.abstract: Abstract This study systematically evaluates the literature of supply chain resilience by integrating bibliometric and network analysis techniques. This analysis is conducted following the dynamic capability, as a theoretical lens, to understand and analyse supply chain resilience. We extracted and curated 294 peer‐reviewed articles from leading academic databases, Web of Science and Scopus, covering the period from January 2000 to 2024. We applied two complementary network analysis methods, a keyword co‐occurrence network (KCON) to analyse the frequency and interrelationships among key terms, and a research focus parallelship network (RFPN) to map the connectivity among research streams. These analytical approaches revealed three distinct research clusters, optimisation for supply chain resilience, technology adoption for supply chain resilience, and resilience strategies against disruptions and risk management. By linking emerging trends in digital transformation with traditional risk management practices, this study offers a new perspective for both academic inquiry and managerial practice. Practically, integrating digital technologies, especially digital twin and machine learning, into risk management processes offers a strategic roadmap for real-time monitoring and decision-making in supply chain resilience. Furthermore, this study identifies significant research gaps, including an exploration of micro‐level dynamics within organisations, and the development of advanced simulation techniques and robust approaches to manage uncertainties.

hot.title: Generative AI and its Transformative Value for Digital Platforms
hot.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) represents a watershed moment in the evolution of digital platforms. The capabilities of this AI technology go beyond traditional AI systems, enabling the autonomous generation of novel outcomes with significant implications for platform value creation, architecture, governance, and stakeholder interactions. We develop an integrative conceptual framework that identifies four key mechanisms through which GenAI transforms digital platforms: intelligent automation, democratization, hyper-personalization, and collaborative innovation. Through intelligent automation, GenAI transforms boundary resources from passive interfaces into active, intelligent mediators of value creation. Democratization systematically lowers barriers to platform participation. Hyper-personalization enables dynamic, individual-level adaptation of platform content. Collaborative innovation transforms platform innovation by making GenAI an active participant in human-AI value co-creation. We use this framework to situate the papers in the special issue and develop a research agenda that explores the transformative impact of GenAI on platform stakeholder relationships.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption for Sustainable Growth in SMEs : An Extended Dynamic Capability Framework
hot.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT The adoption of Artificial Intelligence is transforming enterprises worldwide, influencing various aspects of business operations and affecting all dimensions of the triple bottom line. Companies ready to leverage the potential of this technology can significantly improve their performance. Therefore, it is crucial to understand the relationship between internal capabilities and contextual factors on one hand, and Artificial Intelligence adoption and its impact on performance on the other. Within this research framework, this study introduces an extended dynamic capability framework to analyze the interplay between internal factors, Artificial Intelligence adoption, and companies performance. The proposed model is tested using Partial Least Squares—Structural Equation Modeling on survey data from 210 Italian innovative startups. The findings indicate that companies with well‐developed dynamic capabilities, enabling them to adapt more effectively to environmental changes, are also better equipped to adopt Artificial Intelligence, leading to positive social, economic, and environmental performance.

hot.title: Lower Artificial Intelligence Literacy Predicts Greater AI Receptivity
hot.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms society, understanding factors that influence AI receptivity is increasingly important. The current research investigates which types of consumers have greater AI receptivity. Contrary to expectations revealed in four surveys, cross-country data and six additional studies find that people with lower AI literacy are typically more receptive to AI. This lower literacy–greater receptivity link is not explained by differences in perceptions of AI's capability, ethicality, or feared impact on humanity. Instead, this link occurs because people with lower AI literacy are more likely to perceive AI as magical and experience feelings of awe in the face of AI's execution of tasks that seem to require uniquely human attributes. In line with this theorizing, the lower literacy–higher receptivity link is mediated by perceptions of AI as magical and is moderated among tasks not assumed to require distinctly human attributes. These findings suggest that companies may benefit from shifting their marketing efforts and product development toward consumers with lower AI literacy. In addition, efforts to demystify AI may inadvertently reduce its appeal.

hot.title: Can Generative AI Chatbots Emulate Human Connection? A Relationship Science Perspective
hot.abstract: The development of generative artificial intelligence capable of sustaining complex conversations has created a burgeoning market for companion chatbots promising social and emotional connection. The appeal of these products raises questions about whether chatbots can fulfill the functions of close relationships. Proponents argue that relationships with chatbots can be as meaningful as relationships between humans, whereas critics argue they are a dangerous distraction from genuine connections. This analysis applies theoretical tools from more than 50 years of research on close relationships to evaluate the extent to which human-chatbot interactions meet the definition of and fulfill the functions of close relationships. Interactions between humans and chatbots do possess some characteristic features of close relationships: Humans and chatbots can influence each other and engage in frequent and diverse conversations over time. Chatbots can be responsive in ways humans perceive as supportive, generating feelings of connection and opportunities for growth. Yet because chatbots make only superficial requests of their users, relationships with them cannot provide the benefits of negotiating with and sacrificing for a partner and may reinforce undesirable behaviors. Research that attends to the characteristics of users, chatbots, and their interactions will be crucial for identifying for whom these relationships will be beneficial or harmful.

hot.title: Unveiling triple bottom line's influence on business performance
hot.abstract: Addressing environmental, social, and economic challenges has become a pressing global priority. The Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework offers a holistic approach for evaluating corporate performance by integrating economic, environmental, and social perspectives. Despite its increasing adoption in both managerial and academic research, there remains a significant gap in understanding how the TBL framework influences business performance. To address this, the study conducts a bibliometric review of 207 publications from the Web of Science database. The review highlights the multifaceted impact of practices linked to the TBL dimensions on business performance while introducing the TBL Influence on Business Performance model. This model provides valuable insights into how businesses can effectively apply TBL principles to address socio-environmental challenges, foster innovation, and achieve sustained long-term performance. The findings contribute valuable theoretical and practical insights into how organizations can utilize TBL principles to strengthen resilience, innovation, and performance in the face of global socio-environmental challenges.

hot.title: The past, present, and future of sustainability marketing: How did we get here and where might we go?
hot.abstract: The ever-increasing concerns about global sustainability have sparked intense debates and actions across various sectors, with marketing playing a pivotal role in influencing both the problem and potential solutions. This article maps the historical trajectory of sustainability marketing, analyzes current trends, and explores future directions to enhance sustainability within marketing practice. We show that sustainability marketing has historically centered on resource conservation and green marketing , but in recent years its scope has expanded to encompass a broader range of topics. These include the circular economy , anti-consumption, regulatory frameworks, innovation, carbon emissions , as well as the social and ethical considerations inherent in sustainability marketing. We propose three main areas within which sustainability marketing might expand in the future: system-driven changes, business-driven changes, and consumer-driven changes. Our analysis aims to deepen the understanding of sustainability marketing and inspire marketers to explore questions and solutions that will contribute to a sustainable future.

hot.title: Artificial intelligence technologies and entrepreneurship: a hybrid literature review
hot.abstract: The disruptive potential of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies involves creating new entrepreneurial opportunities and reshaping the entrepreneurial process. The impact of AI technologies on entrepreneurial activity is also reflected in an explosive level of research interest, leading to the fragmentation of existing studies. This phenomenon makes generating a comprehensive and systematic overview challenging. This paper reviews the existing research on the application of AI-based technologies in entrepreneurial practice. Specifically, it conducts a hybrid literature review, analyzing 345 articles from peer-reviewed journals. It identifies the main contributions to the field; the conceptual, social, and intellectual structures; and the leading themes addressed to date. Despite growing interest in the field, this study concludes that most academic research on the subject has been superficial. This study proposes future lines of research based on the antecedents, decisions, and outcomes (ADO) and the theories, contexts, and methods (TCM) frameworks.

hot.title: What you see is not what you get: ESG scores and greenwashing risk
hot.abstract: This paper shows that ESG scores capture a company’s greenwashing behavior. Greenwashing accusations are most prevalent among large companies with high ESG scores. We empirically employ a novel theoretical model that distinguishes between the communication of a company’s environmental efforts (apparent environmental performance) and its actual environmental impact (real environmental performance). The correlation of the apparent (real) environmental performance with ESG scores is significantly positive (negative). Therefore, ESG scores are unsuitable for measuring real environmental impact. Thus, investors focusing on high ESG-rated companies may unknowingly increase their greenwashing risk exposure, and academics may use misleading information to assess greenwashing risk. • ESG scores are positively correlated with greenwashing cases. • ESG scores mainly measure the apparent rather than the real environmental performance. • Higher analyst coverage limits the exaggeration of apparent environmental performance.

hot.title: Understanding Customer Responses to AI-Driven Personalized Journeys: Impacts on the Customer Experience
hot.abstract: Within advertising, the customer journey concept helps explain how customer perceptions and behaviors evolve through seller–customer interactions. The concept has developed to reflect omni-channel marketing but neglects the emergence of algorithmically personalized advertisements. This study therefore explores impacts upon customer experiences of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven recommendations and personalized advertisements by analyzing customer perceptions of tensions between the personalization and customer empowerment inherent within AI-driven advertising. By combining semi-structured phenomenological interviews with Customer Journey Mapping, we capture experiences and behaviors across multiple touchpoints. Our findings show how technological limitations of AI mediate brand–customer relationships and influence customer behaviors. The study contributes theoretically by critically contextualizing AI-driven advertising within broader ethical debates, emphasizing practitioners’ responsibilities to combine technological advancements with consumer autonomy.

hot.title: Are lonely youngsters turning to chatbots for companionship? The relationship between chatbot usage and social connectedness in Danish high-school students
hot.abstract: Are lonely youngsters turning to chatbots to fill their social needs? The present research contributes to the ongoing scientific endeavors to understand the adoption of chatbots as social companions. Specifically, we examined how many Danish high-school students engage in friend-like conversations with chatbots, why they engage in such conversations, and whether this trend is associated with the sense of social connectedness (operationalized as loneliness and perceived social support). In pursuing this goal, a preregistered mixed-methods cross-sectional survey study was carried out. A total sample of 1599 students from 15 Danish high schools was collected. In total, 234 students (14.6%) responded that they engage in friend-like conversations with chatbots. Qualitative thematic analyses of free-text responses revealed two dominant ways of engaging with chatbots: utilitarian conversations (n = 174) and social-supportive conversations (n = 39). A major finding was that social-supportive chatbot users reported significantly more loneliness than non-chatbot users (d = 0.53) and utilitarian chatbot users (d = 0.52). Furthermore, social-supportive chatbot users also reported significantly lower perceived social support than non-chatbot users (d = -0.46). Analyses also showed significant associations between higher loneliness and less perceived social support and various situational triggers for initiating conversations with chatbots, including bad mood, a need for self-disclosure, and a sense of loneliness, but not with a sense of friendship to the chatbot as a trigger of chatbot interactions. These findings suggest a trend among some socially disconnected Danish high-school students toward using chatbots to cope with negative emotions.

hot.title: Greenwashing and market value of firms: An empirical study
hot.abstract: In the modern business environment, green or sustainable claims mushroom, with companies striving to improve their green practices for climate change and sustainability. However, with increasing expectations of sustainable performance, companies encounter mounting financial pressure, which may create opportunities to exploit sustainable efforts to their advantage. Many companies assert environmental-friendly measures to mask their true activities, the phenomenon, known as greenwashing, fuels public scepticism about the sincerity of their green message. This study employs an event study methodology to explore how the stock market values greenwashing announcements through 121 worldwide greenwashing announcements since the 2015 Paris Agreement. Our findings reveal that a modest negative association between greenwashing announcements and stock market reactions. Notably, the market reaction to greenwashing announcements is more negative for firms with greater environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance than for weak ESG performance. The study further finds that there are more negative reactions to announcements providing solid evidence of greenwashing. The companies operating in the manufacturing industry suffer more market value losses than those operating in the service industry. Compared with other stock markets, the Asia-Pacific market experiences negative reactions to greenwashing. This study contributes to the signalling theory and advances the literature on corporate sustainable practices by offering empirical insights within a global context.

hot.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Personalizing Social Media Marketing Strategies for Enhanced Customer Experience
hot.abstract: This paper explores the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in personalizing social media marketing strategies and its impact on customer experience, with a focus on consumers within the MENA region. Using data collected from an online questionnaire completed by 893 individuals, the study confirms that AI significantly enhances social media marketing by offering personalized content, optimizing influencer selection, and enabling real-time consumer interaction. These capabilities not only increase customer awareness but also improve user experience and purchase intentions. Key AI tools such as influencer marketing, content optimization, and customization are effective in capturing consumer attention, although further research is necessary to deepen understanding. By examining AI's ability to analyze vast datasets and support targeted marketing efforts, the study contributes to both academic and practical discourse, offering insights that businesses can use to refine their AI-driven social media strategies. Ultimately, the research aims to guide marketers through the complexities of AI deployment, ensuring its benefits are fully realized for consumers.

latest.title: The social self in sustainable luxury services: psychological ownership, identification and willingness to use
latest.abstract: Purpose Drawing on symbolic interactionism, this study aims to examine how social expressiveness influences consumers’ willingness to use sustainable luxury services (SLS). It further investigates the mediating roles of identification with SLS and utilitarian well-being, and the moderating role of psychological ownership. Design/methodology/approach The research uses a two-study design. Study 1 uses survey data from Prolific to test the hypothesized direct, mediation and moderation relationships and to assess the measurement model. Study 2 provides field-based evidence using two Facebook advertisements for a sustainable luxury hotel and click-through rate (CTR) as the behavioral outcome. Study 1 was analyzed using structural equation modeling and moderation analysis. Findings Social expressiveness is positively associated with willingness to use SLS, and this relationship is sequentially mediated by identification with SLS and utilitarian well-being. Psychological ownership significantly moderates the relationships among social expressiveness, identification, utilitarian well-being and willingness to use SLS; however, the negative interaction terms indicate attenuation rather than the hypothesized strengthening. In Study 2, the social-expressiveness advertisement generated a CTR more than 40% higher than the non-social-expressiveness advertisement. Originality/value This research extends luxury service research by showing how a socially expressive motive is translated into willingness to use SLS through identification and well-being. It also positions psychological ownership as a boundary condition in a non-ownership service context, while showing that high psychological ownership can reduce the marginal importance of other drivers of willingness. The study thereby offe

latest.title: Decision pathways in mobile-app shopping: a Throughput Model study of online consumers
latest.abstract: Purpose Mobile shopping environments increasingly rely on artificial intelligence (AI) to personalise recommendations, curate product information and support purchase decisions. Yet, existing consumer decision-making models maintain a linear, stage-based logic that fails to capture how AI-enabled interfaces compress, extend or reconfigure the pathways consumers actually follow. This study aims to use the Throughput Model (TPM) to conceptualise and empirically validate distinct algorithmic decision pathways through which perception, information search and evaluative judgement interact to shape purchase intentions in mobile-app shopping contexts. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from Gen Z consumers with recent mobile-app shopping experience. The study applies partial least squares structural equation modelling and mediation analysis to test the TPM and estimate one-step, two-step and three-step decision pathways in AI-enabled mobile commerce. Findings Perception, information search and judgement each exert significant effects within the model, with judgement emerging as the central integrative mechanism linking upstream inputs to purchase intention. These results demonstrate that AI-enabled mobile interfaces simultaneously support impulsive, efficiency-driven and deliberative decision architectures. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study provides the first empirical operationalisation of the TPM in mobile-app commerce, reconceptualising purchase decisions as coexisting algorithmic pathways rather than a single sequential route. It offers marketers a diagnostic framework for segmenting consumers by decision architecture and designing adaptive AI-enabled shopping experiences accordingly.

latest.title: Drivers of sustainable fashion purchase in India: a moderated value framework
latest.abstract: Purpose Although sustainable fashion research has extensively examined either consumer attitudes or purchase intentions, limited studies have explicitly distinguished between the cognitive foundation of attitude and the situationally driven nature of intention within the eco-fashion context. Furthermore, the interactive role of psychological traits such as altruism and mindfulness, along with economic considerations like willingness to pay a premium, in moderating the attitude–intention relationship remains underexplored, particularly in emerging markets such as India. This study aims to address these gaps by developing and empirically validating an integrated framework that captures both individual and contextual drivers of eco-fashion purchase intention. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a comprehensive mixed-methods design informed by grounded theory principles, this study explores the underlying factors that shape the phenomenon. Qualitative data from interviews and FGD enabled themes to emerge inductively, while quantitative survey data validated and extended these insights. Statistical analyses examined relationships among variables, and hypotheses were tested using SEM to ensure robustness of the conceptual model. Findings Environmental consciousness, social influence and marketing stimuli considerably shape eco-fashion attitude and purchase intention, while attitude mediates these relationships. Altruism, mindfulness and willingness to pay strengthen the relationship between attitude and purchase intention. Originality/value The study proposes a moderated value framework that explains sustainable fashion purchase more dynamically by treating altruism, mindfulness and willingness to pay as moderators in the Indian context.

latest.title: Pet insurance services adoption: how values, reasoning, and insurance literacy shape consumer intentions in an emerging market
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine pet-insurance adoption in India through behavioral reasoning theory (BRT), focusing on how openness to change and social value shape reasons for and against adoption, how these reasons influence attitude and purchase intention and whether insurance literacy strengthens the attitude–intention relationship. Design/methodology/approach A sequential mixed-methods design was used. Interviews with 17 pet owners identified the facilitators and inhibitors. Survey data from 352 respondents were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling to test the mediation and moderation effects. Demographic moderation was treated as an exploratory analysis. Findings Openness to change strengthened both reasons for and reasons against adoption, whereas social value strengthened supportive reasoning and reduced opposing reasoning. Reasons for adoption positively influenced attitude and intention, whereas reasons against adoption had negative effects. Attitude was the strongest predictor of purchase intention, and insurance literacy strengthened the attitude–intention relationship. The unexpected positive association between openness to change and reasons against adoption suggests that receptiveness to novelty may intensify scrutiny of benefits and barriers instead of uniformly increasing adoption readiness. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional sample limits the causal inference and generalizability of the findings. Future research should test the deliberative role of openness to change using longitudinal, behavioral and cross-market designs. Practical implications Insurers should address benefits and barriers, including affordability, exclusions, coverage limits and claims procedures, while using pet-insurance education

latest.title: أشهر أخطاء ومزايا قوائم الطعام (المنيو): دراسة مقارنة لعشر حالات تشخيصية في قطاع المطاعم والمشروبات
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: تتناول هذه الورقة سؤالًا عمليًا: ما الأخطاء والمزايا التي تتكرر في قوائم الطعام، وهل يجمعها نمط واحد؟ اعتمدت الدراسة على عشر حالات تشخيصية أعدّها الباحث ونُشرت في «أطلس تشخيص قوائم الطعام» (٢٠٢٦): كباب أوزي، والأكيل، وSmiley Hearts، وMIROLA Cheesecake، وتتبيلة، وع الفحم، وTrifillo Gelato، ومصراوي، وسِكّة، ونينو NENO. قُيّمت كل قائمة نوعيًا على أربعة عشر محورًا وبثلاثة مستويات، وفُرّغت التقييمات (١٤٠ تقييمًا) في مصفوفة مقارنة. تكشف النتائج «فجوة العرض والتوجيه»: تنوع المنتجات والهوية البصرية جاءا «جيد» فأعلى في الحالات العشر كلها، بينما جاء تطبيق ممارسات هندسة القائمة «يحتاج تطوير» في الحالات العشر، ووصف المنتجات وإبرازها في تسع حالات، وعرض الأسعار والبيع الإضافي وعلم نفس المستهلك في سبع حالات لكل منها. ورُصدت كثافة المعلومات أو طول القائمة صراحةً في ثماني حالات. تقترح الورقة ترتيبًا عمليًا لأولويات تطوير القوائم، وتناقش حدود الأدلة النوعية في غياب بيانات المبيعات والتكلفة. Abstract. This working paper asks which strengths and shortcomings recur across restaurant menus. It draws on ten diagnostic cases from the author's Restaurant Menu Diagnostic Atlas (2026), each rated qualitatively on fourteen dimensions (140 ratings). Results show a consistent display–guidance gap: product variety and visual identity were rated good or better in all ten cases, while application of menu-engineering practice needed development in all ten, product descriptions and item highlighting in nine, and price presentation, upselling and consumer-psychology cues in seven each. Information density was flagged explicitly in eight cases. The paper proposes practical priorities for menu redesign and discusses the limits of qualitative evidence without sales and cost data.

latest.title: Business Development Analysis of Ayam Geprek Mas Andre Lubuklinggau Based on Business Life Cycle Theory
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the development of the Ayam Geprek Mas Andre micro, small, and medium enterprise (MSME) in Lubuklinggau based on the Business Life Cycle Theory, including the marketing strategy and product innovation applied by the business. The research method used is a qualitative approach with a case study method. The subjects of this study were selected purposively, consisting of the business owner, employees, and customers of Ayam Geprek Mas Andre. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observation, and documentation. The data analysis technique used is the interactive analysis model developed by Miles, Huberman, and Saldana, which includes data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing/verification. The findings show that Ayam Geprek Mas Andre passed through the introduction/birth stage since its establishment in 2017 with pecel lele as its initial product, before developing into the growth stage (Growth Stage) after switching to ayam geprek as its main product, marked by increased consumer interest, business expansion to 13 branches, product innovation, and the use of digital marketing. The conclusion of this study is that Ayam Geprek Mas Andre is currently in the growth stage of its business life cycle, supported by product quality, affordable pricing, innovation, and adaptability to market changes, although it still faces challenges such as rising business competition, changing consumer preferences, and digital technology developments.

latest.title: Evaluating human-like chatbot interaction in customer service: integrating anthropomorphism and conversational capability
latest.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI)-based technology has driven the development of rule-based chatbots into AI-based chatbots. This development is used by various companies to use AI chatbots as the frontline of customer service. Meeting user expectations for AI chatbots requires an evaluation model to measure chatbot quality. Based on the literature, chatbot evaluation models still focus solely on technical quality, even as AI chatbots are evolving towards human-like services. This research will explore the integration of the technical dimensions of information system success with a new dimension, namely Human-Like Chatbot Interaction (HLCI) as a higher-order construct of anthropomorphism and conversational capability. This quantitative study uses an explanatory research approach. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of users of the Veronika chatbot, owned by Telkomsel, an Indonesian telecommunications company. A total of 213 respondents had data ready for analysis using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) method in SmartPLS 4, namely the measurement model and structural model tests. The analysis results show that service quality is not significantly related to user satisfaction but has a direct effect on trust. Meanwhile, information quality, system quality, and human-like chatbot interaction are positively related to trust and user satisfaction. Trust and user satisfaction are positively related to intention to continue using. The results of this study can contribute both theoretically and practically to modern AI chatbot quality evaluation models.

latest.title: The Role of Social Media and Digital Content in Increasing Sales of Culinary MSMEs in Lubuklinggau
latest.abstract: This study aims to determine and analyze the role of social media and digital content in increasing sales of culinary Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Lubuklinggau City, both partially and simultaneously. This study used a quantitative approach with an associative research design. Primary data were collected through questionnaires from 77 culinary MSME respondents selected using purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with SPSS version 25. The results showed that Social Media (X1) had a positive and significant effect on Sales Increase (Y), with a t-value of 11.029. Digital Content (X2) also had a positive and significant effect on Sales Increase (Y), with a t-value of 12.078. Simultaneously, Social Media and Digital Content significantly affected Sales Increase, with an F-value of 143.128. The R Square value of 0.795 indicates that the two independent variables jointly explain 79.5% of the variation in sales increase, while 20.5% is explained by other factors outside the study. These findings indicate that more optimal social media utilization and better digital content quality can strengthen the opportunity for culinary MSMEs to increase sales.

latest.title: A transformer-based explainable machine learning framework for heterogeneous ESG risk and return prediction using text intelligence
latest.abstract: Corporate ESG disclosure has shifted toward narrative form, yet vendor ESG ratings that most empirical work depends on show substantial disagreement across providers, and encoders dominant in financial text analysis inherit a 512-token ceiling that discards most of a typical 10-K. HET-ESGFormer combines hierarchical long-document encoding, heterogeneity-aware sparse expert routing conditioned on industry sector and firm size, and a dual-channel explanation layer subject to faithfulness verification. The framework is evaluated on 3,182 U.S.-listed firms over 2015 to 2024 using 10-K filings, sustainability reports, earnings call transcripts, and ESG-tagged news. Against nine baselines spanning econometric, dictionary-based, contextual encoder, sparse-attention, and time-series approaches, HET-ESGFormer reduces return RMSE from 0.0417 to 0.0389 and QLIKE from 0.148 to 0.128, with Diebold-Mariano tests rejecting equal predictive accuracy against every baseline after correction for multiple comparisons. The text channel's marginal contribution to downside risk prediction is materially larger than its contribution to return prediction, widening at longer forecast horizons, indicating that ESG narratives carry more information about risk than about expected return. Ablations reveal a decoupling between predictive skill and explanation faithfulness: removing the consistency regularizer barely affects accuracy but sharply degrades explanation quality. The dual-channel explanation improves ERASER comprehensiveness by 50% over SHAP applied to XGBoost, and human raters significantly prefer the framework's rationales over SHAP-based rationales on trustworthiness. Decile-sorted long-short portfolios deliver a post-cost Sharpe ratio of 1.31 against 0.74 and 0.62 for portfolios built o

latest.title: Marketing Considerations for Reaching Asian American Segments
latest.venue: Journal of Marketing Development and Competitiveness
latest.abstract: Asian Americans are a rapidly expanding, economically influential, yet historically under-targeted consumer segment. Using machine-learning-based relevance filtering, this paper reviews foundational literature and key considerations for effectively reaching Asian Americans. Findings indicate that marketing strategies are most effective when brands use nuanced segmentation, tailor creative content to acculturation levels and subgroup identities, and avoid generic ethnic appeals. The analysis underscores the importance of authentic representation and inclusion and outlines directions for future research.

latest.title: L'identité numérique au service de la personnalisation de l'expérience client : un levier de compétitivité pour les entreprises
latest.abstract: Résumé À l’ère du digital, l’identité des consommateurs se construit à travers les données qu’ils génèrent en ligne : profils, historiques d’achats, interactions et comportements numériques. Ces informations constituent une ressource stratégique pour les entreprises, qui les exploitent grâce au Big Data, à l’intelligence artificielle et aux outils CRM afin de proposer des expériences personnalisées. La personnalisation des offres, de la communication et des parcours clients renforce la satisfaction, la fidélisation et la proximité avec la marque. Elle devient ainsi un véritable levier de compétitivité, permettant aux entreprises de se différencier, d’améliorer leur performance marketing et d’optimiser leur productivité. Toutefois, cette dynamique soulève des défis liés à la vie privée, à la confiance numérique et à la régulation des données. Cet article s’attache à comprendre comment l’identité numérique des consommateurs, constituée par l’ensemble des données qu’ils laissent en ligne, peut être utilisée par les entreprises pour concevoir des expériences personnalisées. Il met en évidence les mécanismes par lesquels ces données favorisent l’adaptation des offres, la fidélisation des clients et l’optimisation des stratégies marketing. Il interroge également les retombées de cette personnalisation sur la compétitivité des entreprises, en soulignant à la fois les opportunités d’innovation et les défis liés à la confiance, à la régulation et à l’éthique à l’ère du digital.Mots clés : Identité numérique, Expérience personnalisée, Données clients, Compétitivité des entreprises. Abstract In the digital age, consumer identity is built through the data they generate online: profiles, purchase histories, interactions, and digital behaviors. This information is a strategic resourc

latest.title: The Influence of Business Risk, Financial Performance, and Debt Policy on Firm Value
latest.abstract: Firm value reflects management performance and investor confidence, which can be influenced by business risk, financial performance, and debt policy. This study aims to analyze the effect of business risk, financial performance, and debt policy on firm value in Consumer Non-Cyclicals sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2019–2024 period. A quantitative approach was employed using purposive sampling, yielding 396 observations from 66 companies. Data analysis was performed using panel data regression with the Fixed Effect Model via EViews 13. The results indicate that business risk, financial performance, and debt policy simultaneously have a significant effect on firm value. Partially, business risk proxied by Degree of Operating Leverage (DOL) has no significant effect on firm value. Conversely, financial performance proxied by Return on Assets (ROA) has a positive and significant effect on firm value, while debt policy proxied by Debt to Asset Ratio (DAR) shows no significant effect. This study concludes that profitability is a primary factor considered by investors in enhancing firm value.

latest.title: Klasterisasi Karakteristik Pengguna E-Commerce Berdasarkan Profil Pengguna Menggunakan Algoritma K-Prototypes
latest.abstract: Accurate customer segmentation supports more personalized e-commerce marketing. However, the Recency, Frequency, Monetary (RFM) model focuses on transaction history and may not fully capture shopping motivation or the share of a consumer’s spending allocated to e-commerce (Share of Wallet/SoW). This study aims to cluster e-commerce users based on transaction profiles and consumer behavior using the K-Prototypes algorithm. Data were collected from 198 e-commerce users in Palembang, Indonesia. The clustering variables included RFM, SoW, shopping motivation, and product-category preferences, while age category was used for follow-up analysis. The Elbow Method and Silhouette Score supported a four-cluster solution. The resulting personas were High-Value Promo Hunters, Routine Pragmatic Shoppers, Passive Micro-Spenders, and Urgent Big-Ticket Buyers. The Chi-square test indicated a significant association between age category and persona, with Cramér’s V of 0.274. This suggests that age is associated with shopping patterns but does not fully determine consumer profiles. The findings can inform more targeted promotions and user-experience design. The study is limited to 198 respondents from Palembang, so the findings may not represent e-commerce users in other regions.

latest.title: Membentuk Keputusan Pembelian Konsumen: Sinergi Digital Entrepreneurship, Persepsi Harga dan Kualitas Produk Studi Pada Konsumen Jatinangor House Kota Bogor
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze and determine 1) The Influence of Digital Entrepreneurship on Purchase Decisions, 2) The Influence of Price Perception on Purchase Decisions, 3) The Influence of Product Quality on Purchase Decisions of Jatinangor House consumens in Bogor City. The development of a competitive culinary industry in the digital economy era requires business actors to integrate technology and maintain product value alignment in order to influence consumer behavior. The type of research used is a quantitative approach with a survey method. Primary data collection was conducted through the distribution of structured questionnaires with a Likert scale to 180 respondents selected using non-probability sampling technique with a purposive sampling approach, which is a sampling technique based on certain criteria established by the researcher. The criteria for respondents are Jatinangor House consumens in Bogor City who have made a product purchase. The data analysis method used in this research is Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) through the Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) analysis tool with the assistance of SmartPLS 4.0 software. The results of hypothesis testing show that: 1) Digital Entrepreneurship has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Decisions with a t-statistic value of 3.021 and a p-value of 0.003, 2) Price Perception has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Decisions with a t-statistic value of 1.988 and a p-value of 0.047, and finally 3) Product Quality has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Decisions with a t-statistic value of 6.493 and a p-value of 0.000 The results of this study show that the variables of Digital Entrepreneurship, Price Perception, and Product Quality have a positive and significant influence on the Purc

latest.title: Minimum-Bill Thresholds in Promotional Milk Coupon Subscriptions: A Review of Consumer Redemption, Basket Value, and Association Rule Mining
latest.abstract: A minimum-bill coupon requires a shopper to reach a specified transaction value before receiving the offer. This paper examines a milk coupon subscription in which the qualifying minimum bill is raised from Rs 99 to Rs 149, an increase of about 50.5%. Through a focused narrative review of studies on coupon redemption, sales promotions, conditional (minimum-spend) promotions and association rule mining in retail, it argues that the higher threshold may encourage some customers to add products to qualify while discouraging redemption among those whose usual baskets fall below the new threshold, so that the net effect on sales and profitability cannot be inferred from the threshold alone. The paper proposes a conceptual framework, five research questions and four hypotheses, and a methodology for future empirical work combining pre-post or comparison-group analysis of redemption and transaction value with Apriori-based market basket analysis, together with a set of evaluation metrics.

latest.title: The Silent Stylist: Bridging the Garment Literacy Gap Through Educational Labeling
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: This whitepaper introduces a novel consumer-experience and retail strategy framework: Educational Garment Labeling. Despite an abundance of choice in modern retail, consumer uncertainty surrounding color coordination and versatility leads to widespread default purchasing—manifested in the ubiquitous reliance on neutral and black wardrobes. This paper identifies the root cause of this trend as a "visual literacy gap" at the point of decision, where traditional garment tags act solely as regulatory compliance tools rather than instructional guides. To solve this friction, the paper proposes the Styling Card architecture—a physical or hybrid digital labeling standard that provides three core datapoints on high-end and elevated apparel: Definitive Undertone & Color Naming: Demystifying precise shade identities. Palette Harmonization: Practical guidance for classic and accent color combinations. The Tri-Style Matrix: Actionable pairings for Sporty, Casual, and Elevated contexts. The whitepaper outlines the psychological mechanisms, retail conversion metrics (fitting room conversion, basket size, and return rate reduction), and print/digital implementation models necessary for manufacturers and retailers to turn garment tags into silent brand ambassadors.

latest.title: The Effects of Digital Entrepreneurship, Digital Literacy, and Digital Platforms on Gen Z Purchase Decisions
latest.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies has fundamentally transformed the competitive landscape of micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). To remain competitive, MSMEs are increasingly required to strengthen their digital entrepreneurial capabilities, improve consumers' digital literacy, and optimize the use of digital platforms. This study examines the effects of digital entrepreneurship, digital literacy, and digital platforms on Generation Z purchase decisions as a strategy for strengthening MSME competitiveness in the era of artificial intelligence. The study employed a quantitative approach involving 175 Generation Z consumers of a local culinary MSME in Bogor, Indonesia. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The findings demonstrate that digital entrepreneurship has a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions (β = 0.336, t = 4.040, p < 0.001). Digital literacy also positively and significantly influences purchase decisions (β = 0.205, t = 2.009, p = 0.045), while digital platforms show a positive and significant effect (β = 0.296, t = 3.180, p = 0.001). The model explains 55.8% of the variance in Generation Z purchase decisions. These findings highlight the importance of integrating entrepreneurial digital capabilities, consumer digital literacy, and effective digital platform utilization to enhance MSME competitiveness. In the era of artificial intelligence, these capabilities provide an important foundation for MSMEs to improve market engagement, strengthen consumer decision-making, and sustain their competitiveness in an increasingly technology-driven business environment.

latest.title: DIGITAL FINANCIAL LITERACY AND FINANCIAL RESILIENCE AMONG UNIVERSITY STUDENTS IN PAKISTAN: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF FINANCIAL SELF-EFFICACY
latest.venue: Insights (Bhalwal) International Journal of Humanities Management and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to determine the relation between Digital Financial Literacy with Financial Resilience and to investigate financial self-efficacy in the relation of both.Objective: To see the relationship between Digital Financial Literacy and Financial Resilience and to explain the relationship between both variables with financial self-efficacy. As for the method and research design, the positive approach was applied with deductive research and cross sectional design. The respondents included adult university students who had accessed at least one digital financial service during the past six months. Forty (400) valid responses were received. The hypothesized model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with 5000 bootstrap resample number. Contribution: The study identifies financial resilience (the ability to manage financial disruptions) as a different phenomenon from financial well-being, and the psychological process between digital skills and financial coping. The results indicated that perceived digital financial skills were significantly and positively related to the financial self-efficacy (β = .52); and significantly and positively related to the financial resilience (direct path, β = .23) based on the survey data obtained from 400 students. The indirect association via self-efficacy was also positive (β = .20, 95% CI [.15, .27]) which lent support to a complementary partial mediation path. Practical implications: The results can be used for the financial education in university, the protection of digital consumers and the aid for students.

latest.title: From Consumption to Creation: Social Media Engagement and Visit Intention in Vietnamese Restaurants
latest.abstract: Customer engagement with brand-related content on social media is increasingly recognised as a multidimensional phenomenon. Drawing on the Consumers’ Online Brand-Related Activities (COBRA) framework, this study examines how content consumption, contribution, and creation influence consumers’ attitudes toward online reviews and ratings and their purchase/visit intentions in the restaurant industry. Existing research has largely focused on highly visible engagement behaviors, leaving fewer observable forms of engagement underexplored, particularly in emerging markets. A quantitative, cross-sectional design was employed using survey data from 509 social media users engaging with Golden Gate Restaurant Group brands in Vietnam. Measurement scales were adapted from established studies, and the proposed model was tested using Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) with AMOS. The findings show that all three engagement dimensions have significant positive effects on attitudes toward online reviews and ratings and on purchase/visit intention. Content consumption, often considered a passive behavior, produced stronger effects on both attitudinal and behavioral outcomes than content contribution and creation. These results demonstrate the importance of low-visibility engagement behaviors in shaping consumer perceptions and decision-making processes. The study contributes to the literature by extending the COBRA framework to the restaurant context and providing evidence from an emerging market. From a managerial perspective, the findings suggest that restaurant marketers should develop social media strategies that encourage engagement across all behavioral levels rather than concentrating solely on content creation. Overall, the study highlights the strategic value of customer engage

latest.title: SYNERGY OF SCIENCE-EDUCATION-BUSINESS (SEB) COLLABORATIONIN THE ESTABLISHMENT OF RESEARCH UNIVERSITIES: THE CASE OF AZERBAIJAN
latest.venue: Journal of Baku Engineering University Philology and Pedagogy
latest.abstract: This study analyzes the current state and development dynamics of scienceeducation-business (SEB) collaboration in Azerbaijan, focusing on the mechanisms that enable multidimensional synergies within the national innovation ecosystem.The research adopts a qualitative methodology based on comparative evaluation and SWOT analysis, allowing for a systematic assessment of institutional frameworks, policy documents, and collaborative practices regulating interactions among universities, research institutes, and the business sector.The findings reveal that Azerbaijan has considerable institutional potential for SEB integration.Key strengths include modernized material and technical infrastructure, strategic state programs supporting higher education development, and an evolving regulatory framework that encourages innovation activities.However, several challenges remain.These include limited commercialization of scientific research outcomes, misalignment between educational programs and labor market demands, and weak, unsustainable university-industry collaboration.Furthermore, the study identifies structural limitations such as underdeveloped technology transfer mechanisms, insufficient support for spin-offs and start-ups, and a lack of diversified research funding sources.The research contributes to the literature by examining SEB collaboration within a developing innovation system context.It also offers practical and policy-oriented recommendations aimed at enhancing innovation management, strengthening human capital, and establishing a sustainable and effective SEB collaboration model in Azerbaijan.

latest.title: When Is AI Recommendation Transparency Read as Promotion? Disclosure Elaboration, Motive Attribution, and Consumer Trust
Building Operational Excellence: Evaluating Training System and Skills Development Program for Rmfb7
latest.abstract: This study systematically evaluated the current training system and skills development program of the Regional Mobile Force Battalion 7 (RMFB7) at its Headquarters in Sibonga, Cebu. Grounded in the Kirkpatrick Model of Training Evaluation, Human Capital Theory, Knowles’ Andragogy, and Bandura's Social Cognitive Theory, the study utilized a descriptive-evaluative research design. Through purposive sampling, data were gathered from a total of eighty (80) respondents, structurally distributed between seventy (70) frontline Tactical Personnel (Non-Commissioned Officers) and ten (10) Battalion Training and Operations Officers (S7 and S3 command sections).The profiling phase demonstrated that the tactical frontline of RMFB7 is predominantly young and lower-ranking, with 60.0% of the NCOs falling within the 21–30 age bracket and 50.0% holding the rank of Patrolman/Patrolwoman. Unit tenure was concentrated at 1–5 years (54.3%). While baseline training was universal via the Basic Internal Security Operations Course (BISOC, 100.0%), advanced specialized certifications were remarkably low, with only 25.7% completing Special Counter-Insurgency Unit Training (SCOUT) and 20.0% certified in advanced Marksmanship. For the command group, 70.0% held post-graduate master's units, but 50.0% possessed less than two years of direct experience in training management due to rapid personnel rotations. The evaluative phase revealed severe internal imbalances across the four primary dimensions of the training program. Curriculum Content achieved the highest score with a category weighted mean of 3.42 (Very Effective), proving a strong strategic alignment with localized asymmetrical threats in Region 7 (3.55) and terrain applicability (3.48). Instructional Delivery was rated as 3.15 (Effective), h

latest.title: Satisfaction, Continuance and Loyalty in Food Delivery Apps: A Bibliometric Analysis of Research, 2016-2026
latest.venue: International Journal of Business and Management
latest.abstract: Research on why consumers stay satisfied with, continue using and remain loyal to food delivery apps (FDAs) has grown rapidly, but existing bibliometric reviews rely on single subscription databases and do not publish the search, screening or cleaning steps needed to check them. This study maps that research stream with a fully reproducible protocol. A documented query run in OpenAlex on 14 October 2026 returned 539 records; after logged screening, 420 English-language journal articles published between 2016 and 2026 were analysed. Performance analysis compared full and fractional counting and age-normalised citations. Science mapping combined co-citation analysis with concept co-occurrence analysis based on a published 29-concept thesaurus, Louvain clustering with stability checks and a robustness test on core journals. Output grew by about 40% a year between 2019 and 2025 and has levelled off since 2024. It is concentrated in Indonesia, Malaysia and India, while influence is concentrated in a few early studies. The intellectual base forms one cohesive network rather than distinct schools. At the default resolution, three stable conceptual clusters emerge: service performance and experience, technology acceptance in the COVID-19 period, and relational outcomes; finer resolutions separate an emerging experience-oriented theme. Since the pandemic, attention has shifted from COVID-19 framing towards trust, loyalty, customer experience and delivery performance. Few studies name a theory or use non-survey methods. The findings describe research attention, not causal drivers; practical implications are therefore framed as testable hypotheses for different operating scenarios.

latest.title: Analysis of Religion and Consumption Research
latest.venue: International Journal of Business and Management
latest.abstract: The aim of this study is to identify the general trends of the existing literature on international studies on religion and consumption and to explore the conceptual, intellectual and social structure of the field. For this purpose, 1794 publications searched in the Web of Science database were analysed by bibliometric analysis method. The analysis of the data was carried out with R programming language. Performance analysis and science mapping techniques were applied to analyse the data. According to the findings of the study, the author with the most publications is ‘E.A. Minton’ while ‘O. Sandıkcı’ was the author with the most citations. The journals that publish the most study is ‘Journal of Islamic Marketing’, and the country that produces the most works is ‘USA’. The most cited study is by Muniz and Schau (2005). The most frequently repeated words in the studies were ‘religion’, ‘religiosity’, ‘consumption’, ‘Islam’, ‘consumer behaviour’ and ‘spirituality’. Analysis of keyword co-occurrence network, document and author co-citation network, and author and country collaboration network revealed various clusters. This study presents the general academic structure of the field of religion and consumption and provides a holistic perspective on the field.

latest.title: Segmentasi Pelanggan Berbasis Rfm dan K-Means pada Sistem Analitik Penjualan
latest.abstract: The growth of daily transaction data volumes in the retail sector often ends up as passive digital archives due to resource limitations in manual analysis. This condition makes it difficult for management to map consumer loyalty objectively, causing marketing strategies to miss the target. This study aims to design a web-based analytical information system using Python to automate customer segmentation. The approach used is the Knowledge Discovery in Database (KDD) cycle, integrating RFM (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) model feature extraction with the K-Means Clustering Unsupervised Machine Learning algorithm. From a total of 2,590 rows of raw transaction data, the system successfully pre-processed and aggregated them into 60 unique customer entities ready for clustering. Testing using the Elbow Method validated that the optimal number of partitions for this dataset is three clusters. Based on K-Means computation using Euclidean Distance, the system reached absolute convergence at the eighth iteration. This study successfully partitioned consumers into three segments: High Priority or Loyal Cluster, Medium Priority or Regular Cluster, and Low Priority or Passive Cluster. This analytical system is proven effective in visualizing segmentation autonomously, utilized as business intelligence to design targeted promotions and minimize customer churn risk. For future research, it is recommended to integrate directly into the point-of-sale system database in real-time and add customer demographic variables to make the analysis more comprehensive.

latest.title: Impact of restaurant robot service consumption values on their consequences: the moderating effects of perceived risk and human–robot interaction quality
latest.venue: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Insights
latest.abstract: Abstract The present study aimed to develop a new conceptual model on restaurant robot service consumption values (RRSCVs) and investigate their influence on diverse outcome variables. The study collected data from 756 customers who experienced restaurant robot services using convenience sampling techniques. This study employed exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) to assess reliability and validity of the data, as well as to evaluate model fit indices. A structural equation modeling (SEM) analysis with a multi-group approach was used to test relationships. The results showed that functional values of performance and quality, humanlike capability, social, emotional, and epistemic values significantly predicted attitude toward robot services, while price, safety, and privacy values did not. Attitude was found to be a significant predictor of perceived brand equity. Finally, perceived brand equity strongly influenced the intention to pay more, loyalty, intention to recommend to others, and intention to participate in value co-creation. Both perceived risk and human-robot interaction quality partially influenced the relationships in the structural model. This study provides insightful academic and practical implications, facilitating a deeper understanding of the role of the RRSCVs in the hospitality business.

latest.title: Building competitive advantage through digital transformation: How market turbulence shapes performance outcomes in Indonesian SMEs
latest.abstract: This study examines competitive advantage's mediating role in digital transformation-firm performance relationships while investigating market turbulence's moderating effect, addressing gaps in understanding environmental volatility's influence on transformation effectiveness in emerging markets. Survey data from 350 Indonesian SMEs were analyzed using PLS-SEM and Necessary Condition Analysis. Results reveal competitive advantage partially mediates digital transformation-performance relationships, transmitting 30% of total effects through indirect pathways. Market turbulence significantly moderates transformation processes with progressive effect intensification across turbulence levels. NCA demonstrates that competitive advantage, digital transformation, and market turbulence constitute necessary conditions creating performance ceilings rather than merely additive contributors. Organizations must simultaneously develop competitive positioning, transformation capabilities, and appropriate environmental contexts, as deficiency in any factor generates insurmountable performance ceilings. This research reconciles contradictory literature by demonstrating digital transformation operates through dual pathways with contingent effectiveness, providing empirically validated framework explaining when and how digital transformation creates value through moderated mediation and necessary condition logic.

latest.title: Soft total quality management practices and business performance: The mediating role of an integrated quality management system
latest.abstract: This study examines how information sharing, top management commitment, and managerial competence influence business performance through Integrated Quality Management System as a mediating mechanism among East Java beverage manufacturers. Drawing on Resource-Based View and General Systems Theory, a ten-hypothesis model was tested using Consistent Partial Least Squares estimation via SmartPLS on census data from 108 managers across 42 firms. All three soft TQM practices exert significant positive effects on IQMS, while their direct effects on business performance are uniformly non-significant a structural configuration confirming full mediation whereby IQMS absorbs the total performance-relevant variance of each antecedent. Top management commitment produces the most robust mediated pathway, with information sharing demonstrating near-complete transmission through the mediator. These findings resolve two persistent empirical inconsistencies in TQM scholarship: the contested directness of soft practice-to-performance relationships and the context-dependent variability of IQMS performance effects. The study extends RBV capability orchestration theory, advances Systems Theory's organisational application, and provides actionable guidance for managers and policymakers seeking to replicate East Java's counter-cyclical manufacturing resilience at national scale.

latest.title: AI-powered capabilities are associated with green new product development through exploratory and exploitative pathways
latest.abstract: Abstract Purpose – This study aims to investigate the mechanisms through which AI‑powered capabilities influence green NPD in manufacturing firms. Specifically, it examines the dual mediating roles of green exploratory and green exploitative, and tests whether the mediating effect of exploration is stronger than that of exploitation in the AI‑green NPD link. Design/methodology/approach – Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory, this study develops a dual mediation framework distinguishing green exploratory (sensing‑driven opportunity identification) from green exploitative (seizing/transforming‑driven process refinement). Hypotheses are tested using survey data from 333 Chinese manufacturing firms across five high‑priority sectors. Hierarchical regression and bootstrapped mediation analysis (PROCESS Model 4; 5,000 resamples) are employed. Findings – The results show that both green exploratory and green exploitative significantly mediate the positive relationship between AI‑powered capabilities and green NPD. Critically, the indirect effect via green exploratory is significantly stronger than that via green exploitative, supporting asymmetric mediation. The full model explains 54% of the variance in green NPD. Originality/value – This study makes three key contributions. First, it unpacks the mediation black box between AI and green NPD by specifying two distinct process architectures. Second, it challenges the “balance assumption” of ambidexterity theory by demonstrating the primacy of exploratory mediation in AI‑enabled green innovation contexts, thereby extending dynamic capabilities theory. Third, it provides a rigorous methodological template for testing dual and asymmetric mediation, offering actionable guidance for managers, AI vendors, and policymakers.

latest.title: Assurance and ESG rating divergence can limit the informational value of sustainability disclosure mandates
latest.abstract: Abstract Regulators increasingly treat disclosure quantity as the principal policy lever, assuming that more sustainability disclosure yields better-informed investors and more efficient capital allocation. This conceptual paper argues that the assumption is misspecified. Disclosure moves investor beliefs only insofar as it is credible, and credibility is manufactured downstream of the reporting entity, by assurance providers who verify and rating agencies who aggregate. We develop the construct of the credibility wedge, the gap between the quantity of sustainability information a firm discloses and the reliability investors attach to it. Drawing on costly state verification, cheap-talk and signalling models, ambiguity-based asset pricing and institutional theory, we specify a three-layer architecture of preparer, assurer and rater, each with a distinct failure mode. Twelve propositions connect regime design to the wedge, and the wedge to belief revision, the cost of capital and capital allocation. A two-by-two typology is derived and applied to the four architectures observable in 2026: the narrowed European regime, jurisdictions adopting IFRS S1 and S2, the United States, and India’s BRSR Core. As the wedge grows, the marginal informational return to additional disclosure tends to zero, implying that verification and rating infrastructure must be built before disclosure scope is widened. India offers an unusually favourable research setting, and eight estimable models are specified. For the 2030 Agenda, target 12.6 and its report-counting indicator track disclosure volume rather than decision-useful information, making credible verification a precondition for reporting to advance SDGs 12 and 13.

latest.title: Too little, too much, or just right? How AI recommendation information volume shapes trust and consumer behavior
latest.venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) shopping assistants explain why a product is selected, yet the appropriate defaults remain unclear. We define recommendation information volume as the amount of nonredundant, product-relevant information and compare five ordered explanation packages. Study 1 identifies an inverted-U response in a randomized Chinese mobile-retail experiment. Study S1 compares identical messages attributed to an AI assistant or a human salesperson, with separate source-neutral measurement validation. Study 2 reports conditional positive indirect associations through perceived usefulness, trust in AI, and decision comfort, and conditional negative indirect associations through information overload and algorithmic over-justification. Same-session estimates do not establish causal mediation. Its product-version comparison combines complexity, functionality, and safety considerations. Study 3 provides behavioral evidence across 51,248 recommendation impressions and service outcomes for 5000 distinct users. Moderate packages perform best within the tested sets. Bounded information processing explains the benefit–burden trade-off; persuasion knowledge suggests that disproportionate justification depends on expectations of selective versus comprehensive advice, across AI and human sources. Because amount, diagnostic priority, and content composition vary jointly, the experiments identify assigned-package effects, not pure quantity effects. The findings support category-specific testing of default explanations without establishing an exclusively algorithmic mechanism.

latest.title: Studi Literatur : Pengaruh Cash Turnover, Inventory Turnover, dan Total Assets Turnover terhadap Kinerja Keuangan
latest.venue: Jurnal Semesta Ilmu Manajemen dan Ekonomi
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui dan mensintesis pengaruh cash turnover, inventory turnover, dan total assets turnover (TATO) terhadap kinerja keuangan perusahaan yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia, mengingat rasio aktivitas lazim diasumsikan berhubungan positif dengan kinerja keuangan tetapi bukti empiris di Indonesia tidak seragam. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif berbasis studi literatur terhadap 15 publikasi periode 2021-2026 yang dicari melalui aplikasi Publish or Perish dan disitasi melalui Mendeley. Hasil review menunjukkan: 1) Cash turnover tidak pernah berpengaruh positif signifikan; empat dari tujuh studi menemukan pengaruh negatif signifikan dan tiga studi tidak signifikan. 2) Inventory turnover menunjukkan hasil yang berlawanan arah: satu studi positif signifikan, dua studi negatif signifikan, dan tiga studi tidak signifikan. 3) TATO cenderung positif signifikan (empat dari tujuh studi), meski belum seragam. 4) Pada beberapa studi, variabel tidak signifikan secara parsial tetapi signifikan secara simultan. Artikel ini memberikan peta komparatif per variabel dan lima proposisi yang dapat diuji pada penelitian empiris lanjutan.

latest.title: Creating satisfaction and loyalty among tourists: the power of experiential tourism
latest.abstract: Abstract The current research examines whether experiential tourism activities in the tourism industry can influence tourists’ behaviour. Using the stimulus-organism-response framework, the study examines how experience affects travellers’ intentions for satisfaction and loyalty among online travel agents (OTAs). Data were collected from 208 visitors across five travel destinations in India, specifically wildlife sanctuaries and national parks, to examine their lived experiences. The results were analysed using a partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) approach, indicating that experiential tourism indicators have a direct effect on customer engagement. The study suggests that experiential motivation is vital in shaping tourists’ satisfaction and loyalty. The results suggest that tourists are more likely to return to the OTA and recommend it to others if they have positive experiential motivation during their travel encounter. Moreover, the study highlights the importance of co-creation in the tourism industry. In the challenging competitive space, leveraging experiential strategies can help managers gain a competitive advantage. Travel retailers must focus on increasing tourists’ conscious participation and include certain activities that may motivate them and create enthusiasm. This study is one of the few in India to explore the relationship between experiential activities and tourist satisfaction and loyalty among wildlife sanctuaries and national parks travellers.

latest.title: Dynamic Capabilities, Organizational Resilience, Digital Transformation and Organizational Performance of Deposit-Taking Saccos in Nairobi County, Kenya
latest.venue: Journal of Economics Finance and Management Studies
latest.abstract: This study examined the influence of dynamic capabilities on the organizational performance of deposit-taking SACCOs in Nairobi County, Kenya, and tested the mediating role of organizational resilience and the moderating role of digital transformation. Given the importance of SACCOs and the various challenges they face from digital disruption and regulation, this study aims to investigate the impact of dynamic capabilities on the performance of SACCOs in Kenya’s Nairobi County. The survey design was used to collect data directly from the SACCO managers in the study areas. Out of the 240 questionnaires distributed, 210 yielded usable responses for the study, giving the study an 87.50% response rate. The data were collected using five-point Likert scales and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, hierarchical regression, Hayes PROCESS Models 4 (mediation), 1 (moderation), 14 (moderated mediation), and 59 (second-stage moderated mediation). The findings of the study revealed that dynamic capabilities had a positive and significant effect on organizational performance. Furthermore, dynamic capabilities significantly enhanced the organizational resilience of these SACCOs, and the organizational resilience significantly improved their organizational performance. Additionally, digital transformation significantly predicted their organizational performance. The study also established that organizational resilience partially mediated the relationship between dynamic capabilities and the performance of these SACCOs. The index for moderated mediation was significant, as digital transformation significantly moderated the relationship between dynamic capabilities and the organizational performance of these SACCOs.
