latest.title: Human Capital Reporting in the Era of ESG: Analyzing HRA Disclosures and Transparency in Leading FMCG Companies in India
latest.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Commerce Management & Social Science
latest.abstract: In the current business environment global ESG frameworks and traditional financial reporting have intertwined to redefine the organization value paradigm. The Human Capital Development(HCD) and Human Resource Accounting(HRA) have evolved from secondary disclosures to primary markers of a sustainable corporate strategy. Against the global context of sustainability ever so much at the forefront of corporate behaviour, and the impending imposition of mandatory regulatory rationale to ESG standards (e.g., the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR)that SEBI has heard will come into force), this paper investigates human capital reporting and disclosures in five leading Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) companies in India (Hindustan Unilever, Dabur India, ITC, Britannia, and Nestle) as pioneers of practices that seek to achieve improved accountability in the coverage of significant parameters of the Subject Core Component. This study synthesizes recent literature across both emerging and developed markets to propose an integrated theoretical model of how ESG-driven HRA disclosures are associated with organizational governance and corporate performance. This paper used a content analysis study of top Indian FMCG companies including Hindustan Unilever Limited (HUL), ITC Limited, Dabur India and Nestle India to examine disclosure behaviour, reveal structural reporting gaps, and evaluate the influence of attributes of companies on human resource disclosure index. The preliminary finding is that tier-one Indian FMCG companies perform well on international ESG metrics on training, diversity, and occupational health, although the actual measuring of HRA metrics is not common and is usually not standardized in large-mid-sized firms. Finally, this study provide a fra

latest.title: A POST-TRAINING EVALUATION OF TOUR GUIDES’ KNOWLEDGE, ATTITUDES, AND SKILLS IN MUSLIM-FRIENDLY TOURISM
latest.venue: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
latest.abstract: The Muslim tourism market is expanding rapidly worldwide, leading destinations to develop Muslim-centric tourism offerings. Muslim-friendly tourism focuses on delivering comfortable travel experiences that adhere to Muslim principles, including the provision of halal food, prayer facilities, and suitable environments. Tour guides serve as cultural ambassadors and are essential in facilitating culturally sensitive experiences. However, there is a notable lack of comprehensive training programs to equip tour guides with the necessary skills, knowledge, and attitudes to address the needs of Muslim tourists. This study assesses post-training knowledge, skills, attitudes, and readiness among tour guides who completed the Muslim-Friendly Tour Guide (MFTG) course. Employing a quantitative cross-sectional evaluation design, data were collected through questionnaires administered to 50 tour guides in Malaysia. Findings indicate that participants demonstrated strong post-training competence in explaining Islamic beliefs, advising on dress codes, and identifying halal food options. The guides exhibited substantial knowledge of Islamic practices, positive attitudes toward serving Muslim travellers and high motivation to meet their needs. Correlation analysis revealed a strong positive interdependence among skills, knowledge, attitudes, and readiness. The study concludes that professional training programs such as the MFTG course effectively prepare tour guides to address the requirements of Muslim-friendly tourism. Comprehensive training approaches are therefore essential for cultivating culturally sensitive guides and supporting the sustainable growth of Muslim-friendly tourism.

latest.title: INFLUENCER CREDIBILITY AND TRAVEL DECISION-MAKING AMONG YOUNG GEN Z SOCIAL MEDIA USERS IN PENANG
latest.venue: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
latest.abstract: Social media has become a significant influence on consumer decisions worldwide, including decisions about where and how to travel. Drawing on the source credibility model, this study examined the relationship between three influencer credibility dimensions, attractiveness, trustworthiness and expertise; and travel decision-making among young Generation Z (Gen Z) social media users in Pulau Pinang, Malaysia. A total of 266 respondents aged 18 to 28 were recruited using non-probability purposive sampling, supported by online snowball distribution through university and young-adult networks. Data were collected through a self-administered online questionnaire adapted from established credibility scales and analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression. All three dimensions correlated positively and significantly with travel decision-making at the bivariate level. In the regression model, the three dimensions jointly explained 54.3 per cent of the variance, F(3, 262) = 103.68, p < .001. Expertise emerged as the strongest predictor (β = .49, p < .001), followed by attractiveness (β = .23, p < .001), while trustworthiness made no significant unique contribution (β = .10, p = .165), a result attributable to its strong correlation with expertise (r = .80). The achieved sample was predominantly female (82.0 percent), aged 18 to 24 (91.7 percent), and not in paid employment (83.8 percent); the findings therefore characterise this specific segment of young, highly engaged Gen Z social media users rather than the Gen Z population of Pulau Pinang as a whole. The study extends understanding of influencer credibility in a Malaysian travel context and indicates that destination marketers targeting young Gen Z audiences should prioritise dem

latest.title: EXPLORING GEN Z’S AWARENESS OF KUIH KELAMAI IN GOPENG: A QUALITATIVE STUDY
latest.venue: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
latest.abstract: This exploratory study investigates the awareness, consumption barriers, and cultural perceptions of Kuih Kelamai, a traditional Rawa Malay delicacy, among Generation Z in Gopeng, Perak. Employing a qualitative research design, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 Generation Z participants aged between 19 and 23 years (n=15) to explore their familiarity, consumption experiences, and attitudes towards this traditional food. The thematic findings reveal that limited physical market availability and minimal digital exposure significantly reduce awareness and consumption opportunities among younger generations, with encounters largely restricted to festive seasons and cultural occasions. Despite these limitations, participants demonstrated strong appreciation for the cultural authenticity, artisanal craftsmanship, and distinctive bamboo-cooking preparation associated with Kuih Kelamai. However, accessibility challenges, insufficient promotional activities, and the absence of effective digital marketing strategies continue to discourage regular consumption. Furthermore, participants exhibited nuanced price sensitivity, expressing willingness to pay premium prices for authentic traditional products when supported by convenient purchasing options and improved accessibility through modern retail outlets and digital platforms. The study highlights the importance of integrating traditional culinary preservation with contemporary marketing approaches to strengthen youth engagement, enhance product visibility, encourage sustainable consumption, and ensure the continuity of Rawa Malay culinary heritage among future generations.

latest.title: The Impact of Audit on Good Governance in Dimen Shoring Incorporated: Basis for Compliance and Transparency
latest.venue: World Journal of Sustainable Advances in Multidisciplinarity
latest.abstract: This study assessed employee perceptions of the impact of audit practices on good governance in Dimen Shoring Incorporated – Calamba, Laguna Branch. Using a quantitative-descriptive research design, data were collected from 105 employees through a close-ended survey questionnaire and analyzed using weighted means. The findings indicated that employees strongly agreed that internal audit practices (overall weighted mean = 3.68), external audit practices (3.66), compliance audit procedures (3.67), and audit frequency and follow-up implementation (3.69) were effectively practiced and contributed to organizational improvement. Results further showed that good governance was strongly perceived in the workplace, particularly in accountability (3.75), compliance with policies and regulations (3.76), ethical management and resource utilization (3.70), and transparency (3.67). The study concluded that employees perceived auditing as a valuable mechanism that supports governance outcomes through strengthened compliance, accountability, transparency, and ethical management. Recommendations focused on improving communication of audit results, enhancing follow-up visibility, strengthening audit procedure orientation, improving decision-related transparency, and reinforcing ethical culture initiatives.

latest.title: UNDERSTANDING GEN-Z’S ATTITUDE TOWARDS PENANG’S LOCAL FOOD: THE ROLE OF EMOTIONAL, PRESTIGE, AND QUALITY-VALUES
latest.venue: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
latest.abstract: Penang’s local food creates an important element of the state’s cultural identity and serves as a key driver of tourism attractiveness. As Generation Z (Gen-Z) increasingly becomes a prominent consumer group in both the food and travel industries, understanding their perceptions and engagement with local food experiences has become increasingly important for sustaining culinary tourism and preserving cultural heritage. This study aims to examine the factors that contribute to Gen-Z’s attitude towards Penang’s local food by focusing on three variables which is emotional value, prestige value and quality value. A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was employed, utilizing a self-administered questionnaire distributed to 431 Gen-Z respondents aged 18-29 years in Malaysia who had prior experience consuming Penang's local food. Convenience sampling was used, and data were analyzed using Pearson correlation and multiple regression analyses. Results indicated that all three variables significantly influence Gen-Z’s attitudes with prestige value emerging as the strongest predicator, followed by quality and emotional value. These findings suggest that social recognition, sensory satisfaction and emotional connections play an essential role in shaping young consumers’ perception of local food. The study provides useful insights for tourism authorities, local food businesses, and cultural stakeholders to develop more effective strategies in preserving Penang’s culinary heritage while aligning with the preferences of the younger generation in a rapidly digitalized and globalized food culture.

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Abstract Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: A Glance on Changing Workplace Dynamics Post Covid-19 in India: A Review of Psychological Employee Withdrawal Behavior
hot.abstract: Advances in Consumer Research (Abbreviated as Adv. Consum. Res.) is a distinguished journal based in the United States and published by Sheridan Books. The journal is highly regarded in the academic community, particularly within the fields of Business, Management, and Accounting, with a specific focus on Marketing.
