In addition, brand perception partially mediated the relationship between social identity and cultural authenticity and fashion customer behaviour, and students favoured apparel labels that resonated with their cultural identity and social affiliations. Practical and Social Implications: The findings of the study underline the necessity to integrate cultural components and identity values into local fashion branding efforts. For policymakers and fashion marketers, this research provides empirical data supporting programmes that promote cultural authenticity and identity-driven branding as instruments fo

latest.title: Fairness perceptions in marketing strategy and across the marketing mix: An integrative review and call to action
latest.abstract: Abstract Fairness is a foundational and highly consequential construct in marketing, shaping purchase intentions, brand attitudes, complaints, boycotts, and word‐of‐mouth. Yet extant consumer research has largely concentrated on price fairness, leaving fairness across the rest of marketing strategy and the marketing mix comparatively underexplored. This review makes three contributions. First, we review and integrate the field's three theoretical foundations: dual entitlement, inequity aversion, and moralized cognition. Second, we organize recent findings in the fairness literature around two managerial frameworks: strategy (segmentation, targeting, and positioning) and tactics (promotion, place, and product, in addition to price). Third, we highlight understudied areas and topics across the full range of marketing activities and issue a call to action for future research.

latest.title: Low-Carbon Consumer Behavior in the Digital Age: Investigating the Determinants of Green Product Purchase Intentions in E-Commerce Platforms
latest.abstract: Digital commerce is reshaping how consumers discover, evaluate, and purchase products, creating new opportunities to encourage lower-carbon consumption while also intensifying convenience-driven consumption and information overload. This article examines the determinants of green product purchase intention in e-commerce by integrating behavioral, value-based, trust-based, and digital-information perspectives. It develops an integrative conceptual framework that links environmental concern, attitudes toward green products, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, green perceived value, price perceptions, green trust, digital information quality, electronic word of mouth, platform affordances, and perceived greenwashing to purchase intention. The article uses a structured integrative review of recent research and authoritative sustainability reports, emphasizing studies published from 2021 onward while retaining established theories where needed to explain underlying mechanisms. The synthesis indicates that pro-environmental concern is important but rarely sufficient on its own: consumers must also believe that a product performs well, offers acceptable value, can be purchased without excessive effort, and is supported by credible evidence. Digital interfaces may reduce information costs through certification details, traceability, reviews, and product comparisons, yet they can also amplify unsubstantiated environmental claims and impulsive purchasing. Green trust and perceived information usefulness therefore emerge as central mechanisms connecting digital communication to intention, while price sensitivity, perceived risk, delivery impacts, and doubts about green claims can weaken the relationship.

latest.title: When Brands Cross the Line: A Bibliometric Review of Brand Transgression
latest.venue: Vikalpa The Journal for Decision Makers
latest.abstract: Brand transgression occurs when a brand’s action violates consumer expectations or prevailing societal values, potentially damaging consumer-brand relationships and diluting brand equity. Although scholarly attention to this domain has increased, the literature remains fragmented, offering no consolidated view of the field’s development. To address this gap, this study systematically reviews 269 publications on brand transgression indexed in Scopus and Web of Science from 2015 to 2025. Through performance analysis, co-citation analysis and keyword co-occurrence mapping, we identify key knowledge foundations, major research themes and emerging research directions. The findings provide managers with insights into proactive and preventive strategies to address brand transgression.

latest.title: The Influence of Sales Promotion Content, Content Attractiveness, and User-Friendliness on Financial Decision Making through Imitation Intention
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study examines the influence of sales promotion content, content attractiveness, and user-friendliness on financial decision making through imitation intention among social media users in Indonesia, particularly in the context of influencer marketing for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in the food and beverage sector. Research Method: This study uses a quantitative explanatory design with a cross-sectional approach. Data are collected through an online questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale and purposive sampling. Data analysis employs Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) using SmartPLS. Results and Discussion: The study proposes that sales promotion content, content attractiveness, and user-friendliness influence imitation intention and financial decision making. Imitation intention is also expected to influence financial decision making and mediate the relationships between promotional content characteristics and financial decisions. These relationships will be evaluated empirically. Implications: The findings are expected to help MSMEs and influencers develop promotional strategies that encourage informed financial decisions among social media users. Future research may examine other factors affecting consumer financial behavior. Originality: This study integrates three influencer promotional content characteristics with imitation intention to explain financial decision making in the Indonesian MSME food and beverage sector.

latest.title: The Instagram paradox: a mediation analysis of consumer orientations, psychological, cognitive and deep structure dimensions & Instagram motivations shaping purchase intention of sustainable apparel in India
latest.abstract: Introduction This study examines how distinctive consumer orientations - Thrifty, Frugal, Moral, and Shopper influence sustainable apparel purchase intention among Indian Instagram users. Grounded in Uses and Gratifications theory and the Theory of Planned Behaviour, the study examines the parallel mediating roles played by inherent psychological, cognitive and deep structures and external stimuli of Instagram motivation in rendering consumer orientation to purchase intention, thus presenting an empirical justification for the ‘Instagram Paradox’ in the framework of sustainable fashion. Methods A quantitative survey was administered to 285 Instagram users and followers of sustainable apparel brands in India, recruited via snowball sampling. Factor Analyses was conducted to validate constructs spanning consumer orientation, psychological, cognitive and deep structure dimensions, Instagram motivations, and purchase intention. Results K-means cluster analysis identified four distinct consumer orientation segments. Four parallel mediation models tested whether psychological, cognitive and deep structure dimensions along with Instagram motivation mediated the relationship between each consumer orientation and purchase intention. Discussion Across all the mediation models, psychological, cognitive and deep structure constructs emerged as the sole significant mediator, while Instagram motivation consistently failed to generate a significant indirect effect on purchase intention in any model, constituting the central empirical evidence for the Instagram Paradox.

latest.title: Older adults’ social responses to AI virtual humans in digital kinship contexts: associations of loneliness, perceived cues and appraisals with purchase intention
latest.abstract: As AI virtual humans become increasingly prominent communicative actors on short-video platforms, digital kinship content characterized by kinship-based forms of address, family narratives, caring expressions, and companionship-oriented interaction has begun to enter older adults’ everyday media use and become intertwined with commercial recommendation. Selectively drawing on the three-factor theory of anthropomorphism and integrating it with the Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) paradigm, this study conceptualizes loneliness as a manifestation of sociality motivation; emotional appeal, human likeness, and homophily as perceived cues and appraisals associated with elicited agent knowledge; and social presence and empathy as proximal social responses within the CASA framework. It examines older adults’ social perceptions of and emotional responses to kinship-oriented AI virtual humans and their associations with purchase intention. Using a standardized set of AI virtual human short videos representing key features of digital kinship content as stimuli, we collected valid data from 372 Chinese adults aged 65 years and older and employed partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) as parallel and complementary analytical approaches. The PLS-SEM results revealed distinct antecedent patterns for the two proximal responses. Emotional appeal showed the strongest association with social presence, whereas homophily was more strongly associated with empathy than with social presence. Human likeness was significantly associated only with social presence, while loneliness was positively associated with both responses. Empathy showed a stronger association with purchase intention than social presence, and all i

latest.title: The influence of user generated content and electronic word of mouth on TikTok toward purchase intention for Chikuro: a study of Generation Z in Bogor City
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of user generated content (UGC) and electronic word of mouth (E-WOM) on TikTok on consumers’ purchase intention toward Chikuro products among Generation Z in Bogor City. This study is motivated by the high internet penetration in Indonesia, the dominance of TikTok among Generation Z, and the viral phenomenon of Chikuro through UGC and E-WOM content. A quantitative method with a descriptive-associative approach was employed. Data were collected through an online questionnaire from 200 Generation Z respondents in Bogor City who had been exposed to Chikuro content on TikTok, using convenience sampling. Data were analyzed using structural equation modeling–partial least squares (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS 4.1.1.8. The results show that UGC and E-WOM have a positive and significant effect on purchase intention, with an R-square value of 0.646.

latest.title: Too crowded to be adventurous: the effect of social crowding on consumer switching behavior
latest.abstract: Introduction Global urbanization has inevitably increased the density of individuals in public spaces, exerting considerable influence on marketing strategies and consumers. Despite expanding research on how consumers are influenced by social crowding, consensus among researchers remains elusive. Drawing on conservation of resources (COR) theory, this research investigates how social crowding affects consumer switching behavior. Methods Across five studies, including a quasi-experimental field study, we examine the effect of social crowding on switching intentions and test risk aversion motivation as an explanatory pathway, as well as shared consumption and crowding aversiveness as boundary conditions. Results Social crowding significantly decreases switching intentions, with η 2 ranging from 0.03 to 0.16. Mediation analyses provide evidence consistent with risk aversion motivation as an explanatory pathway. Importantly, this effect disappears when consumers engage in shared consumption or when the crowding is non-aversive. Discussion These findings offer a resource-based interpretation of consumer responses to crowding. From the COR perspective, maintaining familiar choices may serve a protective function when crowding is appraised as a threat to valued resources. Practically, managers can mitigate the negative effect of crowding on switching behavior by encouraging shared consumption and providing risk-reducing cues.

latest.title: An examination of economic and non-economic satisfaction among micro-enterprise business banking customers in South Africa
latest.abstract: Purpose Drawing on the business-to-business (B2B) relationship perspective, this study reconceptualises satisfaction as both an antecedent and an outcome within micro-enterprise banking relationships. Specifically, it examines how economic satisfaction influences non-economic satisfaction through the relational mechanisms of trust and commitment and assesses the mediating roles of these constructs. Design/methodology/approach Structural equation modelling was used to analyse the data through testing the proposed relationships. Data were collected from a sample of 381 micro-enterprise business banking customers in South Africa. Findings The results indicate that economic and non-economic satisfaction play distinct roles in shaping relationship quality. Economic satisfaction significantly predicts trust and commitment, whereas non-economic satisfaction is influenced by both trust and commitment. Bootstrapped mediation analysis further shows significant indirect effects of economic satisfaction on non-economic satisfaction through both trust and commitment. As the direct effect of economic satisfaction on non-economic satisfaction remains significant when the mediators are included, the findings indicate partial rather than full mediation. Thus, economic satisfaction influences non-economic satisfaction both directly and indirectly through relational mechanisms. Research limitations/implications The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and non-probability sampling. Future research could adopt longitudinal and comparative approaches across industries to validate and extend these findings. Practical implications Banks serving micro-enterprises should focus on enhancing customers' economic satisfaction (e.g. competitive pricing, business growth support) to build tru

latest.title: El impacto del WOM en la calidad del servicio: estrategias para mejorar la experiencia del cliente
latest.abstract: El presente artículo de revisión examina el impacto del word of mouth (WOM) en la calidad del servicio y propone estrategias basadas en evidencia para mejorar la experiencia del cliente. Mediante un análisis exhaustivo de la literatura científica actual, se destacan los factores que influyen en la generación y propagación del WOM, así como su relación con la percepción de calidad y la satisfacción del cliente. Los hallazgos revelan que el WOM, tanto tradicional como electrónico (e-WOM), ejerce una influencia significativa en el comportamiento del consumidor, las ventas, la lealtad y el desempeño empresarial, superando el impacto de la publicidad tradicional. Se establece una relación bidireccional entre la calidad del servicio y el WOM, mediada por la satisfacción del cliente. El e-WOM impacta directamente en la percepción de la calidad y en las decisiones de compra. Por lo tanto, las estrategias de gestión del WOM deben adaptarse a los nuevos canales digitales y abordar proactivamente la reputación en línea. Las conclusiones respaldan un enfoque holístico que integre la calidad del servicio, la satisfacción del cliente y la gestión estratégica del WOM, tanto tradicional como digital, para obtener una ventaja competitiva significativa, fomentar la lealtad, impulsar las ventas y construir una sólida reputación en el mercado.

latest.title: DOES RELIGIOUS PROXIMITY MATTER? UNIVERSITY BRAND AWARENESS AMONG MADRASAH ALIYAH STUDENTS IN SEMARANG
latest.venue: EDUCATOR Jurnal Inovasi Tenaga Pendidik dan Kependidikan
latest.abstract: Increasing competition among higher education institutions has made university branding an important strategic consideration in attracting prospective students. This study aims to analyze and compare the level of brand awareness of Universitas Islam Negeri (UIN) Walisongo, Universitas Negeri Semarang (UNNES), and Universitas Diponegoro (UNDIP) among Madrasah Aliyah students in Semarang City. A quantitative comparative approach was employed involving 231 Grade 12 students from 18 Madrasah Aliyah institutions selected through proportional simple random sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire measuring five dimensions of brand awareness, namely brand recall, brand recognition, top-of-mind awareness, brand confidence, and brand familiarity. Data analysis was conducted using One-Way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), followed by the Least Significant Difference (LSD) post-hoc test. The results reveal significant differences in brand awareness among the three universities (F = 125.219, p < 0.001). The pairwise comparison shows that UNDIP has the highest level of brand awareness, followed by UNNES, while UIN Walisongo records the lowest level. These findings indicate that religious and educational proximity does not automatically generate stronger brand awareness toward an Islamic higher education institution among Madrasah Aliyah students. The study highlights the need for Islamic higher education institutions, particularly PTKIN, to strengthen institutional positioning through consistent branding, integrated digital communication, clearer academic differentiation, and sustained engagement with prospective students. Future studies should examine factors such as institutional reputation, digital engagement, brand trust, word of mouth, and perceived academic q

latest.title: A Multidimensional Analysis of Factors Influencing the Intention to Follow Travel Influencer Recommendations
latest.abstract: This study examined the factors influencing social media users' intentions to follow travel destination recommendations provided by travel influencers in the context of digital tourism in Indonesia. The study integrated selected constructs from three theoretical perspectives: attitude from the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB); information value and entertainment value from Uses and Gratifications Theory (UGT); and attractiveness, trustworthiness, and expertise from Source Credibility Theory (SCT). Data were collected from 471 respondents residing in the Greater Jakarta metropolitan area (Jakarta, Bogor, Depok, Tangerang, and Bekasi, or Jabodetabek) through an online questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results revealed that attitude toward travel influencers (B = 0.442) and parasocial relationships (B = 0.399) were the strongest direct predictors of the intention to follow travel recommendations. Source credibility had a substantial positive effect on parasocial relationships (B = 0.620; f² = 0.626), while parasocial relationships mediated the relationship between source credibility and behavioral intention (B = 0.247). Among the content-related variables, information value emerged as the strongest predictor of attitude (B = 0.297), followed by content factors (B = 0.219) and entertainment value (B = 0.213). In contrast, perceived congruence did not significantly predict attitude (B = 0.056; p = 0.138). These findings suggested that, in a high-involvement decision-making context such as travel, audiences placed greater emphasis on the informational value and credibility of influencers than on perceived similarity or identity congruence. From a managerial perspective,

latest.title: A Mixed Analytical Approach to Synthesizing Evidence in Digital Transformation Research on Traditional Markets
latest.abstract: Objectives: This study is to examine how traditional markets globally are navigating digital transformation and identify conceptual trajectories relevant for Indonesia’s context.Methodology: The study employs an integrated mixed analytical approach combining bibliometric analysis with probabilistic topic modelling. Bibliometric techniques are used to map publication structures, intellectual relationships, and thematic evolution, while Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), followed by interpretive topic labelling, is used to identify latent semantic patterns within the corpus. A total of 84 Scopus-indexed publications were analyzed using Bibliometrix and topic modelling in Python to map intellectual structures, thematic evolution, and knowledge clusters within the literature.Finding: The findings indicate an increasing presence of themes associated with artificial intelligence, governance, sustainability, and consumer analytics within the analysed literature. Rather than demonstrating a uniform transition toward intelligent market systems, these patterns suggest an emerging diversification of research beyond basic technology adoption toward broader institutional, behavioural, and data-driven concerns. The analysis also shows that digital transformation in traditional markets remains constrained by gaps in digital literacy, uneven infrastructure, and the need for inclusive policy frameworks.Conclusion: The study concludes that successful modernization requires aligning technological innovation with social inclusion, particularly by strengthening digital literacy, expanding equitable infrastructure, and embedding ethical AI governance. These insights provide a foundation for building sustainable and socially resilient pathways for the future of traditional market digitalizati

latest.title: ANALYSIS OF NEW CULTURAL MARKETING, CUSTOMER-PERCEIVED VALUE AND SERVICE QUALITY ON REPURCHASE INTENTION AT RAHASIA COFFEE
latest.venue: International Journal of Economic Business Accounting Agriculture Management and Sharia Administration (IJEBAS)
latest.abstract: This study was motivated by the suboptimal repurchase intention of Rahasia Coffee customers—as evidenced by pre-survey results and issues regarding New Cultural Marketing, Customer Perceived, and Service Quality—as well as a decline in Rahasia Coffee’s sales during the 2022–2025 period. The study aims to analyze the influence of New Cultural Marketing, Customer Perceived [Value], and Service Quality on the repurchase intention of Rahasia Coffee customers, both partially and simultaneously. A quantitative, associative research approach was employed. Non-probability sampling—specifically purposive sampling—was used to select a sample of 110 respondents. Data were collected via Likert-scale questionnaires and processed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27. Analytical techniques included multiple linear regression, partial tests (t-test), simultaneous tests (F-test), and the coefficient of determination. The results indicate that New Cultural Marketing has a positive and significant effect on repurchase intention, with a regression coefficient of 0.235, a calculated t-value of 6.747, and a significance value of 0.000. Customer Perceived also has a positive and significant effect, with a regression coefficient of 0.231, a calculated t-value of 3.125, and a significance value of 0.002. Service Quality shows a positive and significant effect, with a regression coefficient of 0.091, a calculated t-value of 2.296, and a significance value of 0.024. New Cultural Marketing exhibited the highest Standardized Beta value (0.518), making it the variable with the most dominant relative influence on repurchase intention. Simultaneously, the three variables exerted a positive and significant influence, with a calculated F-value of 37.660 and a significance value of 0.000. The R-squared v

latest.title: From engagement to loyalty: the mediating roles of brand trust and social media brand posts
latest.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine how social media brand engagement influences brand loyalty in the smartphone industry. Particular attention is given to the mediating roles of customer engagement with social media brand posts and brand trust, thereby clarifying the mechanisms through which engagement translates into enduring consumer–brand relationships. Design/methodology/approach The study collected survey data from 585 smartphone users in Jordan. Measurement validity was established through confirmatory factor analysis, and hypotheses were tested using a structural path model, providing robust statistical evidence of the relationships among the engagement, trust and loyalty constructs. Findings Social media brand engagement positively influences brand loyalty, both directly and indirectly through brand trust. Aggregated post-level engagement exerts a weaker effect, contributing modestly to loyalty. Disaggregated analyses reveal that engagement behaviors differ in impact: liking significantly influences trust and loyalty, whereas commenting and sharing do not. Serial mediation is not supported for aggregated post-level engagement; a significant sequential pathway emerges through liking, trust and loyalty. Originality/value Customer engagement theory is advanced by differentiating between brand-level and post-level engagement, revealing that visible engagement behaviors are not uniformly valuable. Trust emerges as the dominant relational pathway driving loyalty. Situated within Jordan’s smartphone industry, the study extends the contextual relevance of engagement research in emerging markets. Managerially, the findings prioritize trust-building strategies over surface-level engagement indicators.

latest.title: Rethinking retail patronage: beyond customer loyalty towards reciprocal customer–retailer relationships
latest.venue: International Journal of Retail & Distribution Management
latest.abstract: Purpose This research clarifies retail patronage by combining consumer insights with bibliometric analysis to address conceptual fragmentation and support consistent measurement. Design/methodology/approach We combined qualitative interviews (n = 68) with a bibliometric analysis of 233 articles using Bibliometrix. Five experts provided an interpretive evaluation of the integrated findings. Findings Retail patronage emerges as a multidimensional relational construct integrating behavioural, intentional, and attitudinal components while remaining conceptually distinguishable from loyalty and love. The literature structures around antecedents and methodological foundations. Patronage occurs when repeated behaviour is relationally interpreted rather than situational. Practical implications Retailers should complement behavioural metrics with relational indicators to distinguish routine purchasing from genuine patronage and design relationship-focused loyalty programmes. Originality/value The study integrates consumer perspectives and intellectual foundations, positioning retail patronage as a reciprocal relational exchange construct to provide a basis for scale development. It explains why repetition can occur without loyalty and loyalty without patronage. The findings suggest that retail patronage extends beyond behavioural loyalty by reflecting reciprocal customer–retailer relationships grounded in ongoing relational exchange.

latest.title: Sprinkle, Smell, Remember: How Sensory Salience and Ritualistic Use of Domino's Oregano Drive Nostalgia-Mediated Repurchase Intention and Brand Recall
latest.venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
latest.abstract: Sensory cues serve as potent drivers of consumer behavior, yet their influence on nostalgia-mediated brand outcomes remains underexplored in the context of food service branding. This study investigates how sensory salience and ritualistic usage behaviors associated with Domino's oregano sachets influence repurchase intention and brand recall through three mediating mechanisms: nostalgic feelings, sensory pleasure, and emotional comfort. Employing a quantitative cross-sectional design, we collected data from 350 urban consumers with recent Domino's purchasing experience. Structural equation modeling via partial least squares (PLS-SEM) was utilized to test a comprehensive sensory-emotional branding framework. Results reveal that sensory salience, frequency of exposure, perceived uniqueness, and ritualistic usage behavior significantly predict mediating variables (nostalgic feelings, sensory pleasure, and emotional comfort), which subsequently enhance repurchase intention and brand recall. Notably, sensory pleasure emerged as the strongest direct predictor of both outcome variables (β = 0.283 for brand recall, β = 0.280 for repurchase intention, p < 0.001). The model explains 87.6% of variance in brand recall and 88.9% in repurchase intention, demonstrating the explanatory power of the sensory-emotional framework. This research extends sensory branding literature by conceptualizing micro branding cues as ritualistic touchpoints and contributes practical insights for leveraging sensory marketing in highly competitive food service environments.

latest.title: Food preferences, religion and online food delivery behaviour in India
latest.abstract: Online food delivery (OFD) platforms increasingly operate in culturally heterogeneous markets where patronage may be conditioned on social identities and functional considerations. This study examines whether dietary orientation is associated with three dimensions of OFD engagement – adoption, ordering frequency and multihoming – and whether these associations vary across religious contexts in India. Using survey data from 507 respondents, probit and negative binomial models with marginal effects are employed. The findings indicate that vegetarianism is associated with lower OFD engagement across all three dimensions. The association with adoption is statistically significant among Hindu/Jain respondents, but not among respondents from other religious groups. However, the formal interaction between dietary orientation and religion is not statistically significant, indicating that these sub-group patterns should be interpreted as conditional associations rather than definitive evidence of moderation. Nevertheless, the negative interaction coefficient provides a descriptive indication that the association between vegetarianism and OFD adoption may be attenuated across religious contexts, particularly in larger samples and especially among Hindus/Jains. Education is positively associated with OFD adoption and multihoming, while age and gender are associated with ordering frequency. The findings contribute to OFD research by highlighting dietary orientation as a potentially relevant basis for behavioural segmentation alongside conventional consumer characteristics. For OFD operators, the results suggest that dietary segmentation may inform market strategy, but specialised services or infrastructure should be guided by granular market research on segment size, demand intensi

latest.title: Brand Cross-Boundary Collaborative Innovation and Brand Loyalty: The Mediating Effect of Consumers' Perceived Sincerity and the Moderating Effects of Trait Cynicism and Product Maturity
latest.abstract: Brand cross-boundary collaborative innovation has become an important strategy for strengthening brand loyalty. However, its effectiveness varies substantially in practice, and some cross-boundary collaborations may even produce adverse effects. Existing research has not sufficiently examined the psychological mechanisms underlying this process. This study develops a moderated mediation model in which consumers' perceived sincerity serves as the mediator, while trait cynicism and product maturity serve as moderators. Using Luckin Coffee's cross-boundary collaborative innovation as the research context, the model is empirically tested with 258 valid questionnaires. The results show that cross-boundary collaborative innovation positively affects brand loyalty and that consumers' perceived sincerity plays a partial mediating role. Trait cynicism positively moderates the direct effect of cross-boundary collaborative innovation on brand loyalty, while product maturity positively moderates the conversion of perceived sincerity into brand loyalty. These findings provide a theoretical basis and practical reference for brands to develop differentiated cross-boundary marketing strategies according to consumer traits and product maturity.

latest.title: Strategic Dynamics of Britannia Industries Ltd: A Holistic Analysis of Financial Performance, Marketing Excellence, and Competitive Position
latest.venue: Poornaprajna International Journal of Teaching & Research Case Studies (PIJTRCS)
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study aims to comprehensively evaluate the financial performance, marketing strategies, operational efficiency, and competitive positioning of Britannia Industries Limited within the Indian FMCG sector. It seeks to identify the company's strategic strengths, challenges, and growth opportunities through an integrated analysis of financial indicators, market dynamics, consumer behaviour, and supply chain capabilities, with a focus on sustainable competitive advantage. Methodology: This study adopts an exploratory research case study approach using secondary data from Britannia Industries Limited's audited annual reports, scholarly publications, industry reports, and other credible sources. It integrates descriptive financial and ratio analysis with qualitative SWOC, ABCD, and PESTLE frameworks to systematically evaluate the company's financial performance, marketing strategies, operational efficiency, and competitive positioning within the Indian FMCG sector. Results/Analysis: The analysis reveals that Britannia Industries Limited achieved sustained revenue growth, improved operating profitability, and stronger net earnings, with consolidated revenue increasing by 6.74% and profit attributable to equity shareholders rising by 16.28% in FY 2025–26. The SWOC, ABCD, and PESTLE analyses highlight the company's strong brand equity, extensive distribution network, and product diversification, while identifying challenges related to input-cost volatility, competitive pressures, and changing consumer preferences that require continuous strategic adaptation. Originality: This study offers an integrated exploratory case analysis of Britannia Industries Limited by combining audited financial performance indicators with SWOC, ABCD, and PESTLE frameworks to examine the i

latest.title: A influência das redes sociais no comportamento de consumo da Geração Z
latest.abstract: O presente artigo tem como objetivo analisar, por meio de uma revisão bibliográfica exploratória, a influência das redes sociais no comportamento de consumo da Geração Z. Parte-se do pressuposto de que essa geração, nascida em um contexto de conectividade permanente, constrói suas decisões de compra a partir de estímulos digitais distintos das gerações anteriores, sobretudo por meio de plataformas como TikTok e Instagram e da mediação de criadores de conteúdo. A pesquisa adota abordagem qualitativa, de natureza exploratória, fundamentada na análise de três artigos científicos publicados em periódicos nacionais, complementados por literatura de referência da área de marketing e comportamento do consumidor. Discutem-se o perfil de consumo da Geração Z, o papel das redes sociais como canais de descoberta e o funcionamento do marketing de influência e da prova social digital, além dos riscos associados ao consumo impulsivo mediado por algoritmos de recomendação. Os resultados indicam que a Geração Z é fortemente influenciada por gatilhos de autenticidade, prova social e conteúdo em vídeo curto, ao mesmo tempo em que demonstra ceticismo crescente em relação à publicidade tradicional e aos discursos publicitários percebidos como pouco genuínos. Conclui-se que a influência das redes sociais sobre o consumo dessa geração é real e mensurável, mas condicionada à credibilidade percebida do conteúdo e dos criadores envolvidos, o que impõe desafios teóricos e práticos ao campo do marketing digital e aponta para a necessidade de pesquisas futuras que aprofundem os efeitos de longo prazo dessa relação.

latest.title: Dongkrak Antik: Literature Study in Explaining Nostalgic Marketing and Digital Marketing
latest.abstract: Nostalgic marketing is widely used across consumer industries to elicit favorable attitudes and purchase intentions by activating memories, emotions, and identity-relevant meanings. Yet, the scholarly literature remains fragmented across related constructs such as nostalgia proneness, perceived authenticity, temporal distance, affective forecasting, and brand meaning while also differing in how nostalgia interfaces with digital marketing mechanisms. This literature study synthesizes major theoretical perspectives and empirical findings to explain why nostalgic marketing can be persuasive, how it is operationalized in branding communications, and how these effects may be amplified or transformed in digital environments. Drawing on research in consumer psychology, marketing communication, branding, and digital media studies, the review shows that nostalgia functions through multiple pathways: (1) emotional regulation and positive affect, (2) social and identity signaling, (3) cognitive fluency and perceived credibility, and (4) value-laden interpretation of brand history. In digital contexts, nostalgic content can be distributed and personalized at scale through recommendation systems, platform affordances, user-generated content, and interactive formats, which may strengthen engagement while also increasing risks of perceived manipulation or inauthenticity. Methodologically, the paper emphasizes how constructs are measured (e.g., nostalgia as a state versus trait) and how study designs (experiments, surveys, and observational platform research) affect causal inference. The study concludes with an integrative conceptual framework and research propositions to guide future work.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer

hot.title: Building trust in sustainable brands: Revisiting perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image
hot.abstract: This study revisits the key variables that build brand trust in consumers, addressing a critical issue for building lasting relationships between brands and consumers. Through a conceptual model, we examine how perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image influence consumer trust. The research is based on a sample of 1280 Spanish consumers over the age of 18, who responded to a questionnaire designed with previously validated scales. The PLS-SEM technique was used to validate the hypotheses and the proposed model. The findings reveal that perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image have a positive and significant effect on consumer trust. In particular, it was found that customer service directly influences customer satisfaction, which in turn reinforces brand trust. Additionally, the brand's communication strategy shows a significant positive relationship with brand image. Finally, customer satisfaction is identified as a mediating variable in the relationship between customer service and trust, indicating that a positive experience with customer service is fundamental for consolidating brand trust. This study contributes to enhancing the understanding of the factors that promote brand trust and offers practical implications for the development of effective marketing and brand management strategies. These insights can be especially relevant for sustainable brands, as the identified factors—perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image—are also critical in fostering trust in brands that prioritize sustainability. Incorporating sustainable practices into these areas may further strengthen consumer trust and loyalty toward sustainable brands.

hot.title: Impact of digital transformation on SME’s marketing performance: role of social media and market turbulence
hot.abstract: Despite the rising relevance of digital transformation, there is still a knowledge vacuum due to limited literature available on digital transformation. This study aims to examine the impact of digital transformation on the marketing performance of small and medium enterprises. This research seeks to fill this void by adopting the technology adoption model in order to explore how in a fast-changing technological environment, digital transformation plays its role in firm specific capabilities that are imperative for a firm to adopt, and how they impact firm’s marketing performance. Combination of convenience sampling as well as snowball sampling was used to collect the data. Utilizing survey data from 316 small to medium-sized enterprises in the twin cities (Islamabad & Rawalpindi), Pakistan the results indicate that digital transformation has a positive influence on small and medium enterprises’ marketing performance. This encourages businesses to take advantage of the opportunity presented by new digital technologies and industry-wide digitalization trends by adopting new technologies and improving their digital capabilities in order to increase their productivity, efficiency, and innovation as well as their marketing performance. Hence this study is a practical demonstration of how developing digital transformation may be used to develop novel digital products and services and thereby improve marketing performance that leads to the overall corporate performance. Finally, the study contributes to the literature by evaluating the proposed model that describes the relationships between digital transformation, social media marketing, market turbulence and marketing performance concurrently.

hot.title: Unveiling triple bottom line's influence on business performance
hot.abstract: Addressing environmental, social, and economic challenges has become a pressing global priority. The Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework offers a holistic approach for evaluating corporate performance by integrating economic, environmental, and social perspectives. Despite its increasing adoption in both managerial and academic research, there remains a significant gap in understanding how the TBL framework influences business performance. To address this, the study conducts a bibliometric review of 207 publications from the Web of Science database. The review highlights the multifaceted impact of practices linked to the TBL dimensions on business performance while introducing the TBL Influence on Business Performance model. This model provides valuable insights into how businesses can effectively apply TBL principles to address socio-environmental challenges, foster innovation, and achieve sustained long-term performance. The findings contribute valuable theoretical and practical insights into how organizations can utilize TBL principles to strengthen resilience, innovation, and performance in the face of global socio-environmental challenges.

hot.title: Understanding Customer Responses to AI-Driven Personalized Journeys: Impacts on the Customer Experience
hot.abstract: Within advertising, the customer journey concept helps explain how customer perceptions and behaviors evolve through seller–customer interactions. The concept has developed to reflect omni-channel marketing but neglects the emergence of algorithmically personalized advertisements. This study therefore explores impacts upon customer experiences of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven recommendations and personalized advertisements by analyzing customer perceptions of tensions between the personalization and customer empowerment inherent within AI-driven advertising. By combining semi-structured phenomenological interviews with Customer Journey Mapping, we capture experiences and behaviors across multiple touchpoints. Our findings show how technological limitations of AI mediate brand–customer relationships and influence customer behaviors. The study contributes theoretically by critically contextualizing AI-driven advertising within broader ethical debates, emphasizing practitioners’ responsibilities to combine technological advancements with consumer autonomy.

hot.title: The Impact of Visual Elements of Packaging Design on Purchase Intention: Brand Experience as a Mediator in the Tea Bag Product Category
hot.abstract: While packaging design plays a vital role in experience-oriented markets, how multiple visual elements influence purchase intention through brand experience remains unclear. This study addresses this gap by employing innovative orthogonal experiments to examine the complex relationship between the visual elements of packaging design and purchase intention for low-involvement products, integrating both design and marketing perspectives. Through orthogonal experimental design, we developed 14 packaging prototypes as stimuli by systematically manipulating five visual elements (Colour, Graphics, Logo, Typography, and Layout). The framework and prototypes were validated through expert evaluation. Data were collected via a cross-sectional survey from 490 tea bag consumers and analysed using SPSS (version 29.0) for preliminary data processing and Mplus (version 8.3) for structural equation modelling. Our results reveal the direct effects of visual packaging elements on consumer purchase intention. Notably, Colour, Graphics, Logo, and Layout significantly influence purchase intention through brand experience mediation. Importantly, our multi-level analysis of visual elements unveils distinct patterns in how different design levels (e.g., colour harmony, graphic types) affect consumer responses. This study provides novel theoretical insights into how consumers make purchase decisions based on packaging design visual elements, addressing a significant gap in existing research. Unlike previous studies focusing on isolated design elements, our systematic classification and multi-level analysis offer both theoretical insights into packaging design mechanisms and practical guidelines for designers and practitioners.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence in Digital Marketing Within the Framework of Sustainable Management
hot.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is not only revolutionizing digital marketing through personalized customer experiences and optimized advertising strategies, but it is also contributing to sustainability initiatives. As AI reshapes digital marketing, its impact on sustainability is becoming increasingly significant. This dynamic highlights the necessity of exploring how AI can be utilized to foster more sustainable marketing practices. This study seeks to answer the pivotal question: “How does AI impact the sustainability of digital marketing?” A systematic literature review was conducted in this study, following the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) framework to identify various relevant articles in the areas of sustainability and marketing. Furthermore, this study examines the crucial role of AI in enhancing sustainable business practices, highlighting a significant increase in adoption among enterprises. The findings demonstrate that the effective integration of AI into digital marketing enhances environmental sustainability, supports the attainment of economic sustainability objectives, and contributes positively to social sustainability outcomes. This study contributes to the field by providing a comprehensive analysis of the intersection between AI and sustainable marketing practices and offers valuable insights for marketers, businesses, and policymakers.

hot.title: The Impact of Green Perceived Value Through Green New Products on Purchase Intention: Brand Attitudes, Brand Trust, and Digital Customer Engagement
hot.abstract: This study examines how the introduction of green new products (GNPs) by luxury brands contributes to building brand equity (i.e., brand attitude and trust) through green perceived value (GPV) and empirically assesses its impact on consumers’ purchase intentions. Furthermore, it explores the moderating role of digital customer engagement (DCE) in the relationship between GPV and building brand equity. To verify the hypothesis, we performed the partial least squares structural equation model (PLS-SEM) as an analytical technique using 572 datasets from luxury consumers in China. The results revealed that GPV through GNPs significantly influences both brand attitude and brand trust. In addition, brand attitude and brand trust were found to have a significantly positive effect on purchase intention. Moreover, DCE was observed to positively moderate the relationship between GPV and brand trust. To enhance the purchase intentions for luxury brands, it is essential to foster brand attitude and brand trust by developing a multidimensional GPV through GNPs. Furthermore, DCE plays a crucial role in strengthening the brand trust component of GPV.

hot.title: Influence of short video content on consumers purchase intentions on social media platforms with trust as a mediator
hot.abstract: Short videos on social media platforms have boomed with the rapid growth of the video consumption industry and have become an important marketing tool for businesses. With the rise of platforms such as TikTok or Douyin, short videos have profoundly impacted consumer behavior, making it crucial to understand their role in shaping consumer purchase intention. However, there is still a need for further research on how short video content promotes consumer purchase intent. Based on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model, this study constructs a structural model to explore the impact of short video content on consumer purchase intention, focusing on the mediating role of consumer trust. The model incorporates usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment as external stimuli, consumer trust as internal psychological responses, and purchase intention as the final behavioral outcome. This study collected 372 valid data from Chinese consumers through an online questionnaire and empirically analyzed it using structural equation modeling. The study results show that short-form video content's usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment significantly affect consumers' trust and purchase intention. Moreover, consumer trust positively affects purchase intention and mediates the relationship between short video content and purchase behavior. This research extends the application of the SOR model to the context of social media short videos, highlighting the crucial role of consumer trust in shaping consumer purchase decisions. Based on these findings, we propose actionable strategies for businesses to optimize short video content and build consumer trust, ultimately enhancing marketing effectiveness and driving consumer purchases.

hot.title: Impact of Influencer Marketing on Consumer Behavior and Online Shopping Preferences
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Influencer marketing has emerged as a crucial element in digital marketing, significantly shaping consumer behavior and online shopping preferences. This study examined the multidimensional impact of influencer marketing by analyzing engagement metrics, marketing effectiveness, and consumer decision-making processes, based on consumers in the Greek sector. Through a structured methodological framework, the research employed a questionnaire-based survey, statistical modeling, and Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping (FCM) scenarios to assess consumer interactions with influencer-driven content. Findings highlight that while influencer marketing enhances brand engagement and sales, its effectiveness varies based on content authenticity, transparency, and user trust. Additionally, consumer purchasing decisions are influenced by social media visibility, personalized marketing strategies, and digital platform usability. This study underscores the need for strategic influencer selection and information-driven marketing optimization to sustain long-term consumer engagement. These insights provide practical implications for businesses aiming to enhance digital marketing strategies and contribute to the ongoing discourse on social commerce and consumer-centric marketing models.

hot.title: Guidelines for Theory Selection: The IMPACT Framework
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT Though the role of adopting an appropriate theory in shaping the publishability and impact of research has long been recognized, psychology and marketing researchers lack specific guidance on how to choose a theory to frame their work. Addressing this gap in the literature, this article proposes a set of guidelines for the selection of relevant macro‐foundational theory to guide research projects addressing specific meso‐ or micro‐foundational theoretical entities (e.g., constructs or individual decision‐making) for research impact. Specifically, we develop a set of six guidelines to select an appropriate macro‐foundational theory for research impact, including Interestingness , Matching , Parsimony , Applicability , Conceptual rigor , and Testability (collectively abbreviated as the “IMPACT” guidelines). We next depict the proposed guidelines in an organizing framework that specifies Matching , the theoretical co ‐infusion of the studied micro‐ or meso‐foundational theoretical entity and the chosen macro‐foundational theory, as the central action item for researchers to shape the impact of their work. Researchers are then advised to use the five remaining guidelines to assess the quality of their proposed Matching for research impact. We conclude by discussing pertinent implications that arise from our analyses (e.g., to ensure Interestingness , we recommend researchers to select a macro‐foundational theory that refutes (vs. affirms) prior findings).

hot.title: Authenticity in Influencer Marketing: How Can Influencers and Brands Work Together to Build and Maintain Influencer Authenticity?
hot.abstract: This study examines how different stakeholders perceive influencer authenticity, revealing the misalignments that arise when each group prioritizes different aspects of authenticity. In doing so, the authors generate new theory on influencer marketing and provide managerial insights for brands and agencies to collaborate effectively with influencers to resolve these misalignments and ultimately build and sustain influencer authenticity. Using exploratory, in-depth interviews with consumers, influencers, brand managers, and influencer marketing agencies, the study triangulates stakeholder perspectives on influencer authenticity. Specifically, it examines the misalignment among these groups through the lens of assemblage theory and explores how these misalignments may be resolved to produce successful and lasting influencer assemblages. Finally, it explores how influencer marketing agencies can help manage authenticity misalignments.

hot.title: Impact of social media advertising on consumer behavior: role of credibility, perceived authenticity, and sustainability
hot.abstract: Introduction Social media advertising is a crucial factor for predicting consumer behavior. Further credibility, authenticity, and sustainability of social postings enhance consumer purchase intentions in general and online shopping in particular. This empirical study investigated the impact of social media advertising on consumer behavior and the role of credibility, perceived authenticity and sustainability. The study also investigated the mediating effect of trust in the relationship between social media advertising and consumer behavior. Methods To measure the impact of the social media advertising effect on consumer behavior, eight reflective constructs, namely, credibility, sustainability, perceived authenticity, social media advertising effectiveness, satisfaction, purchase intentions and perceived value, were assessed. For the mediation analysis, consumer behavior was modeled as a higher-order construct with three sub-dimensions: satisfaction, perceived value and purchase intentions. Furthermore, the construct social media effectiveness is also modeled as a higher-order construct with four sub-dimensions: credibility, sustainability, authenticity and social media advertisement effectiveness. The data were collected from active social media users who engage in brand advertising and online shopping. A total of 500 valid responses were subjected to exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, and the hypotheses were tested via structural equation modeling. Results and discussion The SEM results reveal that constructs credibility and sustainability are strong predictors of consumer behavior in the context of social media advertising effectiveness. The mediating variable of trust partially mediated the relationship between social media effectiveness and consumer beh

hot.title: Factors influencing Generation Z’s intention to purchase sustainable clothing products in Vietnam
hot.abstract: The increasing awareness of environmental challenges has significantly influenced consumer behavior, with sustainable products, particularly sustainable clothing, becoming a top priority for Generation Z consumers. This study aims to investigate the factors influencing Generation Z's purchase intentions toward sustainable clothing in Vietnam, guided by the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model and Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) frameworks. Specifically, it examines the effects of green perceived value, green perceived quality, perceived price, social influence, product design, environmental concern, and environmental knowledge on purchase intentions. The study also explores the mediating roles of environmental attitude and product attitude in these relationships. The research employed a quantitative approach, using a Likert scale questionnaire to gather data from 641 Vietnamese Generation Z consumers. The study utilized exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and structural equation modeling (SEM) to analyze the data. The results revealed that all proposed hypotheses were supported, indicating that all factors significantly impact environmental attitude and product attitude, which, in turn, influence purchase intention. The results emphasize the strong mediating role of environmental attitude and product attitude, suggesting that consumers with positive attitudes toward the environment and products are more likely to intend to purchase sustainable clothing. This research provides valuable insights into the psychological and contextual factors that influence Generation Z's sustainable consumption behavior. For marketers, these findings underscore the need to promote transparency in sustainable practices, emphasize high product quality an

hot.title: Roles of logistics service quality in shaping generation Z customers’ repurchase intention and electronic word of mouth in E-commerce industry
hot.abstract: As e-commerce continues to reshape retail landscapes, logistics service quality (LSQ) has become a crucial determinant of customer trust, satisfaction, and long-term engagement. This study investigates the impact of logistics service quality (LSQ) dimensions on the behavioral intentions of Generation Z consumers within Vietnam's rapidly expanding e-commerce sector. The research focuses on how various LSQ factors-timeliness, personal contact quality, order accuracy, order condition, order discrepancy handling, and return convenience-affect trust and satisfaction, which subsequently influence repurchase intention and electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM). A quantitative approach was employed, gathering data from 495 Generation Z consumers with prior online shopping experience. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) was used to test the proposed model and its hypotheses. This study found that key LSQ attributes play a significant role in shaping both trust and satisfaction, which, in turn, drive repurchase intention and eWOM. However, the findings indicate that Generation Z's expectations for seamless logistics experiences vary across different service attributes. While factors such as order accuracy, order condition, and order discrepancy handling contribute to satisfaction, they do not necessarily build trust, highlighting the generation's high standards and perception of these aspects as fundamental rather than differentiating features. This study challenges traditional LSQ frameworks by highlighting the evolving expectations of digital-native consumers. It offers practical insights for e-commerce businesses, emphasizing the need for a strategic blend of technological efficiency, personalized interactions, and seamless post-purchase services to enhance c

hot.title: The Evolution of Digital Tourism Marketing: From Hashtags to AI-Immersive Journeys in the Metaverse Era
hot.abstract: This study examines how social media platforms influence tourism marketing strategies, consumer perceptions, and travel behaviors, addressing their sustainability implications. It aims to evaluate the current state of research on social media in tourism marketing, identify dominant trends, assess empirical evidence of impact, and critically highlight research gaps. The analysis focuses on three core marketing outcomes: destination image, travel intention, and user engagement-and includes a section examining sustainability considerations across environmental, sociocultural, and economic dimensions. The study uses a systematic critical review of 147 peer-reviewed academic articles published between 2015 and 2025, combined with a meta-analysis of 38 quantitative studies that report statistical effect sizes. The meta-analysis uses a random-effects model to compare the influence of different platforms and study contexts. Moderator variables include geographic region, platform type, and methodological design. Findings show that social media marketing has a statistically significant positive effect on destination image (Cohen's d = 0.61), travel intention (d = 0.54), and user engagement (d = 0.43). The analysis also reveals geographic bias, limited research on emerging platforms, and a lack of longitudinal and ethical inquiry. Findings suggest that tourism researchers and marketers may have to adopt more contextsensitive, interdisciplinary, and ethical approaches. Critical sustainability concerns emerge, including "overtourism", cultural commodification, digital inequities, and algorithmic biases. Further studies may focus on specific platform-related behaviors, long-term impacts, and integrated online strategies appropriate for global tourism diversity. Lastly, this paper adv

hot.title: Unveiling the future of responsible, sustainable, and ethical consumption: a bibliometric study on Gen Z and young consumers
hot.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
hot.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the key research themes and their evolutionary trajectory within the Gen Z and young consumers (GZYC) field, focusing on the interconnected dimensions of responsible, sustainable and ethical consumption. By using thematic maps and co-occurrence networks, the research seeks to identify significant trends and interconnections that shape sustainable behavior among this demographic. Design/methodology/approach This study used a bibliometric analysis of 546 papers sourced from the Scopus and Web of Science databases, following the framework established by Zupic and Cater (2015), Donthu (2024), Donthu et al. (2021) and Lim et al. (2024). Using R and Biblioshiny, the authors conducted performance analysis and science mapping to examine scientific output and conceptual themes within the GZYC field. Findings The performance analysis reveals an annual growth rate of 22.02% in publications, highlighting the increasing research interest in this area. The keyword co-occurrence analysis revealed eight distinct research clusters within the GZYC field, each representing key dimensions of responsible, sustainable and ethical consumption. These clusters encompass themes such as corporate social responsibility, gender and generational differences, green products, food sustainability, pro-environmental behaviors, the sharing economy and collaborative consumption, among others. The thematic maps and evolution revealed that over time, the focus has shifted. The first decade centered on sustainability and young consumers, while the second decade broadened to corporate social responsibility, green advertising and the sharing economy. By 2024, the focus has shifted toward more systemic and psychological perspectives, emphasizing the circular economy, susta

hot.title: Cyber Shopping Beyond Boundaries: The Metaverse Revolution in e‐Commerce and Consumer Behavior
hot.abstract: The metaverse is swiftly flattering an important player in the e‐commerce domain. It provides innumerable opportunities and indicates a revolutionary paradigm shift in e‐commerce. Online businesses can now create virtual storefronts that enable immersive, lifelike product exploration within the metaverse, in contrast to traditional brick‐and‐mortar stores that cater to local customers. Current research offers a novel conceptual framework based on theories of interactive media effects and the stimulus–organism–response paradigm to understand consumer purchase intentions in the metaverse. Carefully gathered data from 342 survey participants were then examined using the analytical tools of structural equation modelling (SEM) and importance–performance map analysis (IPMA). The results of the study shed light on how much perceived augmentation and interaction affect consumers’ cognitive and emotive reactions, including feelings of realism, immersion, and telepresence. Remarkably, these reactions have a significant influence on how customers behave. The study’s distinctive worth is found in its creative recommendations, which can help tech firms and metaverse developers improve the purchasing experience in this dynamic digital environment.

hot.title: Digital Tourism and Smart Development: State-of-the-Art Review
hot.abstract: The intersection between digital technologies and tourism emerges as a prominent area of research within the tourism industry. This is primarily driven by the immense complexity of digital tourism itself as a multifaceted social, economic, and cultural phenomenon. This paper reveals the future implications of tourism in the context of digital intelligence. To gain insights into the latest applications of digital tourism, this work reviews 278 studies spanning from 2012 to 2024. A systematic literature analysis method is proposed to identify the research hotspots and trends. Through value co-creation theory and Schumpeter’s innovation theory, five key trajectories are suggested, as follows: in-depth application of digital technologies in tourism, spawning new scenarios, new forms and new modes of digital tourism, and deep integration of digital economy and tourism real economy. This state-of-the-art review will help to reflect the efforts towards promoting the smart development of digital technologies in tourism.

hot.title: The influence of brand experience on brand loyalty in the electronic commerce sector: the mediating effect of brand association and brand trust
hot.abstract: Businesses are increasingly focusing on brand experience due to its dual role in directly creating customer value and shaping customers’ perceptions of brand equity. This study investigates the impact of brand experience on brand equity in Vietnam’s e-commerce sector. Primary data were collected from respondents with prior online shopping experience on e-commerce platforms. The research identifies four critical dimensions of brand experience in e-commerce services: sensory, affective, intellectual, and behavioral experiences. These components positively influence brand equity, particularly in terms of brand association, brand trust, and brand loyalty. Moreover, the study confirms the mediating roles of brand association and brand trust in the relationships between affective experience and brand loyalty, intellectual experience and brand loyalty, and behavioral experience and brand loyalty. This research offers a valuable contribution to the literature on brand experience and brand equity, especially within the e-commerce context. Managerial implications are also provided to guide businesses in enhancing customer brand experiences and strengthening brand equity.

hot.title: Service quality in mobile banking
hot.abstract: Purpose The rise of mobile technologies has driven rapid growth in mobile banking (m-banking), making service quality a central area of inquiry for researchers and industry practitioners alike. Despite this focus, understanding of service quality in m-banking remains fragmented. In this regard, this article endeavors to provide a comprehensive, state-of-the-art overview of service quality in m-banking. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on a systematic review of 71 studies, this article explores the concept of service quality in m-banking through the lens of theories, constructs, contexts, and methods (TCCM), revealing the multifaceted nature of service quality and its role in m-banking. Findings The review underscores the multifaceted nature of service quality and its pivotal role in steering pivotal customer-centric outcomes in m-banking. Introducing the stimulus-organism-response (S-O-R) framework into the discourse of m-banking, the review reveals a range of quality-, system success-, and user-based stimuli, affecting m-banking users’ attitude, brand attachment, flow, and trust, thus shaping their intended and actual behavior, including usage, satisfaction, loyalty, and word-of-mouth. Further scrutiny underscores opportunities for renewed endeavors to bridge identifiable gaps by harnessing mixed methods, exploring new constructs, probing demographic and cross-cultural variations, and forging new instruments tailored to evaluate contemporary m-banking service quality. Originality/value This review distinguishes itself by providing a comprehensive and systematic exploration of service quality in m-banking through the lens of TCCM. Unlike previous studies that often focus on isolated aspects, this review integrates diverse perspectives to offer a holistic understandin

hot.title: Interactive Viral Marketing Through Big Data Analytics, Influencer Networks, AI Integration, and Ethical Dimensions
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: The rapid growth of digital platforms has fundamentally reshaped network and viral marketing, profoundly transforming how information spreads across social networks and influences consumer behavior. This comprehensive review synthesizes theoretical, computational, and ethical perspectives into an integrated narrative, providing novel insights into the mechanisms driving information diffusion within contemporary interactive marketing. By integrating foundational concepts from social network theory, advanced graph models, and behavioral dynamics, the paper demonstrates how the interplay between network structures, influencer behaviors, and AI-driven algorithms significantly redefines traditional marketing paradigms. A distinctive theoretical contribution of this study lies in its innovative combination of Big Data analytics with AI-based predictive modeling, explicitly revealing how real-time algorithmic personalization not only enhances marketing effectiveness but also creates new ethical tensions surrounding misinformation, algorithmic bias, and consumer vulnerability. Addressing recent calls for greater theoretical originality and narrative coherence in interactive marketing research, this review explicitly highlights how these insights resolve critical theoretical puzzles and clarify contemporary ethical dilemmas. Additionally, the paper identifies emerging trends—including Web3 marketing, decentralized platforms, and neuroscience-driven targeting—offering clear future research directions. Through its integrative, narrative-driven framework, this study significantly advances interactive marketing theory, providing essential guidance for scholars and practitioners navigating the evolving complexities of digital influence.

hot.title: Generative AI for Consumer Behavior Prediction: Techniques and Applications
hot.abstract: Generative AI techniques, such as Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), and transformers, have revolutionized consumer behavior prediction by enabling the synthesis of realistic data and extracting meaningful insights from large, unstructured datasets. However, despite their potential, the effectiveness of these models in practical applications remains inadequately addressed in the existing literature. This study aims to investigate how generative AI models can effectively enhance consumer behavior prediction and their implications for real-world applications in marketing and customer engagement. By systematically reviewing 31 studies focused on these models in e-commerce, energy data modeling, and public health, we identify their contributions to improving personalized marketing, inventory management, and customer retention. Specifically, transformer models excel at processing complicated sequential data for real-time consumer insights, while GANs and VAEs are effective in generating realistic data and predicting customer behaviors such as churn and purchasing intent. Additionally, this review highlights significant challenges, including data privacy concerns, the integration of computing resources, and the limited applicability of these models in real-world scenarios.

hot.title: Applying the S-O-R model to explore impulsive buying behavior driven by influencers on social commerce websites
hot.abstract: ., videos and articles). When fans encounter these messages, they may make unplanned purchases, resulting in impulse buying behavior, a long-standing issue in marketing research. This study aims to explore the factors that lead to such behavior. Using the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) model as a framework, the study investigates how interactions between individuals and influencer content (Stimuli) trigger psychological changes in consumers, namely positive affect, flow state, and emotional attachment (Organism), which in turn lead to impulse buying behavior (Response). The study surveyed fans who had previously purchased products recommended by influencers, collecting 404 valid responses. The findings reveal that: (1) Consumers' psychological changes (positive affect, flow state, and emotional attachment) significantly and positively influence impulse buying behavior. (2) Scarcity, discounted price, review quality, and observational learning also have significant positive effects on impulse buying. (3) Social presence and sense of belonging significantly enhance flow state. (4) Entertainment and informativeness significantly enhance emotional attachment.

hot.title: Understanding tourist barriers and personality influences in embracing generative AI for travel planning and decision-making
hot.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (GAI) technologies become increasingly integrated into the travel industry, understanding the barriers tourists face in adopting these innovative technologies for their travel planning and decision-making has growingly become a critical area of focus.
